articles.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra tem menor preço desde maio em oferta exclusiva Prime • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch Ultra tem menor preço desde maio em oferta exclusiva Prime
Galaxy Watch Ultra com caixa de titânio, GPS integrado e longa bateria recebe desconto significativo com pagamento via Pix na Amazon
O Galaxy Watch Ultra está disponível por R$ 1.519,20 no Pix em oferta exclusiva para assinantes Prime da Amazon. O smartwatch esportivo premium da Samsung com conexão 4G LTE e tela AMOLED, lançado por R$ 4.999, fica 70% mais barato após a chegada do Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 e atinge o menor preço já visto em meses.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra traz uma tela Super AMOLED de 1,5 polegada protegida com vidro de Cristal de Safira e corpo robusto em titânio de 47 mm. Além do display com brilho máximo de 3.000 nits, que facilita a visualização mesmo sob sol forte, o acessório tem botões e coroa giratória para navegação pelos menus do sistema Wear OS.
O smartwatch usa o sensor de saúde BioActive para monitorar frequência cardíaca, pressão arterial, padrões de sono e outros dados do usuário. Além disso, o modelo pode registrar diferentes atividades físicas, como caminhada, corrida, ciclismo e natação.
Todos os dados registrados pelo Galaxy Watch Ultra podem ser sincronizados com o Samsung Health. Dessa maneira, a pessoa consegue criar um histórico digital sobre saúde e condicionamento físico, recebendo dicas para obter uma rotina mais saudável.
Um dos destaques do smartwatch da Samsung é o suporte para conexão 4G LTE via eSIM, mantendo o usuário conectado à internet sem depender de um smartphone Galaxy ou Wi-Fi. Ele ainda conta com um GPS integrado para mapear trajetos em atividades ao ar livre ou receber dicas de rotas em trilhas.
Segundo a marca, o acessório tem uma autonomia de até 60 horas de uso moderado com o recurso Always On Display ativo. Para quem optar por usar o relógio sem manter a tela sempre ativa, o tempo de bateria se estende até 80 horas.
Fechando o pacote, o Galaxy Watch Ultra (R$ 1519,20 no Pix para assinantes Prime) tem suporte ao Galaxy AI e ao Google Gemini. Internamente, o dispositivo tem 2 GB de RAM, 64 GB de armazenamento interno e conexões Bluetooth 5.3 e NFC para ações por aproximação.

articles.title: Así son las muñecas inteligentes que cuidan y hacen compañía a adultos mayores: “enfermera” en casa
articles.text:
Corea del Sur está recurriendo a la inteligencia artificial para enfrentar uno de los mayores desafíos derivados del envejecimiento de su población: la soledad de los adultos mayores. En un país donde una gran proporción de hogares está integrada por una sola persona, distintas administraciones locales comenzaron a incorporar robots y muñecas inteligentes capaces de conversar, monitorear el estado de salud y alertar a los servicios sociales ante posibles emergencias.
La iniciativa forma parte de una estrategia más amplia para reducir el aislamiento social y mejorar la calidad de vida de las personas mayores. Estos dispositivos, equipados con inteligencia artificial y sensores, no solo ofrecen compañía mediante conversaciones cotidianas, sino que también registran información relacionada con los hábitos diarios del usuario, como el sueño, el estado de ánimo, la alimentación o el cumplimiento de la medicación.
PUBLICIDAD
El objetivo es que trabajadores de los sistemas de bienestar social puedan detectar señales de deterioro físico o emocional y actuar antes de que se produzcan situaciones de riesgo.
Un país que envejece rápidamente
Corea del Sur figura entre las naciones con mayor velocidad de envejecimiento del mundo. La combinación de una baja tasa de natalidad y una esperanza de vida cada vez mayor ha modificado profundamente la estructura de su población.
PUBLICIDAD
A este fenómeno se suma otro dato preocupante: cerca del 42 % de los hogares está compuesto por una sola persona. Esto significa que miles de adultos mayores viven sin compañía permanente y, en muchos casos, con un contacto muy limitado con familiares o vecinos.
Las autoridades consideran que esta situación incrementa el riesgo de depresión, deterioro cognitivo y problemas de salud asociados al aislamiento prolongado.
Uno de los fenómenos que más preocupa es el aumento de las llamadas “muertes solitarias”, casos en los que una persona fallece en su vivienda y su muerte permanece sin ser descubierta durante días o incluso semanas.
PUBLICIDAD
Muñecas inteligentes que conversan con sus usuarios
Entre las soluciones tecnológicas implementadas destacan las desarrolladas por empresas como Hyodol, Wonderful Platform y Mr. Mind.
En el caso de Hyodol, la compañía ya ha distribuido más de 14.000 muñecas inteligentes en distintas regiones del país.
Estos dispositivos utilizan modelos de inteligencia artificial basados en ChatGPT para mantener conversaciones naturales con los usuarios. A diferencia de un asistente virtual convencional, las muñecas han sido entrenadas específicamente para desempeñar un rol de compañía, adaptando sus respuestas y rutinas a la vida cotidiana de cada persona.
PUBLICIDAD
La inteligencia artificial recuerda el nombre del usuario, conversa sobre temas cotidianos, pregunta cómo se siente y busca mantener una interacción constante para reducir la sensación de aislamiento.
Mucho más que compañía
Además de conversar, estos dispositivos incorporan funciones orientadas al cuidado diario.
Las muñecas pueden recordar la hora de tomar medicamentos, animar a realizar actividades físicas ligeras, sugerir horarios de descanso e incluso registrar cambios en determinados hábitos que podrían indicar un problema de salud.
PUBLICIDAD
Parte de esta información puede compartirse con trabajadores sociales o familiares autorizados, permitiendo detectar situaciones de riesgo con mayor rapidez.
Algunos modelos también son compatibles con sistemas de domótica, lo que les permite controlar determinados dispositivos del hogar, como luces o electrodomésticos inteligentes.
Diseñadas para generar un vínculo emocional
Uno de los aspectos más llamativos del proyecto es el diseño psicológico de las muñecas.
Según Hyodol, estos dispositivos fueron concebidos para comportarse como un nieto cariñoso. La inteligencia artificial utiliza un tono afectuoso, expresa interés por la rutina diaria del usuario y responde con cercanía durante las conversaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa explica que esta estrategia busca responder a una realidad frecuente entre muchas personas mayores que dedicaron gran parte de su vida al cuidado de sus familias y que, tras la independencia de sus hijos o la jubilación, experimentan un profundo sentimiento de vacío.
Aunque una mascota también puede ofrecer compañía, los desarrolladores sostienen que una inteligencia artificial puede mantener conversaciones fluidas, responder preguntas y estimular cognitivamente al usuario mediante el diálogo.

articles.title: Retraite en ligne : cette aide méconnue vous offre l'assistance d'un expert gratuit
articles.text:
Retraite en ligne : cette aide méconnue vous offre l'assistance d'un expert gratuit
Remplir sa demande de retraite sur internet tourne vite au casse-tête quand on n'est pas à l'aise avec l'informatique. Pourtant, une aide humaine, gratuite et proche de chez soi existe partout en France. Dans les espaces France Services, des agents et des conseillers numériques accompagnent pas à pas les futurs retraités, du relevé de carrière jusqu'à la validation du dossier.
Le curseur clignote dans la case vide. À l'écran, le formulaire de demande de retraite réclame un numéro de sécurité sociale, un code, une pièce jointe scannée. Assis devant l'ordinateur, le futur retraité sent monter la panique : un faux clic, et il craint de tout perdre. Cette scène se rejoue chaque jour dans des millions de foyers. Ce que la plupart de ces personnes ignorent, c'est qu'elles n'ont pas à l'affronter seules.
L'illectronisme, un mur invisible à l'heure du tout-numérique
Le problème porte un nom : l'illectronisme, cette difficulté à utiliser les outils numériques du quotidien. Il ne s'agit pas d'un phénomène marginal. Selon l'INSEE, entre 13 et 15 % de la population française est concernée, soit plusieurs millions de personnes, souvent les plus âgées. Or c'est précisément au moment de préparer sa retraite, une démarche lourde et intégralement dématérialisée, que cette fracture devient la plus pénalisante.
Le paradoxe est cruel. L'État vise la dématérialisation totale des démarches administratives, tandis qu'une part importante des futurs retraités se retrouve dans l'incapacité de faire valoir ses droits sans aide. Créer un compte sur le portail retraite, se connecter via FranceConnect, télécharger un relevé de carrière, joindre un justificatif scanné. Autant d'étapes qui semblent évidentes aux uns et infranchissables aux autres. Résultat, certains reportent leur demande, commettent des erreurs coûteuses, ou renoncent à des droits faute d'accompagnement. C'est ce vide que le service public a entrepris de combler.
France Services, un guichet unique près de chez soi
La réponse tient dans un réseau déployé sur tout le territoire, y compris dans les zones rurales : les espaces France Services. Le principe est celui du guichet unique. En un seul lieu, souvent une mairie, une médiathèque ou un bureau de poste, un agent formé aide les usagers dans leurs démarches auprès de neuf grands organismes publics. Parmi eux figurent la CNAV, c'est-à-dire l'Assurance retraite, et la MSA pour le régime agricole, mais aussi les impôts, la CAF, l'Assurance maladie ou France Travail.
Un futur retraité peut ainsi y être accompagné pour l'ensemble de son dossier. L'agent aide à créer et sécuriser le compte retraite, à récupérer et vérifier le relevé de carrière, puis à repérer d'éventuels trimestres manquants. Il accompagne enfin la saisie et l'envoi de la demande en ligne. Le tout gratuitement, et dans un cadre confidentiel. L'engagement du réseau est qu'un espace se trouve à moins de trente minutes de chaque domicile. Pour savoir où est le plus proche, une adresse suffit. La cartographie officielle disponible en ligne recense tous les points d'accueil, que l'on peut aussi appeler avant de se déplacer avec ses papiers.
Le conseiller numérique, pour gagner en autonomie
À côté de l'agent qui aide à faire, un autre professionnel apprend à faire : le conseiller numérique France Services. Sa mission n'est pas seulement de boucler un dossier à votre place, mais de vous rendre autonome face à l'écran. Lors d'ateliers collectifs ou de rendez-vous individuels, gratuits eux aussi, il enseigne les gestes de base. Manier une souris, gérer une boîte mail, scanner un document, reconnaître un site officiel d'une tentative d'arnaque.
Le dispositif a une ampleur réelle. Déployé depuis 2021, le réseau des conseillers numériques a déjà réalisé plusieurs millions d'accompagnements, et la grande majorité des personnes aidées déclarent avoir progressé. Pour les futurs retraités, cette montée en compétence est précieuse : elle transforme une démarche subie en geste maîtrisé, et sécurise durablement l'accès à ses droits. Un bémol mérite toutefois d'être signalé. Porté par des financements publics revus à la baisse ces dernières années, le maillage peut varier selon les territoires. Mieux vaut donc se renseigner localement sur les créneaux disponibles. Reste l'essentiel : personne n'est obligé d'affronter seul le labyrinthe administratif de sa retraite. L'aide existe, elle est humaine, gratuite, et souvent à quelques minutes de chez soi. Il suffit de pousser la porte.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 hacked an external organization during cybersecurity test - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 hacked an external organization during cybersecurity test
A large language model developed by Meta Platforms Inc. hacked a third party organization during a cybersecurity evaluation.
The Facebook parent disclosed the incident on Wednesday without specifying the LLM. According to The Information, the cyberattack was carried out by Muse Spark 1.1, an algorithm that Meta released last month. It joins a string of frontier models that carried out breaches in recent months.
The incident occurred during an evaluation of Muse Spark 1.1’s hacking capabilities. Meta carried out the test in collaboration with Irregular, an AI cybersecurity startup. The companies ran the model in a sandbox designed to isolate it from the web. However, a configuration error gave Muse Spark 1.1 internet access, which is what enabled it to carry out the cyberattack.
The model used its internet connection to comprise the infrastructure of an unnamed third party organization. According to Reuters, Muse Spark 1.1 “altered its internal environment.” It’s unclear whether the model also gained access to internal data.
“The incident exposes a fundamental flaw in how organizations approach AI safety. Instruction is not containment,” said Cliff Steinhauer, the director of information security and engagement at the National Cybersecurity Alliance. “Telling a model it lacks internet access is a guideline, not a guardrail. Real security requires hard, infrastructure-level boundaries like sandboxing, zero-trust networking, and strict access controls.”
The other LLM-caused breaches that were disclosed over the past month unfolded in a similar manner. Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC tested their models in Irregular-powered sandboxes that were accidentally given internet access. The error led to at least five different breaches, one of which affected the popular AI hosting platform Hugging Face.
A sixth incident was disclosed this week by the U.K. government’s AI Security Institute. Its researchers tested Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol in sandboxes that were deliberately given internet access. According to the group, the former model attempted to inject malicious code into an open-source GitHub repository.
In June, Anthropic disclosed that Mythos 5 can autonomously find and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities. It’s unclear whether Muse Spark 1.1 possesses the same capability.
The model scored 53.3 on DeepSWE 1.1, a benchmark that evaluates AI models’ ability to perform long-running coding tasks. Finding a zero-day vulnerability can take upwards of weeks in some cases. GPT-5.6 Terra, the mid-range version of OpenAI’s flagship LLM, scored 11 points higher on DeepSWE 1.1.
Meta released a more capable LLM called Muse Spark 1.2 on Wednesday. It came within 6 points of GPT-5.6 Terra’s DeepSWE 1.1 score. In conjuction, Meta released a companion AI agent called Muse Code that is specifically designed to make the model better at long-running coding tasks. It enables Muse Spark 1.2 to split complex tasks among multiple subagents.
Meta is still in the process of investigating the Muse Spark 1.1 breach. The company plans to release more information about the incident after it completes the review. Irregular, for its part, will publish a paper with best practices on securing LLM evaluation sandboxes.

articles.title: Decathlon ha llevado su experiencia al diseño de un traje espacial europeo. Y de momento todo va viento en popa
articles.text:
Hay empresas que uno espera encontrar en una misión espacial y otras que, al menos de entrada, parecen pertenecer a otro mundo. Decathlon pertenece claramente al segundo grupo. La tenemos asociada al deporte cotidiano, a productos accesibles y a soluciones prácticas para gente que corre, nada, pedalea o se va al monte el fin de semana. Y, sin embargo, su nombre se ha colado en una conversación mucho más exigente: la de un prototipo europeo que ya se está probando con astronautas.
La historia no se queda en un proyecto sobre el papel. La NASA ha documentado actividades de Sophie Adenot a bordo de la Estación Espacial Internacional relacionadas con el EuroSuit, un prototipo intravehicular europeo que se está evaluando en condiciones reales de misión. La agencia estadounidense señaló que la astronauta de la ESA lo había probado en el módulo Columbus para estudiar su comodidad, movilidad y facilidad de uso. No es todavía un parte final del consorcio, pero sí una señal clara de que el proyecto ya ha pasado por la ISS.
El proyecto que une el deporte con el espacio
Hablar de “traje espacial” puede llevarnos a una imagen equivocada. EuroSuit no es, al menos en esta fase, un traje pensado para caminar por el exterior de la Estación Espacial Internacional ni para sustituir a los equipos de actividad extravehicular. Es un prototipo intravehicular: una prenda concebida para usarse dentro de una nave o de un hábitat, especialmente en fases como el lanzamiento, el aterrizaje o una situación de emergencia. Ahí el desafío no está solo en proteger, sino en permitir que el astronauta pueda moverse, ajustárselo con rapidez y operar sin que el propio traje se convierta en un obstáculo.
El reparto de papeles ayuda a entender por qué el nombre de Decathlon aparece en esta historia sin convertirla en una exageración. CNES impulsó el desarrollo del EuroSuit mediante un contrato con un consorcio francés encabezado por Spartan Space, que lidera el proyecto desde el punto de vista técnico. La cadena deportiva participa en el diseño textil y ergonómico, justo donde su experiencia tiene sentido, y MEDES añade el conocimiento médico y fisiológico ligado al cuerpo humano en condiciones espaciales. La fórmula, por tanto, no sustituye a la industria espacial clásica: la complementa con competencias muy específicas.
Ahí es donde el proyecto empieza a ganar cuerpo. La NASA no ha presentado el EuroSuit como un producto terminado, pero sí ha dejado constancia de una campaña progresiva: primero una referencia a un traje intravehicular en fase de prototipo, después una prueba identificada ya con su nombre y más tarde una nueva actividad durante la jornada del 20 de julio. Esa continuidad permite hablar de un programa que avanza en condiciones reales de misión, aunque de momento falte la parte más visible: no se han publicado imágenes de esas pruebas en la ISS.
Vale, Decathlon forma parte del proyecto. La pregunta entonces es bastante lógica: qué está haciendo realmente una cadena deportiva en el desarrollo de un traje espacial europeo. Su aportación no está en sustituir a los especialistas aeroespaciales, sino en un terreno mucho más reconocible para cualquiera que haya usado ropa técnica: tejidos, ajuste al cuerpo, libertad de movimiento y ergonomía. En un traje intravehicular, todo eso cambia de escala, pero no de naturaleza. Si un astronauta tiene que ponérselo deprisa y operar dentro de una nave, la prenda no puede convertirse en un problema añadido.
La prueba de fuego no termina con una sesión en la estación. El plan pasa ahora por continuar con las pruebas de tierra previstas para 2026-2027 y alimentar el desarrollo de una futura versión operativa. Hasta entonces, EuroSuit seguirá siendo un prototipo, no una solución cerrada. Pero lo que ya hemos visto basta para entender por qué esta historia merece atención: Europa está explorando una pieza muy concreta de autonomía espacial y, en ese proceso, la frontera entre la ropa técnica que usamos aquí abajo y la ingeniería orbital parece un poco menos lejana.

articles.title: Thousands of server motherboards are vulnerable to controller flaws that could give attackers hardware-level control
articles.text:
Facepalm: Attackers are targeting hardware that keeps modern servers running, with the weak point being the baseboard management controller (BMC) installed on the motherboard. New research shows that thousands of these controllers, shipped for years by major server manufacturers, remain exposed on the Internet and within corporate networks due to serious, long-standing flaws that are still easy to exploit.
Baseboard management controllers, or BMCs, are small computers built into nearly every enterprise server. They have their own firmware, operating system, network stack, and IP address. Administrators use them to reboot machines, install updates, reinstall operating systems, and monitor hardware, even when the main server is powered off or unresponsive.
That deep level of control makes BMCs valuable for IT operations but dangerous if attackers gain access. If compromised, a BMC can give an attacker control over the underlying server.
At the Black Hat security conference in Las Vegas, firmware security expert HD Moore, CEO and founder of runZero, presented new research showing that many of the weaknesses he identified back in 2013 are still present. He also revealed more than a dozen newly discovered vulnerabilities affecting BMCs from HPE, Supermicro, Avocent, Huawei, Lenovo, Dell, and other vendors.
The core problem continues to center around IPMI, the protocol that allows BMCs to manage servers out of band.
"The end result is a pervasive, under-monitored, under-patched parallel attack surface that is both Internet-exposed and widespread inside corporate networks, and is much more exploitable than many folks realize," Moore wrote in an email ahead of his talk.
To measure the scale of the exposure, Moore conducted two broad scans. One looked for BMCs accessible over the public Internet, while the other searched internal corporate networks.
The external scan found more than 86,000 BMCs with management services exposed to the public Internet. More than half of them (54%) had at least one critical vulnerability. As many as 75,000 remained vulnerable to CVE-2013-4786, a flaw in the IPMI 2.0 authentication protocol that allows attackers to crack administrator passwords offline. Inside corporate networks, an internal scan of 126,761 BMCs found that nearly 29% contained one or more critical vulnerabilities.
The vulnerabilities Moore described affect multiple layers of the BMC stack. Some involve IPMI authentication, while others affect session security, memory management, and the handling of firmware and secrets.
One category of vulnerabilities stems from flaws in the IPMI authentication handshake. Attackers can manipulate the order of messages to bypass checks and gain a limited foothold in the BMC.
Affected products include HPE iLO, Supermicro, OpenBMC, and OpenBMC-derived systems from H3C and Nvidia. Once an attacker gains that foothold, additional vulnerabilities can be chained together to achieve full control.
Another set of vulnerabilities exists because IPMI does not always enforce integrity and encryption during sessions. "The device decides whether to authenticate and decrypt each packet from that attacker's own header, and not from the algorithms the session negotiated, so an unsigned, unencrypted command is accepted on a secured session," Moore said.
He developed a proof of concept that uses these flaws to "chain otherwise-unexploitable issues into full sessions." Affected vendors include HPE, Supermicro, and legacy Intel systems.
Session IDs are another weak point in some systems. Instead of generating strong random values, some implementations create tokens based on simple counters or clock values, making them predictable.
An attacker can guess another user's active BMC session and take control of it through both IPMI and browser-based KVM consoles. Moore said the two most serious vulnerabilities of this type affect Supermicro systems.
Moore also discovered pre-authentication memory corruption vulnerabilities. In HPE iLO systems, a length-validation flaw in the management SSH service can be exploited before authentication and used to execute attacker-controlled code. This provides a direct path to remote code execution on the BMC.
Firmware integrity is another area of concern. In some systems, firmware is unsigned or can be modified by attackers, while configuration integrity checks are not enforced. An authenticated administrator account could be abused to install a persistent implant or replace keys used for firmware verification. These weaknesses can also be combined with other vulnerabilities to bypass authentication and escalate privileges. Supermicro, H3C, and Dell are affected by these firmware-level issues.
The handling of secrets stored in firmware creates additional risks. Keys and constants embedded in publicly available firmware images can be extracted and reused as valid credentials. This can allow attackers to authenticate to BMCs or decrypt traffic. Moore identified this pattern in devices from Supermicro, OpenBMC, Huawei, and Dell.
Password practices make the situation worse. Many BMCs still rely on default or factory-generated credentials. With CVE-2013-4786, attackers can obtain password hashes and perform offline cracking attacks. Even when vendors randomize passwords before shipment, the available keyspaces can still be too small.
Moore found that HPE uses "eight digits or alphanum," which he described as the weakest approach. Supermicro and Dell use somewhat longer default credentials that slow attacks but do not prevent them, extending password recovery attempts from hours to days depending on available computing power.
Although many of the newly discovered vulnerabilities require authentication to exploit, that barrier can often be bypassed by chaining them with pre-authentication flaws. In other cases, attackers who gain limited access can install older, vulnerable, or deliberately backdoored firmware on the BMC and then use control of the operating system to further modify the controller.
To help defenders understand their exposure, Moore released an open-source scanner called OOBscan. The tool allows administrators to scan entire server fleets for the BMC weaknesses he documented and begin addressing the most serious issues.
He also recommends several basic hardening measures: use long, unique usernames and complex passwords; disable IPMI and KCS when possible; block host-side access to the BMC; and isolate each BMC network interface instead of placing multiple controllers on a shared VLAN.
"BMCs are still an underrated risk," Moore wrote. "This work points to the ecosystem being well behind the curve in terms of code quality and architecture."

articles.title: ‘It is hard to imagine a big tech company agreeing to share the world wide web for no commercial reward’: As the web turns 35, and its creator believes it’s not too late to save it
articles.text:
35 years ago today, the World Wide Web changed our lives forever — as Tim Berners-Lee says, ‘trading personal data for use certainly does not fit with my vision for a free web’
An invention that changed the world in an instant
- The World Wide Web was created 35 years ago today
- It was initially designed for sharing documents at CERN
- Its creator says we can return to its spirit of openness and collaboration
These days, it’s hard to go long without connecting to the Internet in one way or another: whether through one of the best web browsers or by connecting to a smart home device, it’s something we often take for granted. The primary means of interacting online — the World Wide Web — has just turned 35 years old today, and its creator has a timely message that couldn’t be more relevant for modern users.
The World Wide Web is the creation of British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee. Working at the scientific body CERN in the 1980s and 1990s, Berners-Lee wanted a way to store, update, and locate documents within the sprawling organization. At the same time, he sought a solution that would allow for these documents to be shared with outside bodies quickly and straightforwardly.
That desire led to his creation of the World Wide Web. It was announced to the public on August 6, 1991, with Berners-Lee humbly stating that “We are very interested in spreading the web to other areas.” It was a platform whereby anyone could link to any document in a database using hyperlinks, or links embedded in text, images, and other media. Importantly, multiple users were able to access this platform simultaneously and independently of each other.
Adoption quickly spread from CERN to other research organizations before being opened up to the wider public, whereupon it exploded in popularity. And 35 years later, it’s an invention that has turned the world on its head.
An absolutely vital component of this system was that it had to be both free and decentralized. Berners-Lee was adamant that anyone should be able to create a website and implement hyperlinks on their own, without paying a fee and without a central body dictating what could and could not be done. That principle of openness still stands today — but it’s increasingly under threat.
‘It’s not too late’
Speaking to The Guardian in September 2025, Berners-Lee lamented that plenty of the web today is no longer free and open. “We see a handful of large platforms harvesting users’ private data to share with commercial brokers or even repressive governments,” he noted, adding: “We see ubiquitous algorithms that are addictive by design and damaging to our teenagers’ mental health. Trading personal data for use certainly does not fit with my vision for a free web.”
At the same time, user data is sold “to actors we never intended it to reach,” with the result being “deliberately harmful content that leads to real-world violence, spreads misinformation, wreaks havoc on our psychological wellbeing and seeks to undermine social cohesion.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This is especially challenging in the age of AI, Berners-Lee argued. To put things right and get back to the original vision of his creation, the father of the web advocated for strong AI governance and guidance from organizations that are not motivated by data and profit but instead by collaboration and the needs of the individual. On this point, Berners-Lee quipped: “It is hard to imagine a big tech company agreeing to share the world wide web for no commercial reward like CERN allowed me to.”
As the World Wide Web turns 35, the spirit of “collaboration, creativity and compassion” that allowed it to be given away for free is being increasingly challenged by Big Tech — but Berners-Lee still thinks there’s time to put things right: “We can re-empower individuals, and take the web back. It’s not too late.”

articles.title: Le Galaxy S26 FE se dévoile, avec une puce signée Qualcomm à bord
articles.text:
Si le Galaxy S26 FE ne devrait pas profiter d'un SoC de chez Qualcomm, le constructeur américain pourrait tout de même avoir sa présence à l'intérieur du futur smartphone du géant sud-coréen.
C'est un document de la FCC qui révèle la future puce Qualcomm présente dans le Galaxy S26 FE de Samsung. Le smartphone, attendu après la rentrée, devrait opter pour un SoC maison de Samsung, mais profiter de la technologie Qualcomm FastConnect.
Pas de Snapdragon, mais du FastConnect
Le Galaxy S26 FE a déjà obtenu sa certification auprès de la Federal Communications Commission (FCC), l'autorité américaine de régulation des télécommunications. Les documents associés à cette certification mentionnent des composants issus de deux fabricants distincts : Samsung LSI, la division semi-conducteurs de Samsung, et Qualcomm, avec sa technologie FastConnect.
Cette présence de Qualcomm ne signifie pas pour autant que l'appareil embarquera un processeur Snapdragon. Il s'agirait uniquement d'une puce dédiée à la connectivité sans fil. La technologie FastConnect est en effet un système d'accélération Wi-Fi et Bluetooth qui se présente sous la forme d'un composant distinct, gravé en 6 nm. La dernière version de cette puce, la FastConnect 8800, intègre selon Qualcomm le Wi-Fi 8, le Bluetooth à haut débit, l'UWB et le Thread dans un seul composant.
Le SoC du Galaxy S26 FE resterait donc l'Exynos 2500, conformément aux informations qui circulaient jusqu'ici. Contrairement au Galaxy S26 "classique", il ne devrait pas exister de modèles avec des puces différentes.
De la charge 45 W et une grosse batterie
Les documents de la FCC apportent également une confirmation sur un autre point : la charge filaire de 45W, déjà évoquée dans de précédentes fuites, est bien au programme. L'appareil devrait par ailleurs disposer de la charge sans fil inversée, du NFC, du Wi-Fi 6 et d'une connectivité satellite.
Selon les informations disponibles, le Galaxy S26 FE serait équipé d'un écran Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 6,7 pouces, avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 120 Hz et une luminosité de pointe de 1 900 nits. La batterie aurait une capacité de 5 000 mAh. Le système photo serait identique à celui de son prédécesseur.
Quand sera lancé le Galaxy S26 FE ?
Samsung pourrait présenter le Galaxy S26 FE le 4 septembre prochain. Son prix de départ devrait être annoncé à 699 dollars, ce qui, même en tenant compte d'une éventuelle hausse de 50 dollars évoquée par certaines rumeurs, le placerait environ 200 dollars en dessous du Galaxy S26 classique, tout en proposant un écran plus grand, une batterie de plus grande capacité et une charge plus rapide.

articles.title: SK hynix Invests 54 Trillion Won in Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 to Secure Mid-to-Long-Term Production Base for AI Memory Demand
articles.text:
Friday, August 7th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
SK hynix Invests 54 Trillion Won in Yongin Y2 and Cheongju M17 to Secure Mid-to-Long-Term Production Base for AI Memory Demand
SK hynix Inc. announced today that it has decided to build new fabs in Yongin and Cheongju to respond to the continuously growing demand for memory in the AI era. 
The company approved a total investment of approximately 54 trillion, 35.2 trillion won in Yongin "Y2" fab and 19.1 trillion won in the Cheongju "M17" fab, in a board meeting.
This decision represents execution of the mid-to-long-term investment strategy announced by the company last June. Under its master plan to invest 600 trillion won in the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster and 100 trillion won to expand its Cheongju production base, SK hynix is currently constructing its first fab in Yongin (Y1). With this latest decision, the company is embarking on the construction of subsequent fabs in both Yongin and Cheongju.According to market research firm Omdia, both DRAM and NAND demand are projected to maintain a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19% from last year through 2030. The company views this growth not as a temporary supercycle, but as a structural transformation in which memory transcends its role as a mere component to become core infrastructure determining AI performance itself.
SK hynix stated that in the AI era, technological competitiveness alone is not enough and the ability to supply the required volume at the exact moment customers need it is the ultimate competitive advantage. We reached this investment decision after a thorough review of market demand.
Yongin Y2 is the second of four fabs planned sequentially for the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster. It will serve as a DRAM production base spanning a total floor area of 341,000 pyeong (approximately 1,130,000m2). Construction is scheduled to break ground in July next year, targeting the opening of its first cleanroom in June 2029 to produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other next-generation DRAM products. Meanwhile, construction on Y1 is progressing smoothly toward its initial cleanroom opening target of February next year.
SK hynix previously set a goal to advance the completion date of the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster by 12 years—from the originally planned 2045 to 2033—to finish constructing all four fabs. The Y2 construction serves as the second phase supporting this accelerated timeline and the investment spans to October 2031 sequentially. The investment amount includes construction costs for "Business Support Building" with administrative and welfare facilities for Y2 personnel, an "Integrated R&D Center" to consolidate product development testing, analysis, and experiments, as well as auxiliary infrastructure.
For the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster—sprawling over approximately 1.26 million pyeong (approximately 4,160,000 m²) in Wonsam-myeon, Cheoin-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do—Phase 1 power and water infrastructure required up through Y2 operation is nearing completion, currently at a 99% progress rate. As fab construction and infrastructure setup have been carried out concurrently, the company plans to proceed with the Y2 construction according to schedule.
In the NAND market, demand is surging rapidly centered on enterprise SSDs driven by the full-scale expansion of AI services. This is further boosted by demand for key-value (KV) cache2storage in AI inference, with application fields expected to broaden further as Agentic and Physical AI are introduced.
SK hynix selected Cheongju as its new NAND fab base because it offers the fastest fab construction timeline. The Cheongju Campus already houses the M11, M12, and M15 fabs, enabling efficient production linked to existing operations on sites equipped with substantial pre-established power and water infrastructure. Cheongju M17 will be built across a total area of 206,000 pyeong (approximately 680,000 m²), breaking ground in February next year with plans to open its first cleanroom in December 2028. The investment period runs through April 2031 according to the master plan.
SK hynix plans to proactively secure production infrastructure based on mid-to-long-term demand discussed with customers, while expanding actual production capacity in alignment with the timing of customer needs. Fabs will be constructed according to the master schedule, whereas cleanroom expansions and equipment installation will take place sequentially in line with demand trends to maximize capital efficiency.
The company expects this investment to secure future growth foundations while strengthening the competitiveness of the domestic semiconductor ecosystem and boosting local economies. The large-scale simultaneous investments in Yongin and Cheongju are anticipated to expand joint growth opportunities for supply chain partners, generate employment, and revitalize local commercial districts, thereby contributing to the sustainable growth of the national economy.
An SK hynix official stated that "This investment is a decision made to seize opportunities in line with the market's growth speed. By proactively securing production capabilities, we aim to establish ourselves as a key partner in AI infrastructure, contributing to the stability of the global AI semiconductor supply chain."

articles.title: ChatGPT libera mensagens ilimitadas no plano gratuito • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT libera mensagens ilimitadas no plano gratuito
Atualização remove limites de interação mesmo para não-assinantes e troca o GPT-5.5 pelo GPT-5.6 Luna.
Quem usa versões gratuitas de chatbots de IA já se deparou, em algum momento, com avisos de limite atingido, que impedem a continuidade do uso ou redirecionam as respostas para um mais básico. A OpenAI, no entanto, revelou nesta quinta-feira (06/08) que chats de texto passarão a ser ilimitados, mesmo para quem não tem uma assinatura ativa.
Além da remoção dos limites, contas dos planos Free e Go passam a usar o GPT-5.6 Luna, substituindo de vez o GPT-5.5 como o padrão para esses usuários. Segundo a OpenAI, o Luna foi desenvolvido para lidar melhor com tarefas do dia a dia.
Além do novo modelo, o chatbot vai reviver um botão chamado “Pensar”, no qual os usuários podem pedir para que a IA leve mais tempo de processamento em perguntas difíceis.
A mudança na política da empresa será aplicada gradualmente a partir da semana que vem e é importante reforçar que só vale para chats de texto. Aquelas conversas com imagens geradas pela IA ou com arquivos anexados continuarão restringindo as interações.
Dias antes, vale lembrar, a empresa revisou os preços do consumo de tokens nos modelos GPT-5.6 Terra e GPT-5.6 Luna, para quem acessa a tecnologia através de APIs.
Para os planos Plus e Pro, a novidade é uma versão atualizada do GPT-5.6 Sol que, segundo a OpenAI, trará respostas mais diretas.
O chatbot também traz uma revisão do ajuste de raciocínio do modelo, agora feito através de um controle deslizante, no canto direito do campo de pergunta.
Ele permite definir o tempo de processamento para cada solicitação: do instantâneo ao “Pro”. No nível mais baixo, como o nome sugere, a IA priorizará respostas diretas, sendo indicado para tarefas simples. Nos níveis seguintes, a proposta é atender pedidos que exigem mais planejamento, redação aprofundada, análise de código ou pesquisas detalhadas.
A OpenAI ressalta que essa versão do GPT-5.6 Sol vale para o chat. As versões usadas nas plataformas Work e Codex não foram alteradas. O GPT-5.6 Sol atualizado já está disponível para assinantes Plus e Pro.
A empresa afirma ter reduzido erros factuais nos novos modelos. Em testes internos, conduzidos pela própria OpenAI, com prompts das áreas financeira, médica e jurídica, respostas com pelo menos um erro caíram 62% no GPT-5.6 Luna e 68% no GPT-5.6 Sol, na comparação com o GPT-5.5 Instant.
O comunicado também detalha novas medidas de segurança para usuários com menos de 18 anos. A OpenAI afirma que treinou o modelo para recusar pedidos envolvendo roleplay romântico, desafios perigosos de internet e interações que simulem substituição de relacionamentos reais.
A empresa é alvo de processos nos Estados Unidos após a ferramenta, ainda na era do GPT-4o, ter supostamente incentivado suicídios e outros problemas na vida real.

articles.title: AMD acquires Taalas to hardwire AI models into silicon - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AMD acquires Taalas to hardwire AI models into silicon
Advanced Micro Devices Inc. said today it has agreed to buy Taalas Inc., a Toronto startup that hardwires artificial intelligence models directly into silicon, in a deal that pushes the chipmaker deeper into the market for AI inference.
Terms were not disclosed. AMD shares rose about 1.5% following the announcement.
Founded in 2023, Taalas builds what it calls model-specific integrated circuits, chips that cast a model’s weights and dataflow into transistors instead of shuttling them in and out of high-bandwidth memory. Its first test chip, HC1, was built on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd.’s 6-nanometer process and served Meta Platforms Inc.’s Llama 3.1 8B at close to 17,000 tokens per second, a rate Taalas said in February was 73 times that of Nvidia Corp.’s H200 at one-tenth the power. A second chip, HC2, targets models of about 20 billion parameters.
The tradeoff is flexibility. A finished Taalas part runs the model it was built for and nothing else, so a new model means new silicon. Taalas says that is cheaper than it sounds. Only two of the chip’s 100-plus layers change from one design to the next, and the company puts its tape-out time at roughly two months using in-house tools.
The technology is headed for AMD’s accelerator roadmap. The larger plan is systems, not just parts. AMD wants Taalas chips working next to its Instinct GPUs, wired into the Helios racks and Epyc processors it sells and programmed through its ROCm software.
Vamsi Boppana, senior vice president of AMD’s Artificial Intelligence Group, said the aim is choice, giving customers “the right compute solutions for every AI workload.” Taalas brings what he called differentiated inference performance and efficiency.
Taalas co-founder and Chief Executive Ljubisa Bajic is on his second AI chip company. He ran Tenstorrent Inc. before leaving to start Taalas. The startup was founded “to rethink AI inference from the ground up by building the hardware around the model,” he said. His Toronto team joins Boppana’s group when the deal closes.
The purchase lands in a market that has reorganized itself around inference over the past year. Nvidia agreed in December to license inference technology from Groq Inc. in a reported $20 billion deal, then put it to work in the Groq 3 language processing unit unveiled at its GTC conference in March. Taalas is AMD’s third AI acquisition in nine months, following MK1 in November and memory optimization startup Mext in June. The FastFlowLM team joined the company in July.
Taalas raised $169 million in February from Quiet Capital, Fidelity and semiconductor investor Pierre Lamond, taking its total to about $219 million.
The acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

articles.title: Fondos animados para WhatsApp: es gratis y se pueden editar en Android y iPhone
articles.text:
WhatsApp está a punto de transformar la personalización de los chats en Android con la llegada de fondos de pantalla animados. La función, que actualmente se encuentra en fase de desarrollo, permitirá a los usuarios elegir entre nuevas categorías de temas que incluyen fondos con animaciones suaves en movimiento, una novedad que busca ofrecer una experiencia visual más atractiva y adaptada a cada preferencia.
Cómo son las nuevas animaciones para WhatsApp
WhatsApp está organizando los nuevos temas de chat en tres categorías principales: Destacados, Doodle y Minimalista. Cada una ofrece una propuesta diferente, desde lo visualmente sofisticado hasta lo clásico o lo simple.
PUBLICIDAD
Fondos animados: categoría Destacados:
La categoría Destacados introduce fondos de pantalla animados que se mueven lentamente en el fondo del chat. El movimiento es suave y discreto, pensado para evitar distracciones o molestias, especialmente entre usuarios con necesidades de accesibilidad. Esta opción ofrece un aspecto renovado a los chats, sin que el fondo tome protagonismo sobre los mensajes.
PUBLICIDAD
Fondos clásicos: categoría Doodle:
La categoría Doodle recupera los fondos oficiales con doodles característicos de WhatsApp, reconocibles por quienes han utilizado la plataforma por años. Es una oportunidad para quienes buscan mantener la estética clásica de la app o prefieren un entorno visual familiar y coherente.
PUBLICIDAD
Estilo sencillo: categoría Minimalista:
Para los usuarios que priorizan la claridad y la ausencia de distracciones, la categoría Minimalista ofrece fondos planos y sin patrones. En modo claro, el fondo será blanco; en modo oscuro, será un fondo oscuro. Esta opción busca que la atención del usuario se centre únicamente en la conversación, sin elementos visuales adicionales.
PUBLICIDAD
El interés por esta actualización radica en que los fondos animados no solo aportan dinamismo, también se diseñaron para no interferir con la legibilidad de los mensajes ni resultar distractores durante la conversación. La apuesta por una personalización más profunda responde a una demanda creciente de usuarios que buscan mayor control sobre la estética y funcionalidad de sus chats cotidianos.
Cuáles son los cambios que se avecinan para los chats
Selección automática de colores de burbuja
Una de las innovaciones más destacadas es la selección automática del color de burbuja. WhatsApp ajusta el color de las burbujas de chat según el fondo elegido, asegurando que el texto siempre tenga el contraste necesario para garantizar la legibilidad.
PUBLICIDAD
De este modo, la aplicación combina estética y accesibilidad sin exigir configuraciones manuales, aunque quienes lo deseen podrán modificar los colores de las burbujas a voluntad.
Privacidad y personalización individual
Las configuraciones de temas seguirán siendo privadas: solo el usuario verá el fondo y la personalización aplicada, sin que los demás participantes del chat perciban cambios en su propia interfaz. Esta decisión mantiene la privacidad y la individualidad en la experiencia de uso, permitiendo personalizar cada chat o toda la aplicación según las preferencias.
PUBLICIDAD
Estas nuevas categorías de temas están en desarrollo en la versión beta de WhatsApp para Android, identificada como 2.26.31.2 en Google Play Store. Por el momento, la función aún no está habilitada para los probadores beta y tampoco existe una fecha oficial para su lanzamiento al público general.
Se espera que, una vez superada la fase de pruebas, la actualización esté disponible para todos los usuarios de Android y, probablemente, posteriormente para otras plataformas.
PUBLICIDAD
La llegada de los fondos animados y nuevas categorías de temas responde a una tendencia del mercado de aplicaciones de mensajería: ofrecer a los usuarios mayor control sobre la apariencia de sus chats y la posibilidad de crear entornos más personales.
WhatsApp, que ya había probado estos cambios en su cliente web, busca ahora llevar la experiencia a todos los dispositivos Android, consolidando su posición frente a competidores que ya ofrecen niveles avanzados de personalización.
PUBLICIDAD
Con la futura actualización, WhatsApp da un paso más hacia la integración de opciones visuales avanzadas, apostando por una experiencia que equilibra personalización, funcionalidad y accesibilidad para millones de usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: En plena sequía y ola de calor, Rumanía ha tenido una singular idea para mantener funcionando una central nuclear: usar explosivos
articles.text:
Hay infraestructuras que asociamos con la continuidad, incluso cuando todo alrededor empieza a fallar. Una central nuclear pertenece, en principio, a esa categoría. Pero lo que hemos visto en Rumanía recuerda que incluso una fuente de energía diseñada para operar de forma estable puede quedar condicionada por algo tan básico como el agua. Con el Danubio en niveles excepcionalmente bajos y una ola de calor presionando el sistema eléctrico, las autoridades terminaron recurriendo a una medida poco habitual: usar explosivos para intentar ganar tiempo.
La urgencia tenía una traducción muy concreta en la red eléctrica rumana. El 28 de julio, la operadora Nuclearelectrica detuvo de forma preventiva y controlada la Unidad 1 de Cernavodă ante la caída del nivel del río. La Unidad 2 todavía podía seguir funcionando, aunque bajo una vigilancia constante de los parámetros de captación, y era sobre ella donde se concentraban todos los esfuerzos. No era una pieza menor: los dos reactores de la única central nuclear del país aportan habitualmente cerca de una quinta parte de la producción eléctrica de Rumanía.
Para entender por qué el nivel del Danubio podía detener la producción, hay que separar los distintos sistemas de la central. Los reactores CANDU emplean agua pesada en sus circuitos nucleares, completamente separados del agua captada del río. Esta última se utiliza para enfriar los condensadores de las turbinas y otros intercambiadores de calor. Cuando el nivel baja demasiado, la instalación deja de disponer del caudal necesario y la operadora debe reducir potencia o detener preventivamente la unidad. No había una emergencia nuclear, sino un problema que impedía seguir generando electricidad dentro de los márgenes establecidos.
Explosivos para ganar tiempo en plena ola de calor
La parte más llamativa de la operación se concentró en la roca de Pârjoaia, una formación que obstaculizaba los trabajos previstos en el cauce. Las fuerzas navales rumanas emplearon un total de 180 kg de explosivos en varias detonaciones controladas para dislocarla y abrir paso a las siguientes fases de la intervención. Pero los estallidos, por sí solos, no enviaban más agua hacia Cernavodă. Su función era actuar sobre el impedimento físico para poder retirar los fragmentos, dragar la zona y preparar una modificación provisional del reparto del caudal.
Tras dislocar la roca y comenzar a retirar sus restos, llegaba la parte decisiva del plan. Los equipos debían dragar el fondo y hundir cuatro barcazas cargadas con piedra para formar una barrera provisional bajo el agua. La estructura buscaba reducir el caudal que se desviaba por el brazo Bala y favorecer que más agua continuara por el Danubio Viejo hacia el sistema de canales que alimenta la toma de Cernavodă. No se trataba de cambiar por completo el curso del río, sino de modificar temporalmente cómo se distribuía un caudal cada vez más escaso.
El plan, sin embargo, aún no podía darse por completado. El hundimiento de las cuatro barcazas tuvo que aplazarse porque las condiciones del río no permitían ejecutar la maniobra con seguridad. Eso significaba que las detonaciones habían permitido avanzar sobre uno de los obstáculos, pero todavía no garantizaban que llegara más agua hasta la captación de la central. Incluso si la barrera funcionaba como estaba previsto, su propósito era mucho más modesto: prolongar durante unos días la actividad de la Unidad 2, no resolver la sequía ni asegurar su funcionamiento a largo plazo.
La ola de calor cerraba el círculo de la crisis. Mientras el Danubio ofrecía menos agua para sostener la producción, las altas temperaturas elevaban el consumo eléctrico y obligaban a Rumanía a buscar más energía justo cuando tenía menos capacidad disponible. La sequía también estaba reduciendo la generación hidroeléctrica y no era un problema aislado: Hungría había recortado la potencia de su central nuclear de Paks y Serbia mantenía su principal hidroeléctrica en torno al 20% de su capacidad. Compensar la pérdida mediante importaciones era difícil porque los países vecinos afrontaban problemas similares y la capacidad de interconexión era limitada.
Rumanía alteró provisionalmente el reparto de un río para conservar el caudal que necesitaba su último reactor operativo. Las detonaciones fueron la parte más visible de una intervención mucho más compleja, pensada para ganar unos días mientras la sequía seguía sin dar tregua. Como podemos ver, incluso una fuente estable como la nuclear puede quedar limitada por el agua cuando coinciden caudales excepcionalmente bajos, temperaturas elevadas y una demanda disparada por el calor.

articles.title: I tested the BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U — an affordable and effective 4K monitor for creative professionals
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U has a super-strong feature set for creative pros at a great price, including good colour coverage, support for multiple digital workflows and excellent connectivity. For general computing tasks, however, there are better value and more suitable 4K options.
Pros
- +Fantastic creator-centric feature set
- +Excellent connectivity
- +Nice build quality
Cons
- -Not a true HDR display
- -Limited SDR brightness
- -There are cheaper 4K options
Why you can trust TechRadar
If the clue is in the name, it's not hard to clock who the BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U is aimed at. This is a very well specified 27-inch 4K IPS monitor that's been carefully optimised for creative workflows while hitting an accessible price point.
For sure, there are still much cheaper 27-inch 4K monitors. But not with the suite of connectivity and colour management features offered here.
On the connectivity side, that includes Thunderbolt 4, an integrated KVM switch and display daisy chaining support. If anything, however, the features for creative workflows are even more comprehensive.
That starts with excellent colour coverage given the price point and extends to factory calibration and hardware calibration support, Pantone Validation, Calman certification, specific support for MacOS devices and more. There are also some neat extras, including a wireless control puck that makes it as quick and easy as possible to switch between colour modes and inputs.
The one obvious feature omission is true HDR capability. There is HDR10 support. But without local dimming hardware, the actual HDR performance is very limited. But then this monitor is not intended to replace an HDR reference monitor, which is a very different market with monitors costing upwards of 10 times the price.
On paper, then, the BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U looks set to take its place as the affordable display of choice for creative pros among the best photo editing monitors we've tested. But does it actually deliver?
BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U: Design and features
- Slick design
- Excellent connectivity
- Creator-centric feature set
Panel size: 27-inch
Panel type: IPS
Resolution: 3,840 x 2,160
Brightness: 400 nits
Contrast: 1,000:1 (static)
Pixel response: 5ms
Refresh rate: 60Hz
Color coverage: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Adobe RGB
HDR: HDR10
VESA: 100mm x 100mm
Connectivity: HDMI 2.0 x1, DisplayPort 1.4 x1, Thunderbolt 4 x2 with 90W PD and daisy chaining, USB hub with USB-C x1 and USB-A x3
The BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U looks familiar and that's no bad thing. It sports BenQ's premium design ethic of the last few years and it remains a cut above much of the competition in terms of both visual appeal and overall build quality.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The part metal construction and gun metal colorway is certainly more appealing than the often creaky feeling and anonymous black plastic of much of the monitor market, that's for sure. OK, Apple's displays including the latest Studio Display XDR, feel quite a bit better built still. But then they're much more expensive, too.
If styling is ultimately a subjective call, what can't be objectively denied is the BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U's excellent all-round feature set that's been fully optimised for creative professionals.
First up, there's good color coverage, including 99% of both DCI-P3 and Adobe RGB. Those figures are better than you'll find on cheaper 4K IPS monitors, which tend to be around the 95% to 97% range. The PD2732U also comes factory calibrated with sub-2 DeltaE across the board and further supports hardware calibration.
What's more, it's Pantone Validated, Pantone SkinTone Validated, and has Calman Verified certification. When you factor in the wide Adobe RGB coverage, this monitor is particularly well suited to digital-to-print workflows and photography, including SDR color grading.
It's also well specified for SDR video workflows, though with a peak brightness of 400 nits and no local dimming, it's far less optimised for HDR content, albeit with HDR10 and HLG support, it can at least accept an HDR signal.
Connectivity is another major part of the PD2732U's appeal, starting with a main Thunderbolt 4 interface and 90 W of power delivery. That's supported by a Thunderbolt out port, allowing for display daisy chaining and dual-monitor setups via a single cable. Incidentally, all of the primary connectors hook up perpendicularly on the rear as opposed to up from the bottom, which is generally a plus in terms of ease of use and access.
There's also Smart KVM, allowing you to use a single keyboard and mouse with two computing devices, handy if you regularly switch between, say, a Mac and PC. Speaking of Apple Macs, BenQ has included its M-Book color space mode, which BenQ says, "minimises the visual differences between the monitor and the connected MacBook series product."
Exactly how it differs from the P3 mode which BenQ also includes and aligns with the default P3 operation of MacOS isn't clear. But the results are good, all the same. With M-Book mode enabled, this display is an excellent visual match for MacBook displays.
Rounding out the main features both physically and figuratively is the BenQ Hotkey Puck. It's basically a wireless controller that simplifies settings access via shortcut functionality. It offers three customisable keys for quick access to Color Mode, Input, KVM, or app launch. It also has a rotary dial for precise control over brightness, contrast, and volume.
BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U: Performance
- Good color coverage
- Nicely calibrated
- Limited SDR brightness
If you want a really succinct summary of the BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U's performance, what you're looking at is a 27-inch 4K IPS monitor with some added color coverage and capability.
Out of the box, it's very nicely calibrated, both in sRGB mode on PC or in M-Book mode with a Mac. In both cases, color rendering is accurate and pleasing. The one potential snag is brightness in SDR mode.
For most serious professional SDR content creation workflows, this is not going to be a problem. You'll likely be targeting a brightness level well below 200 nits, which this display will easily achieve. But it won't do the full 400 nits in any of its SDR modes.
If anything, what the capped SDR brightness does is underline that this monitor isn't an ideal choice for generic computing remits, where you might want a bit more day-to-day pop. You can pay less and get more in that regard from what you might call a standard 27-inch 4K monitor.
That said, you can see the full capability, in brightness terms, of the PD2732U in HDR mode. Indeed, if you then crank up the brightness of SDR content in either the MacOS or Windows display settings, the result is actually nicely calibrated SDR colors and plenty of visual punch. But that's ultimately something of an aside given that this monitor lacks local dimming and has very limited actual HDR capability.
It's also worth noting that the refresh rate is limited to 60Hz. Again, for the content creation remit, this is not a technical limitation. It's just that if you are used to 120Hz-plus displays, 60Hz doesn't feel terribly slick or responsive. It's a day-to-day feel issue rather than being relevant to the vast majority of content workflows.
Of course, as a 27-inch 4K monitor, you also get decent pixel density and thus good image detail and crisp text rendering. The pixel density of around 160DPI isn't up to full Apple Retina display standards, which would require something above 200DPI and a native resolution of 5K on this display size. But it's still pretty sharp.
BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U: Final verdict
The BenQ Creative Pro PD2732U is either very sharply priced or not great value depending on what you're looking for. As a general computing display it's both pretty expensive and slightly flawed.
You can get far cheaper 27-inch 4K IPS monitors than this. Indeed, you can have one with 144Hz refresh for under half the price. What you won't get for less money, or arguably even the same price as the PD2732U's $699 / £649 asking, is anything like the same feature set for content creation.
The combination of excellent color coverage, various validation standards, and good factory calibration makes this an excellent choice for a sensible-money monitor for SDR content creation of pretty much any kind.
Sure, it's arguably still more of a prosumer display than, say, a true professional class grading monitor. But even in a really demanding professional context, it wouldn't be at all shabby, which is impressive for the price.
Then factor in some neat touches, like the wireless control puck, and excellent connectivity and you have a recipe for one of the most compelling content creation monitors currently available at an affordable price point. That's very much the remit BenQ was aiming for and fair to say the company has nailed it.
For more displays, we've tested the best business monitors and the best monitors for video editing.

articles.title: Dolby Vision 2 is rolling out now, starting with select Hisense TVs
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Dolby Laboratories and Hisense have announced that Dolby Vision 2 has begun rolling out to customers as a firmware update. The first sets to get the feature all come from Hisense's 2026 lineup, and include the UX, UR9, UR8, and U7 models. Each model must be running either Google TV or VIDAA, Hisense's own television operating system, for the update to be installed.
Dolby Vision 2 is the successor to Dolby Vision, the dynamic HDR format that has adjusted brightness and color on a scene-by-scene basis for more than a decade. Dolby unveiled the sequel last September, just ahead of the IFA show in Berlin, then spent the following 11 months gradually answering questions about what it actually does.
It turns out the technology does quite a bit, with features spread across two tiers: a standard version and a higher-end variant that Dolby calls Dolby Vision 2 Max. The standard version relies on a rebuilt image engine, which is why Dolby believes existing Dolby Vision movies and games will look better as soon as the firmware update is installed.
The engine performs that work blindly, improving whatever content you put on the screen without knowing anything about it in advance. Sitting alongside it is a second feature that does the opposite, reading the metadata attached to a title – both newly authored metadata and information already embedded in older releases.
Dolby calls it Content Intelligence, and it allows the TV to follow instructions left behind by whoever mastered the content for a given scene. This helps because a murky stretch of a thriller and a floodlit soccer match require very different handling. The feature works this out automatically instead of forcing viewers to switch between picture modes.
That slider and the image engine behind it are what everyone on the standard tier gets. The Max tier is where all four of those Hisense models really stand out, starting with Authentic Motion. This feature smooths out judder while attempting to avoid the soap opera effect that plagues most motion-processing systems. Light Sense 2 is included as well, using your TV's ambient light sensor to keep dark scenes visible in a sunlit room.
It's worth noting that none of this will reach older Dolby Vision TVs, as the format requires a specific piece of silicon – the MediaTek Pentonic 800 – to handle the processing. Those sets can still play Dolby Vision 2 content, of course, but they will ignore the additional metadata included with it.
For now, content authored specifically to take advantage of that metadata remains limited, with Canal+, Peacock, and iQIYI the only streaming services Dolby has named so far. Netflix and Disney+ are absent from that list for now.
Beyond those three, Dolby has some TCL sets and European Philips TVs lined up for later this year.

articles.title: Como mudar a senha do Gmail: 4 métodos para alterar a palavra-passe do login • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como mudar a senha do Gmail: 4 métodos para alterar a palavra-passe do login
Trocar a senha do Gmail periodicamente mantém a Conta Google protegida e encerra automaticamente sessões ativas em outros dispositivos para impedir acessos não autorizados
Mudar a senha do Gmail é um procedimento essencial para proteger a Conta Google e pode ser realizado via link direto, pelo aplicativo Gmail, pelo app Google ou via navegador no PC. Em todos os quatro métodos, o processo centraliza a alteração da palavra-passe em um único local, garantindo a proteção do ecossistema digital.
Após alterar a senha do Gmail, o sistema pode encerrar automaticamente as sessões ativas em navegadores e dispositivos para impedir acessos não autorizados. Além disso, será necessário atualizar a nova credencial em gerenciadores de senhas e apps de terceiros.
A seguir, veja o passo a passo para trocar a senha do Gmail em diferentes meios.
O link direto para trocar a senha do Gmail é ideal para quem já está conectado à Conta Google e lembra da senha atual. Ele simplifica o processo ao levar o usuário diretamente à página de segurança para redefinição.
Alterar a senha do Gmail pelo aplicativo para celular Android ou iPhone é a solução para quem prefere gerenciar a Conta Google em dispositivos móveis. O app agiliza a verificação ao utilizar o login pré-existente para fazer as alterações de segurança.
O uso do aplicativo do Google para mudar a senha do e-mail é indicado para quem prefere centralizar a segurança da Conta Google, mas não utiliza o app nativo do Gmail. A ferramenta unifica as configurações em um único local, facilitando a vida dos usuários.
Mudar a senha da Conta Google e do Gmail pelo navegador no PC é indicado para quem busca uma interface completa com recursos avançados. O método oferece visão abrangente do painel de segurança.
Acesse o site gmail.com pelo navegador do seu PC, clique na sua foto de perfil no canto superior direito e selecione “Gerenciar sua Conta do Google”.
Selecione a opção “Senha do Google”, localizada no menu lateral esquerdo, para avançar.
Insira a credencial atual ou use um dos métodos disponíveis para fazer login para acessar a opção para trocar o código de acesso da conta.
Digite a nova palavra-passe no campo indicado, repita a combinação e clique no botão “Alterar senha” para finalizar o processo.
Para recuperar a senha do Gmail, acesse a página de login da Conta Google e clique na opção “Esqueceu a senha?”. O sistema iniciará a verificação de identidade enviando um código por SMS, e-mail alternativo ou notificação no celular Android cadastrado.
Após validar a identidade no fluxo de recuperação, o sistema libera a tela para mudar a senha do Gmail com uma nova credencial. Por fim, lembre-se de atualizar essa nova palavra-passe no seu gerenciador de senhas para evitar contratempos nos próximos logins no Gmail.
Diversas medidas de segurança são aplicadas automaticamente ao trocar a senha do Gmail e da Conta Google:
Ao alterar a senha do Gmail, sua passkey configurada não é excluída nem desativada da Conta Google. Isso acontece porque a chave de acesso utiliza a biometria ou o PIN do próprio dispositivo, operando independentemente da palavra-passe tradicional.
A única mudança é o encerramento automático das sessões ativas em outros aparelhos para proteção do perfil. Dessa forma, você mantém o acesso prático via passkey no aparelho principal, tendo a nova senha como uma alternativa segura de login.
Não existe diferença entre a senha do Gmail e da Conta Google, pois ambas são exatamente a mesma credencial de acesso. Por ser um ecossistema integrado, um único código dá entrada direta ao e-mail e a serviços como Drive, YouTube e Fotos.
Consequentemente, ao redefinir a senha no Gmail, a alteração é sincronizada automaticamente em todos os produtos associados. A única exceção ocorre ao utilizar senhas de aplicativos específicas para softwares antigos, mas o login principal permanece centralizado na Conta Google.

articles.title: Une mise à jour de ChatGPT corrige deux gros défauts et supprime une limite majeure
articles.text:
OpenAI a déployé une mise à jour qui s’attaque à certains problèmes bien connus des utilisateurs de ChatGPT. Le modèle de langage devrait ainsi moins donner de fausses informations avec assurance et moins tergiverser alors que la question impliquait une brève réponse. Mais surtout, OpenAI fait sauter la limitation d’utilisation de GPT-5.6 pour les utilisateurs Free et Go.
La limite d’utilisation de GPT-5.6 pour les utilisateurs Free et Go disparaît
La plupart des utilisateurs de la version gratuite de ChatGPT ont déjà fait face à ce message particulièrement frustrant : « Vous avez atteint la limite de messages pour GPT-5.6 ». Deux solutions étaient alors proposées : passer à une offre payante ou ouvrir une nouvelle discussion et bénéficier d’un modèle moins performant. Bonne nouvelle, OpenAI a décidé de faire sauter cette limitation pour les utilisateurs Free et Go. Dès aujourd’hui, ces derniers peuvent interagir sans limite avec GPT-5.6 Luna, qui devient donc le modèle par défaut pour les utilisateurs Free et Go en remplaçant GPT-5.5. Précision importante : il est seulement ici question des échanges textuels. Les envois de fichiers, d’images ainsi que les fonctions les plus exigeantes resteront quant à eux soumis à des quotas.
Mais cela n’est pas tout. En effet, les utilisateurs disposant d’un compte gratuit bénéficient d’un nouveau mode baptisé « Think ». Celui-ci propose un raisonnement approfondi lorsqu’il est question de sujets complexes.
ChatGPT devrait moins donner de fausses informations avec assurance
Avec sa nouvelle mise à jour, OpenAI s’attaque à certains problèmes bien connus des utilisateurs de ChatGPT. Le modèle de langage vous a déjà donné de fausses informations avec une assurance déconcertante ? L’entreprise de Sam Altman assure avoir travaillé pour corriger ce point. ChatGPT devrait donc faire preuve de plus de prudence lorsqu’il a des doutes sur une information. Autre correction plus que bienvenue : OpenAI assure que ChatGPT donne dorénavant des réponses plus directes et concises. Fini donc les dissertations alors que vous lui avez demandé les ingrédients pour faire un gâteau au chocolat. Du moins, on l’espère. Notons également l’apparition d’un curseur qui permet de définir le temps de réflexion accordé au chatbot. Placé à une extrémité, ChatGPT donnera des réponses courtes, de façon rapide. Placé à l’autre extrémité, l’IA prendra le temps de rechercher des informations et de les assembler, comme le mode « Think » le fait.
OpenAI assure également que son modèle de langage est dorénavant plus précis sur les informations factuelles, comme les dates, les chiffres, les règles ou encore les résultats obtenus lors d’une recherche sur le web. Enfin, précisons que les abonnés Plus et Pro bénéficient quant à eux d’une version plus avancée de GPT-5.6 Sol. Certaines de ces nouveautés sont en cours de déploiement. Il se peut donc que vous ne les voyiez pas, ou ne les percevez pas, dès aujourd’hui. Dans tous les cas, OpenAI frappe un grand coup en instaurant GPT-5.6 Luna comme modèle par défaut, sans limite d’utilisation, pour les utilisateurs Free et Go.

articles.title: IA : chez ByteDance, on dit non à la distillation
articles.text:
Il est de bon ton d'accuser les géants chinois de l'IA de s'adonner à la distillation. Pourtant, l'un d'eux vient de s'élever contre la pratique, avec des arguments intéressants.
Que ce soit à la sortie de DeepSeek R1 en janvier 2025, ou plus récemment du modèle IA de Moonshoot, Kimi K3, la même accusation est sortie des États-Unis : la distillation. Pour rappel, cette pratique permet de transmettre le savoir déjà travaillé d'un modèle « enseignant » à un modèle « élève », et donc de produire un modèle IA presque aussi performant en travaillant infinimement moins. Et pourtant, même en Chine, on critique cette pratique.
ByteDance demande à ses équipes d'éviter la distillation
La distillation a-t-elle des limites ? Il semble que oui, vu ce qu'il se passe du côté de ByteDance (le géant chinois à l'origine de TiKTok). En effet, selon le média étatique The Paper, dont Reuters se fait l'écho, le fondateur Zhang Yiming a demandé à ses équipes d'éviter la pratique de la distillation pour améliorer leurs modèles IA.
Toujours selon la même source, Zhang Yiming aurait expliqué, à l'occasion d'une réunion interne, que le développement de l'IA nécessitait « une vision à long terme et une capacité à différer la gratification, plutôt que de s'appuyer sur les résultats des autres pour figurer en tête des classements à court terme ».
Pour le géant chinois, la distillation interfère dans le développement technologique à long terme
En somme, si la distillation permet de sembler à la hauteur, sur le long terme, la pratique empêcherait les entreprises d'intelligence artificielle de développer une base robuste à partir de laquelle créer leurs propres IA. Et c'est cette vision que Zhang Yiming veut propager dans son groupe.
Il a ainsi exhorté l'équipe de recherche Seed AI de « sacrifier certains gains à court terme au profit d'objectifs à long terme ». Reste maintenant à savoir s'il s'agit d'une position que l'on retrouvera seulement chez ByteDance, ou si les autres géants chinois du secteur comme DeepSeek, Monshot ou Qwen (Alibaba) partagent le même genre de constat.

articles.title: Gadhouse Unveils the Wesley Wired Headphones
articles.text:
Friday, August 7th 2026
	
	
	
	
Gadhouse Unveils the Wesley Wired Headphones
Audio lifestyle brand Gadhouse today announced a renewed focus on analog listening culture, led by its retro-inspired Wesley Wired On-Ear Headphones. As cassette tapes, wired audio and physical music formats continue to experience a global resurgence—driven largely by younger listeners—Wesley has been created to meet growing demand for simple, dependable and tactile audio experiences. The Wesley headphones are available from Amazon and Amazon UK for $69.99/£50.62.
Recent industry data shows that analog formats are enjoying their strongest revival in more than a decade. UK cassette sales have risen for ten consecutive years, reaching their highest level since 2003, while US cassette album sales grew 17.5% in 2025, climbing to 446,500 units—five times higher than a decade ago. Early 2025 saw an even sharper rise, with cassette sales increasing 204.7% year-on-year in Q1. Gen Z listeners now account for 59% of physical music consumption, signalling a cultural shift toward ownership, collectability and analog authenticity.Against this backdrop, Wesley offers a modern take on classic wired listening, blending timeless '80s aesthetics with practical everyday usability.
Designed for students, commuters, remote workers, gamers and music lovers, the Wesley Wired On-Ear Headphones deliver rich, detailed audio through 40 mm dynamic drivers supporting 48 kHz lossless clarity. A built-in omnidirectional microphone and in-line control button allow for hands-free calls, play/pause and track skipping, while the lightweight 105 g design and PU leather/stainless steel headband ensure comfort throughout the day.
Wesley's plug-and-play wired connection removes the need for batteries, charging or Bluetooth pairing. The included USB-C to 3.5 mm adapter and 6.35 mm adapter provide compatibility with laptops, phones, tablets, mixers and studio equipment, making the headphones suitable for both everyday use and creative environments.
Inspired by the golden age of cassette players and synth-pop culture, Wesley reflects Gadhouse's commitment to celebrating classic audio formats while delivering modern performance.
Miko Cassette Player and Wesley bundle
The renewed interest in analog listening also aligns with Gadhouse's broader retrotech ecosystem. Alongside Wesley, the brand recently launched the Miko Cassette Player, a portable analog device featuring Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity, built-in recording and a translucent design inspired by the 1985-1995 cassette era. The Miko + Wesley bundle is available now, offering a complete retro-modern listening setup for fans of analog audio.
Gadhouse has also expanded its product lineup with blank cassette tapes and modular cassette storage, supporting the growing community of collectors, creators and analog enthusiasts who value the tactile experience of physical media.
"Wesley represents the simplicity and authenticity that people are rediscovering in analog audio," said the Gadhouse team. "As more listeners return to physical formats, we're committed to creating products that honor classic design while meeting the needs of today's users."

Heatwaves are getting so bad you can buy this portable 'human fridge' in Japan to save you from heatstroke — and it'll blast you with 41F air
