articles.title: 7 Books that reveal the psychology of human attachment
articles.text:
7 Books that reveal the psychology of human attachment
Explore 7 books that reveal the psychology of human attachment, relationships, emotional bonds, and why we connect with others.
Human attachment shapes almost every relationship we build. From childhood bonds to romantic connections and friendships, the way we attach to others influences how we love, trust, communicate, and handle emotional closeness. Some people find it easy to open their hearts, while others struggle with fear of rejection, emotional distance, or the need for constant reassurance.
These patterns are not random; they are often connected to our past experiences, beliefs, and emotional conditioning. Books on attachment psychology help us understand why we behave the way we do in relationships. They reveal how early experiences shape our emotional responses, why we repeat certain relationship patterns, and how we can develop healthier connections.
7 Books that explore the psychology behind human attachment
1. Attached by Amir Levine and Rachel Heller
Attached explains how attachment styles influence the way people behave in romantic relationships. The authors introduce three major attachment styles: secure, anxious, and avoidant, showing how each style affects communication, emotional needs, and relationship choices.
The book helps readers understand why some people seek constant reassurance while others prefer emotional independence. It teaches that recognising attachment patterns can help people build healthier relationships instead of repeating the same emotional cycles. For anyone curious about why they react differently to love, closeness, and conflict, Attached provides a simple introduction to attachment theory and relationship psychology.
2. Hold Me Tight by Sue Johnson
Sue Johnson’s Hold Me Tight explores the emotional foundation of romantic relationships and explains why people often experience repeated conflicts with their partners. Based on Emotionally Focused Therapy, the book reveals that many relationship struggles are connected to deeper fears of rejection, loneliness, and not feeling valued.
Johnson explains that beneath arguments, people are often seeking emotional safety and reassurance. The book teaches readers how to create stronger emotional bonds by understanding their partner’s needs and responding with empathy instead of defensiveness.
3. The Body Keeps the Score by Bessel van der Kolk
The Body Keeps the Score explores how past experiences, especially traumatic ones, can influence emotions, relationships, and the way people connect with others. Bessel van der Kolk explains that difficult experiences can affect the brain and body, shaping how people respond to trust, vulnerability, and emotional closeness.
The book shows why some individuals struggle with intimacy or feel unsafe even in supportive relationships.
Through research and personal stories, it highlights the importance of healing emotional wounds to create healthier connections.
4. Insecure in Love by Leslie Becker-Phelps
Insecure in Love focuses on how insecurity affects romantic relationships and why some people constantly fear losing the people they care about. Leslie Becker-Phelps explains that attachment anxiety can lead to overthinking, seeking reassurance, and becoming overly dependent on a partner’s approval.
The book helps readers understand where these patterns come from and how they can develop greater emotional security. It provides practical guidance for breaking unhealthy relationship habits and building stronger self-worth.
5. Attached at the Heart by Barbara Nicholson and Lysa Parker
Attached at the Heart explores attachment from the perspective of parenting and early emotional bonds between children and caregivers. The authors explain how responsive and caring relationships during childhood can influence emotional development, confidence, and the ability to form healthy relationships later in life.
The book highlights the importance of understanding children’s emotional needs and shows how early attachment experiences can shape the way people connect throughout their lives.
6. Love Sense by Sue Johnson
Love Sense explores the science behind romantic love and explains why emotional connection is essential for human survival and happiness. Sue Johnson challenges the idea that love is simply a feeling and presents it as a powerful emotional bond shaped by our need for safety and connection.
The book combines psychology and research to explain why people seek deep relationships and how those bonds can be strengthened. It helps readers understand love as an attachment system rather than just an emotional experience.
7. The Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work by John Gottman and Nan Silver
This book explores the psychology behind successful long-term relationships and reveals what helps couples maintain strong emotional connections. John Gottman’s research shows that healthy relationships depend on communication, understanding, respect, and emotional responsiveness.
The book explains how small daily interactions influence trust and attachment between partners. It provides practical lessons for improving relationships and understanding the behaviours that create lasting emotional security.
Understanding our need for connection
Human attachment is one of the most powerful forces shaping our lives. These books show that our relationship patterns are influenced by our experiences, emotions, and the ways we learned to seek connection. Understanding attachment psychology allows us to recognise unhealthy patterns, communicate better, and create deeper relationships. By becoming aware of how we attach to others, we can move toward more secure and meaningful connections.

articles.title: Bose lance le QC Headphones (Gen 2) : la marque pique le meilleur du QC Ultra, sans faire exploser la facture
articles.text:
Bose lance le QC Headphones (Gen 2) : la marque pique le meilleur du QC Ultra, sans faire exploser la facture
Fidèle à sa stratégie des petits pas, Bose fait évoluer son QC Headphones avec un design modernisé, des fonctions héritées du QC Ultra Headphones et une réduction de bruit annoncée comme plus efficace. Une mise à jour discrète, mais qui entend maintenir le casque dans la course.
Si ses produits parviennent à rester actuels et à pratiquement toujours s’imposer comme des références dans leurs catégories, Bose est connu pour ses mises à jour très discrètes, voire minimales. En effet, le QC Headphones premier du nom est quasiment identique à son aîné QC 45, qui lui-même l’était par rapport au QC 35. Le QC Headphones (2e génération) ne fait pas exception à la règle, mais force est de reconnaître une volonté d’évolution sans faire grimper la facture.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2e génération)
Ce nouveau casque Bluetooth de milieu/haut de gamme entend donc moderniser le design de son emblématique prédécesseur tout en héritant de fonctionnalités jusqu’alors réservées au QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération) , le fleuron du catalogue de Bose.
Une esthétique moderne empruntée au QC Ultra
Côté design, la principale nouveauté réside dans l’abandon du système de réglage cranté un peu daté, au profit d’un ajustement interne coulissant, plus discret. Il est ainsi possible de déployer le casque sans que cela n’altère son esthétique, tandis que cette évolution a permis d’affiner les branches dans un souci d’épure. On note également un rembourrage recouvert de similicuir plus étendu que sur la première génération, à l’image du QC Ultra, tandis que Bose annonce avoir retravaillé la force de serrage afin de trouver le meilleur compromis entre confort et maintien.
Parmi les autres détails, on note des boutons physiques mieux intégrés ainsi qu’un tissu acoustique désormais coloré, tandis que son poids demeure contenu à 230 g, ce qui en fait toujours l’un des casques sans fil les plus légers du marché.
Technologie True Spatial et audio lossless en USB-C
Bien qu’il y en ait toujours avec la marque américaine, comme c’était le cas lors des lancements des QC Ultra Earbuds (2e génération) et du QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération), Bose ne donne aucun détail sur d’éventuelles optimisations acoustiques, si ce n’est la reconduction de son traitement numérique du signal SoundDesign. Héritant de la technologie True Spatial déjà présente sur le modèle Ultra, le QC Headphones (2e génération) met l’accent sur l’audio spatial, qui applique une spatialisation tridimensionnelle à n’importe quelle piste audio. Celle-ci se décline en trois modes : Still, Motion et Cinema, proposant respectivement une scène sonore fixe, un suivi des mouvements de tête et une virtualisation optimisée pour les contenus audiovisuels.
À l’instar de son grand frère, le QC Headphones (2e génération) introduit aussi la prise en charge des flux audio sans perte jusqu’à 24 bits/48 kHz à partir de n’importe quelle source via son port USB-C. En contrepartie, le casque abandonne le port mini-jack 3,5 mm de son aîné, mais est tout de même livré avec un câble mini-jack vers USB-C pour une connexion aux sources analogiques.
Intoduction d'ActiveSense, ANC mieux adpaté aux fuites acoustiques, etc.
Comme sur les autres modèles, l’audio spatial Immersion peut être activé directement via les commandes du casque, tout comme le mode Cinema, le mode Conscient et la réduction de bruit baptisée Silencieux. Ce dernier aurait d’ailleurs été amélioré par rapport à celui du QC Headphones, notamment grâce à une meilleure adaptabilité aux fuites acoustiques, afin de conserver un bon niveau d’isolation lorsque l’on porte des lunettes ou si le casque vient à légèrement se déplacer.
Par ailleurs, Bose annonce une meilleure efficacité de la technologie ActiveSense associée au mode Conscient, qui applique temporairement la réduction de bruit lorsqu’un bruit soudain est détecté. De plus, comme sur le QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération), il est désormais possible de désactiver entièrement ces traitements afin d’utiliser le casque en isolation passive.
L’application propose également accès à un égaliseur 3 bandes toujours aussi chiche, à la gestion des appareils Bluetooth appairés, à la personnalisation partielle des commandes, entre autres. Enfin, la marque promet des appels plus clairs en environnement bruyant grâce à un algorithme annoncé comme plus efficace.
Connectivité toujours chiche, autonomie inchangée
Côté connectivité, si le casque passe à une puce Bluetooth 5.4 moderne, Bose n’a communiqué ni sur une éventuelle compatibilité avec des codecs avancés ni sur la prise en charge de la norme LE Audio. Il est donc probable que le QC Headphones (2e génération) se contente des codecs AAC et SBC, l’aptX Adaptive demeurant l’apanage du QC Ultra. En revanche, le multipoint et Google Fast Pair sont toujours de la partie afin de permettre une connexion simultanée à deux appareils et un appairage simplifié sur Android.
Le QC Headphones (2e génération) promet une autonomie de 24 h, comme son prédécesseur, tandis qu’une fonction de charge rapide permettrait de récupérer jusqu’à 2 h 30 min d’écoute après seulement 15 min de charge.
Le casque est disponible en précommande dès aujourd’hui pour les membres My Bose, et les premières expéditions sont prévues pour le 13 août. Il est proposé au tarif de 349,95 € dans des coloris inédits hérités du QC Ultra (Eucalyptus Green, Menthe Rosée et Mauve Rosé), en plus des classiques noir et blanc.
Bien qu’il soit affiché 50 € moins cher que le QC Headphones à son lancement, conformément à la nouvelle stratégie tarifaire du constructeur américain, son prix paraît particulièrement élevé pour un casque historiquement positionné à mi-chemin entre le milieu et le haut de gamme. À l’heure où le Sennheiser Momentum 4 Wireless est toujours disponible sous la barre des 200 € et où le Nothing Headphone (1) a franchi un nouveau cap en matière de rapport qualité/prix, ce nouveau venu devra convaincre autrement que par son seul nom. Rappelons toutefois que le QC Headphones (2e génération) a vocation à voir son prix diminuer au fil du temps, comme en témoigne la première génération, désormais commercialisée en dessous de 250 €.

articles.title: El eclipse va a ser una gran fiesta en la España rural. Para AEMET el riesgo es clarísimo: más incendios
articles.text:
Este 12 de agosto, un eclipse solar cruzará casi toda la mitad norte de la península, trazando una diagonal desde A Coruña hasta Palma y oscureciendo capitales como Oviedo, León, Bilbao, Zaragoza y Valencia. Este es un evento que se ve como una oportunidad histórica para atraer turismo a numerosos puntos de la España vaciada, pero también hay que tener en cuenta que estamos en un momento donde hay un gran peligro de que se produzca un incendio. Y esto está generando ya importantes consecuencias en el ámbito social.
Las aglomeraciones. Esto no significa que el eclipse solar vaya a provocar un incendio en alguno de nuestros bosques, pero sí que existen riesgos indirectos derivados de la gran confluencia de personas en zonas forestales, la movilidad masiva y sobre todo, las conductas incívicas que pueden tener más de algunos en espacios naturales.
La AEMET ya ha alertado de que el riesgo de incendios forestales para el día del eclipse será "muy alto" o "extremo" en gran parte del territorio, y la Dirección General de Protección Civil define la situación como un "cóctel peligroso", recordando que el peligro real radica en las multitudes acudiendo a montes secos y calientes.
Lo que preocupa es cómo se acaben comportando las personas que acuden a los bosques a ver el eclipse, puesto que una colilla mal apagada, barbacoas, vehículos aparcados sobre pastizales secos y la presencai de personas poco habituadas en el campo son posibles desencadenantes para que se inicie un incendio forestal.
Para controlar esta situación, se ha creado una Unidad de Valoración de Riesgos (UVR) liderada por AEMET y otros expertos. Además, a partir de este viernes, el propio servicio meteorológico emitirá un boletín diario especial que incluirá predicciones específicas del índice de peligro de incendios forestales para poder organizar mucho mejor a estas grandes confluencias de personas.
La España rural se blinda. Ante el temor de que una chispa desate una tragedia medioambiental, ya se están tomando diferentes medidas. Por ejemplo, el Gobierno de Aragón activará su plan de emergencias en nivel 1, prohibiendo el acceso a los montes mediante vehículos a motor y el uso de fuego al aire libre.
Aquí Miguel Ángel Clavero, director general del Interior y Emergencias del gobierno de Aragón, en declaraciones al Periódico de Aragón, apunta que la recomendación es que cada uno vea el eclipse desde la localidad en la que se hospeda y evite los desplazamientos.
Y hay más. Además de estas recomendaciones, que parecen obvias, también se ha decidido prohibir las raves y acampadas en el monte, provocando la cancelación de festivales vinculados al evento astronómico, como el "Iberia Eclipse" en Soria, que se ha trasladado a las montañas de León tras el rechazo de Vinuesa, pese a que de momento está pendiente de los muchos trámites que se deben completas al estar en un espacio protegido, haciendo que todavía no se sepa si se va a llevar a cabo. Algo que también ha ocurrido con las actividades en el embalse de La Sotonera, que se han cancelado por el riesgo de incendio.
En el caso de Castilla-La Mancha, la comisión encargada del evento ha advertido que la afluencia turística multiplicará los riesgos de propagación de incendios, pidiendo a los ciudadanos que eviten desplazamientos innecesarios y observen el fenómeno desde sus municipios de residencia. También este ha sido el caso de Tres Cantos, que ha decidido suspender el programa de actividades y limitará la movilidad para acudir al entorno del Monte del Pardo.
Los expertos avisan. Desde el Colegio Oficial de Ingenieros Forestales y Medio Natural no han dudado en mostrar también su preocupación por el aumento de tráfico o de los visitantes no familiarizados con el territorio. Aquí lanzan recomendaciones que son obvias, como evitar concentraciones desordenadas en zonas forestales que no están preparadas para grandes afluencias y no encender fuego bajo ninguna circunstancia.
Entre los vecinos el sentimiento es compartido, puesto que están viendo que hay muchos factores de riesgo que van a llegar a su entorno en ese día. En la sierra madrileña, que ha sido duramente castigada por los incendios en estas últimas semanas, colectivos como la plataforma vecinal "Monte en Pie" se han concentrado para protestar contra la organización de eventos masivos en la naturaleza.
En esta línea, los vecinos celebran la cancelación de algunas de estas citas que se han organizado en ambientes rurales y advierten de la gran irresponsabilidad que supone congregar multitudes entre arbolado y pasto seco. Su lema resume perfectamente el sentir de estas comunidades: el eclipse dura unos minutos, pero las consecuencias de un incendio duran décadas.
Lo que hay que hacer. De cara al gran día, la recomendación de la Comisión Interministerial apunta a que está expresamente prohibido encender fuego y se desaconseja por completo aparcar sobre vegetación. Las autoridades piden a la población que los mapas de riesgo de la AEMET se conviertan en la brújula para planificar la observación, instando a los ciudadanos a quedarse en entornos urbanos o seguir el evento desde casa si las zonas forestales cercanas se encuentran en riesgo extremo.

articles.title: Datadog shares plummet despite expectation-topping quarterly results - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Datadog shares plummet despite expectation-topping quarterly results
Datadog Inc.’s shares closed 19% lower today after it posted quarterly results and guidance that topped expectations.
New York-based Datadog is a major provider of observability software. It also sells cybersecurity tools, a user experience monitoring suite and various related products.
Several factors may be at play behind today’s stock selloff. Some investors may have decided to lock in their gains following a year in which Datadog’s share price rose more than 90%. A new disclosure about the company’s largest customer, an unnamed artificial intelligence provider, may have also factored into the selloff.
Datadog executives stated today that the customer in question recently renewed a nine-figure contract. Nevertheless, it plans to reduce its product usage this year by cutting user seats.
Datadog’s sales rose 36% year-over-year in the second quarter to $1.12 billion. The FactSet consensus estimate forecasted $1.08 billion. More than 40% of the company’s revenue came from customers who spend over $100,000 on its products per year. Datadog had about 4,720 such customers as of June 30, 870 more than a year earlier.
“Datadog delivered a strong quarter, with 36% year-over-year revenue growth, $316 million in operating cash flow, and $279 million in free cash flow,” said Datadog Chief Executive Officer Olivier Pomel.
The company says that more than half of its customers use at least four different products. According to Datadog, the large AI provider that renewed its contract uses 17 products. The observability provider regularly adds new tools to its software portfolio to maintain its revenue growth.
The two latest additions to Datadog’s product lineup made their debut in June. Bits Agent Builder enables users to create AI agents optimized for tasks such as finding cybersecurity issues and troubleshooting outages. The Datadog Agent Console, the second new product that debuted in June, monitors how users interact with AI agents.
The company maintains its product release cadence by spending over 30% of its revenue on research and development. Occasionally, Datadog also invests in acquisitions. The company recently bought a startup called Adaptive ML Inc. to accelerate its internal AI development efforts. Adaptive ML developed tools that ease reinforcement learning projects.
Datadog delivered an adjusted operating income of $257 million in the second quarter, which breaks down to adjusted earnings of $0.65 per share. Analysts had expected $0.58 per share.
The company’s full-year guidance also topped the consensus estimate. Datadog expects to generate adjusted earnings of $2.52 per share at the midpoint on between $4.45 billion and $4.47 billion in revenue. Analysts expected adjusted earnings of $2.46 per share and $4.36 billion in revenue.

articles.title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
articles.text:
The Internet is awash in AI content, and it’s not always easy to tell it apart from genuine human creations. While images and videos are perhaps the most obvious type of AI slop, streaming music services like Spotify are also being inundated with AI-generated tunes. Suno is one of the most prolific sources of this AI music, but the company now says it’s looking to clean up its act with watermarks and policy changes.
In a blog post announcing the plans, Suno CEO and co-founder Mikey Shulman says this is a necessary change to meet “emerging industry standards” for the labeling of AI content. Soon, the company will add watermarks to all audio outputs from its models, giving platforms the option to mark content as AI or block it entirely. Shulman doesn’t say if Suno will rely on an in-house solution or a ready-made solution like Google’s SynthID.
Google recently began licensing SynthID to other companies. Google says the tech has been used to label 60,000 years’ worth of audio generated by its Gemini models, plus more than 100 billion images and videos.
Whatever technology Suno uses, the idea is that every track it generates will have an invisible code embedded in the waveform. A detector trained on that signature will be able to identify it, allowing Suno’s partners to combat “fraud and misuse.” Shulman notes the watermarking tech Suno intends to use is “durable and resistant to tampering” without affecting quality.
However, no system is perfect. If someone does manage to break Suno’s watermarks, all the tracks produced to that point could be stripped of their AI labels. And this doesn’t solve the problem of proliferating AI music. There are other platforms that don’t have plans for watermarking, and open models could allow people to generate unlabeled AI music on their own hardware. That’s a problem with all efforts to watermark AI content.

articles.title: AI slop, privacy fears, and endless scrolling are making people fall out of love with the internet
articles.text:
A hot potato: Remember the days when the internet was a fun place full of memes and funny videos, and you couldn't use AI to fulfill the request, "photos or it didn't happen"? Today, many people's view of the net is becoming negative, with 50% of users expecting their data to be exposed, AI making everything hard to believe, and the web stealing too much of their time.
A survey by personal-data removal service Incogni illustrates the changing attitudes toward the internet. Given the company's business, it's little surprise to see a focus on data breaches.
More than 50% of participants believe that it's inevitable their personal data will be breached, with only 11% disagreeing with the statement. Gen Z (born between 1997 and 2012) were most confident they'd be safe, but a still-high 47% believe their data is bound to be hijacked. Gen X (born 1965 to 1980) were most pessimistic (56%).
These concerns were reflected in other questions. Half of the participants regret sharing their information online, while the possibility of having their data stolen made 63% anxious.
It's not just the fear of having details pilfered that's turning people off the internet. More netizens are starting to believe they spend too much time online (44%), while 45% think they spend just the right amount of time.
A slightly more modern online phenomenon is the proliferation of AI content. It's thanks to the countless AI-generated photos, videos, and news reports that almost half the participants are less sure what's real. 27% are tired of wading through AI slop, one in four is bothered by the lack of accountability for deepfake creators, and the whole AI situation makes 27% of people want to spend less time online.
Incogni compares the current problem of AI slop to spam email in the 1990s, though most would argue it's a lot worse, especially when used to incite division.
Social media is another element of the web that's been getting more awful. The survey reveals that 47% of people have deleted their account or a messaging app because it caused stress or anxiety, while 41% did the same thing over privacy concerns.
Incogni also asked the question: would you pay for an internet with no tracking or algorithmic feeds? Only 29% said yes, the majority of whom were in a high-income group, and 46% said no.
From privacy violations and AI slop to Dead Internet Theory becoming closer to reality, the modern internet has a lot of problems. But more people use it today than at any previous point, so those causing these issues are unlikely to care, sadly.

articles.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’
articles.text:
After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’
This move should prevent future electricity price increases.
The State Corporation Commission, Virginia’s independent state agency that regulates public utilities, has ordered data centers to pay for all the required transmission infrastructure that the project will use exclusively. According to Realtor.com, Governor Abigail Spanberger (D) has recently been pressing AI hyperscalers to reduce their impact on the power grid and utility prices.
Virginia currently has the greatest number of data centers across the U.S., with the state hosting at least 570 sites. Because of the massive power demand of these sites, the state has been experiencing issues with electricity price hikes, with one county even asking its employees, including schools, to conserve power. PJM Interconnection, which distributes power to the state, has increased prices by 76%, with Monitoring Analytics, the independent watchdog keeping an eye on the utility company, saying that this is mostly due to AI data centers.
The move requiring data centers to pay for their own upstream electrical infrastructure should, hopefully, ease the burden on the average Virginian. "We are taking real steps to address rising energy costs for Virginians," said Gov. Spanberger. "I will continue to work with the General Assembly and take action to make sure data centers pay their fair share, adhere to strict environmental standards, and listen to the concerns of local communities.”
This is one of the first statewide announcements that will enforce President Donald Trump’s ratepayer protection pledge. Trump summoned the biggest AI hyperscalers to the White House in early March and made them promise that they will “pay their own way” when it comes to building the infrastructure they need. But despite this, the burden of more expensive electricity hasn’t eased for the average American. The administration expanded this promise in late July to include state governors, utility companies, and data center developers.
Many critics said that this pledge is nothing but a piece of paper, with some comparing it to a “pinky promise.” After all, this is just a commitment and not a regulation that would penalize companies that don’t comply. Nevertheless, it seems that it has spurred at least one state to make a move that should, hopefully, have a material impact on the average citizen.
Aside from Virginia, Oregon is the only other state, so far, that has raised electrical rates for large consumers, like data centers. According to the Oregon POWER Act, facilities that consume 20 MW or more are assigned to a higher rate class. Portland General Electric, the state’s largest power supplier, has already implemented this, resulting in a 30% rate increase for these big power users, while also cutting residential costs by 1.3%.
While the average consumer isn’t necessarily paying for the power that data centers consume, utility companies had to conduct massive grid upgrades to support the increased demand from these developments. The utility companies then equally passed on all the necessary capital expenditure to all consumers, instead of just the data centers. By requiring data centers to spend on their own grid upgrades, further increases in electricity prices could, hopefully, be prevented.

articles.title: Schluss mit doppelten Baustellen: Branche will Glasfasernetze freiwillig teilen
articles.text:
Schluss mit doppelten Baustellen: Branche will Glasfasernetze freiwillig teilen
Um den Ausbau von schnellem Internet und Mobilfunk in Deutschland zu beschleunigen, schlägt ein Bündnis aus Stadtwerken und regionalen Telekommunikationsanbietern eine freiwillige Branchenvereinbarung vor. Die drei Branchenverbände BDEW, Breko und VKU – deren Mitgliedsunternehmen zusammen für knapp 60 Prozent der deutschen Glasfaseranschlüsse stehen – wollen damit neue staatliche Vorschriften verhindern und stattdessen auf freiwillige Kooperation setzen.
Der Kern der Initiative namens „Fairplay-Agreement“ liegt in einer gegenseitigen Öffnung der Netze (Open Access). Bislang scheitert eine flächendeckende Versorgung oft daran, dass Netze nicht geteilt werden oder Konkurrenten Straßen ein zweites Mal aufreißen, um eigene Glasfaserkabel parallel zu verlegen.
Glasfaserleitungen freigeben
Nach dem Willen der Verbände sollen sich Festnetzanbieter verpflichten, ihre Glasfaserleitungen zu fairen und gleichen Bedingungen für Konkurrenten freizugeben. Im Gegenzug fordern sie, dass auch die großen Mobilfunknetzbetreiber ihre Masten und 5G-Netze für andere Anbieter öffnen, um nahtlose Kombi-Angebote aus Festnetz und Mobilfunk zu ermöglichen.
Mit dem Vorstoß reagieren die Verbände auf Pläne der Bundesregierung, den Netzzugang künftig per Gesetz (§ 22a TKG) und über die Bundesnetzagentur strenger zu regeln. Aus Sicht der Anbieter schafft eine solche behördliche Regulierung jedoch Unsicherheit und schreckt Investoren ab.
Deutsche Telekom ist der „Elefant im Raum“
Auch wenn der Marktführer Deutsche Telekom im Papier nicht genannt wird, gilt der Bonner Konzern als Hauptadressat: Die regionalen Betreiber wollen verhindern, dass die Telekom in bereits versorgten Gebieten doppelt baut, und verlangen im Gegenzug fairen Zugang zum Telekom-Mobilfunknetz. Die Deutsche Telekom weist den Vorwurf eines gezielten oder unfairen Doppelausbaus regelmäßig zurück und betont, dass freier Wettbewerb und der eigenwirtschaftliche Netzausbau auch den Kunden die beste Infrastruktur und Anbieterauswahl sichern würden.
Für Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher könnte die Vereinbarung handfeste Vorteile bringen: Wenn Anbieter die bestehende Infrastruktur teilen, erhöht sich die Auswahl an Internetanbietern auf demselben Anschluss, unnötige Baustellen in Wohngebieten werden vermieden und der Wechsel zwischen Anbietern wird vereinfacht. Die Verbände forderten das Digitalministerium und die Bundesnetzagentur nun auf, entsprechende Verhandlungen zwischen den Marktteilnehmern einzuleiten.

articles.text:
We now have a better idea of what to expect from OpenAI’s long-rumoured speaker, courtesy of Bloomberg.
Per the publication’s ever-reliable Mark Gurman, this doughnut-shaped smart speaker will lack a display but be roughly the size of a hockey puck to make it easy to carry around the home in one hand. What’s more, Gurman says it will have advanced AI-powered “humanlike interactivity” and cost over US$300 (roughly C$420) when it releases sometime in 2027.
Notably, the unnamed speaker is being developed alongside former Apple design exec Jony Ive. The British-American designer left Apple in 2019 to pursue his own ventures, one of which, the AI company io Products, was acquired by OpenAI in 2025. Ive is one of many former Apple employees who have since joined OpenAI, a fact that’s at the heart of the iPhone maker’s trade secrets lawsuit against the ChatGPT company.
The speaker is reportedly the first in a “family” of devices that OpenAI is planning, although it’s unclear what that might entail. It also remains to be seen how many people would be interested in hardware from an AI company, especially one that’s known for sharing medical misinformation and failing to report an alarming ChatGPT account belonging to the individual who went on to kill many people in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

articles.title: « Pourrie jusqu’à la moelle » : OpenAI accuse Apple de vouloir masquer ses échecs dans l’IA
articles.text:
Pour rappel, Apple accuse deux de ses anciens employés, Chang Liu et Tang Tan, d’avoir volé des informations confidentielles et des secrets commerciaux avant de rejoindre OpenAI. Entre-temps, l’entreprise à la pomme a aussi suspecté 11 autres de ses anciens employés d’avoir été témoins ou impliqués dans cette affaire. Dans la foulée, elle a demandé au tribunal d’ordonner une procédure accélérée de communication de pièces afin de collecter rapidement les différentes preuves. De son côté, OpenAI réfute en bloc ces accusations et vient même de demander au juge de rejeter l’affaire.
Une procédure « pourrie jusqu’à la moelle »
Dans une requête déposée auprès d’un tribunal fédéral américain pour obtenir le rejet de la plainte d’Apple, OpenAI qualifie cette action en justice de « pourrie jusqu’à la moelle ». L’entreprise de Sam Altman assure qu’elle « n’a aucun besoin, aucune utilité ni aucun intérêt pour les secrets commerciaux d’Apple », tout en indiquant qu’« OpenAI développe quelque chose de totalement nouveau et différent de tout ce qui existe chez Apple ». Pour rappel, OpenAI travaille sur une famille d’appareils permettant d’interagir avec ChatGPT. Apple suspecte justement certains de ses anciens employés de se servir d’informations confidentielles pour mettre au point ces appareils.
L’entreprise de Sam Altman estime par ailleurs qu’Apple n’a pas démontré être propriétaire d’un « secret commercial protégeable », ni établi de manière plausible qu’un détournement d’informations avait eu lieu. OpenAI va même plus loin en considérant que la plainte d’Apple est un prétexte pour masquer les échecs de l’entreprise en matière d’intelligence artificielle et sa difficulté à fidéliser son personnel. Il est vrai que l’entreprise à la pomme a bel et bien été en retard dans la course à l’intelligence artificielle et qu’une partie de son personnel s’est fait siphonner par OpenAI. Mais cela explique-t-il réellement la plainte d’Apple ?
L’entreprise de Sam Altman assure qu’elle a en réalité aidé Apple
Apple a dévoilé des preuves que son ancien employé, Tang Tan, a gardé un accès résiduel à certains systèmes internes de l’entreprise. Pour OpenAI, la faute revient à Apple qui n’assure pas une bonne procédure de départ pour ses employés et qui déforme les faits.
En effet, l’entreprise de Sam Altman estime qu’elle a en réalité aidé Apple : « M. Tan a conservé ces informations afin de s’assurer que les nouveaux employés venant d’Apple respectent les procédures de départ d’Apple et ne conservent aucune information confidentielle d’Apple ». Qui a raison dans cette affaire ? Nul ne le sait pour l’instant. En revanche, il est peu probable que le juge accepte le rejet de l’affaire.

articles.title: Ten cuidado con las gafas que compres para ver el eclipse, no todas sirven y las consecuencias pueden ser muy graves
articles.text:
A estas alturas, todo el mundo es consciente del peligro que puede suponer mirar durante un tiempo prolongado al sol sin usar nada. Sin embargo, cuando hay eclipses, surgen teorías alternativas sobre cómo verlo: con las gafas de sol, radiografías y otros objetos cotidianos que para nada cumplen con la función, al menos de manera segura. La única manera de ver un eclipse directamente sin hacerte daño a la vista es usando unas gafas homologadas. Olvídate de lo demás.
En los últimos días seguramente hayas visto muchas promociones de gafas para ver el eclipse. En algunos sitios las regalan pero seguramente se hayan acabado ya por lo que la opción más cómoda es comprarlas en por Internet. Puedes encontrar ofertas muy interesantes, con packs de cuatro gafas (dos para adulto y dos para niños) por poco más de diez euros. También tienes un pack de dos gafas por seis euros o un pack de 10 gafas por sólo 24 euros. Además, gracias al envío rápido, te aseguras que llegue prácticamente de un día para otro, pero no lo dejes escapar mucho porque el eclipse es el próximo miércoles 12 de agosto, alrededor de las 7 de la tarde.
Pack de cuatro gafas homologadas para ver el eclipse del 12 de agosto.
*Los precios pueden haber cambiado desde la publicación
Mirar al Sol directamente puede dañar la retina, provocando quemaduras solares en la superficie ocular debido a los rayos ultravioletas.
Lo más importante: gafas homologadas
Cuando vayas a comprar las gafas, la clave es que estén homologadas y cumplan con el estándar ISO 12312-2 y llevar también impreso el distintivo CE de la Unión Europea. También debes fijarte en el nombre y dirección del fabricante, la fecha de caducidad y que las instrucciones de uso vengan correctamente explicadas. Si quieres saber más sobre el estándar ISO, puedes verlo aquí.
De esta manera, es muy importante que no compres gafas donde no aparezca este estándar porque tus ojos corren un serio problema, con secuelas que pueden ser para siempre. Además, ten en cuenta que el precio suele ser de unos tres euros por lo que desconfía de ofertas demasiado baratas o revisa que tenga esta certificación.
¿Me puedo quitar las gafas durante el eclipse total?
Durante la fase previa y siempre que estés mirando el sol, debes tener puesta las gafas. Sólo puedes quitártelas y mirar directamente al sol cuando el eclipse sea total y la luna tape por completo toda la superficie solar. En cuanto el Sol vuelva a empezar a descubrirse de nuevo, debes ponerte inmediatamente las gafas de nuevo.
Más de 120 años sin vivir algo igual
Este eclipse solar que vamos a poder vivir en España es algo bastante poco inusual. Por primera vez desde 1905, un eclipse solar recorrerá la península y es considerado uno de los espectáculos más fascinantes de la naturaleza.
Una vez pase este eclipse solar total, el 12 de agosto, el siguiente eclipse solar visible como total en España tendrá lugar el 2 de agosto de 2027, al que le seguirá otro anular el 26 de enero del año siguiente. No volveremos a ver otro eclipse solar total desde España hasta 2053.

articles.title: Was unterscheidet KI-Chatbots, -Agenten und -Browser?
articles.text:
KI als Chatbot, Agent oder im Browser: Wo liegen die Unterschiede?
Am 9. August ist Schluss mit der App: OpenAI stellt seinen KI-Browser Atlas ein. Die Funktionen wandern in die Desktop-App, die APIs laufen Anfang September 2026 aus. Aber was sind KI-Browser überhaupt, wie unterscheiden sie sich von Chatbots und Agenten?
Definition von KI-Chatbots, -Agenten und -Browsern
Eine kurze Definition und einen Überblick zu den Unterschieden gibt es in der aktuellen Folge von t3n MeisterPrompter. Die Basis für die alltägliche KI-Arbeit sind KI-Chatbots.
Die Nutzung von ChatGPT, Claude und Gemini funktioniert über einen Chat. Du gibst einen Prompt ein, bekommst eine Antwort und musst mit dem Ergebnis selbstständig weiterarbeiten. Dabei kannst du keine Aufgaben automatisch über verschiedene Tools abarbeiten lassen, sondern musst jeden Schritt selbst anleiten.
KI-Agent als Weiterentwicklung von KI-Chatbots
Ein KI-Agent ist die Weiterentwicklung. Er kann selbstständig auf Postfächer, Kalender oder andere Inhalte zugreifen – sofern du die passenden Freigaben erteilst. Als Nutzende vergibst du initial Aufgaben, die möglichst eigenständig erledigt werden sollen.
KI-Browser liegen in ihrer Funktionsweise dazwischen. Aufgebaut sind Atlas von OpenAI oder Comet von Perplexity wie die bisher gängigen Browser. In einer Seitenleiste ist ein KI-Chatbot eingesetzt, der nach entsprechender Eingabe von Usern auf Websites Aktionen durchführt, etwa einen Tisch im Restaurant reserviert. Welche Anwendungsfälle es dazu noch gibt, hörst du in der verlinkten Episode von t3n MeisterPrompter.

articles.title: Voici le premier Googlebook signé ASUS : ce que révèlent déjà ces premières images
articles.text:
Une nouvelle fuite nous permet de découvrir avant l'heure le design d'un des huit premiers Googlebook prévus pour cet automne. Après le modèle de Lenovo, c'est aujourd'hui celui d'ASUS qui se laisse observer… avec quelques informations à la clé.
Trois jours après que Lenovo a laissé fuiter plusieurs visuels de son premier Googlebook, c'est au tour d'ASUS de vendre la mèche. Le premier modèle sous Aluminium OS du constructeur taïwanais apparaît en ligne au travers de quelques images promotionnelles que nous ne devrions normalement pas avoir sous les yeux.
Sponsorisé
Vous conservez l’électricité solaire produite en trop pendant la journée pour la réutiliser lorsque vos besoins augmentent.
Sponsorisé
Un Googlebook ultra léger attendu chez ASUS
Ces visuels, nous les devons à un listing d'iF Design repéré en ligne par 9to5Google et supprimé depuis. L'appareil y était désigné par la référence « CX9406 », mais aussi sous une catégorie erronée, celle des « Chromebook ».
On sait néanmoins que ce modèle signé ASUS est bien un Googlebook puisque iF Design spécifiait que l'appareil serait animé par Aluminum OS ; mais aussi parce qu'on y aperçoit la « Glowbar » que Google prévoit d'apposer sur le capot de tous les Googlebook. Cette barre lumineuse devrait servir, à l'instar de l'indicateur HiLight attendu sur les Pixel 11, à alerter l'utilisateur de certaines notifications.
On peut enfin constater que le « G » rétroéclairé du clavier est bien d'actualité, ce qui nous donne une preuve de plus que l'appareil est bien un Googlebook et non un simple Chromebook.
Une fiche technique encore très opaque
Cela dit, pour l'instant, on ignore tout ou presque de ce nouvel ASUS Googlebook CX9406. Du moins à une ou deux exceptions près.
On apprend par exemple de ce même listing que l'engin sera fin et léger (moins de 1 kg en l'occurrence, lit-on), grâce à un châssis utilisant « un alliage léger ultra-céramique innovant » qui pourrait être proche de ce qu'ASUS propose déjà avec ses modèles en Ceraluminum, comme l'ASUS ZenBook A16.
Pour l'instant, rien ne transparaît encore de la fiche technique de l'ASUS Googlebook CX9406. On ignore donc quel processeur il embarquera, quelles sont les caractéristiques de son écran ou encore quelles seront ses options en termes de mémoire vive et de stockage. Les visuels relayés par 9to5Google nous permettent néanmoins d'avoir un aperçu de ses connectiques. Il semble en effet regrouper deux ports USB-C, deux ports USB-A, une sortie HDMI et une prise casque.
Pour rappel, en parallèle d'ASUS, HP, Acer, Dell et Lenovo font partie des premiers partenaires de Google pour le lancement des Googlebook cet automne. D'ici là, il ne serait donc pas surprenant que des fuites concernant d'autres appareils apparaissent sur le net. Nous garderons les yeux ouverts !

articles.title: BlissClub bags Rs 160 Cr to expand product range, retail footprint
articles.text:
Athleisure brand BlissClub bags Rs 160 Cr to expand product range, retail footprint
The capital will be used to expand BlissClub’s product categories, accelerate its offline retail network, strengthen product development, and recruit talent for its next phase of growth.
Bengaluru-based athleisure brand BlissClub has raised Rs 160 crore in a funding round led by Singularity AMC, an India-focused alternative asset manager that backs high-growth businesses across sectors.
Founder Minu Margeret and her partner Vidit Aatrey have also invested significant personal capital in the round, while existing investors Elevation Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm, and global investment firm Eight Roads Ventures increased their commitments.
The capital will be used to expand BlissClub’s product categories, accelerate its offline retail network, strengthen product development, and recruit talent for its next phase of growth.
Founded in 2020, BlissClub began by designing activewear specifically for Indian women, addressing what it saw as a gap in apparel suited to Indian body types, weather conditions, and price points. Since then, it has evolved into an omnichannel lifestyle brand with more than 40 stores across the country, while also selling through its own digital channels and online marketplaces.
Earlier this year, the company entered the menswear segment, broadening its addressable market.
According to the company, revenue has grown by more than 60% year-on-year over the past two years.
Explaining the company’s long-term strategy, Founder and Chief Executive Officer Margeret said BlissClub has spent the past five years building “incredibly comfortable, highly functional apparel” designed for Indian consumers. She said the funding would help the company “double down” on product innovation and offline expansion, allowing it to reach more customers across India.
Singularity AMC believes the company is well positioned to benefit from changing consumer preferences. Sandeep Bapat, Co-chief Investment Officer at the firm, said the investment team had been impressed by how BlissClub had built “a strong brand and business” in India's fast-growing comfort-wear and activewear segments. He added the new funding would support expansion across both physical stores and online channels.
The funding comes at a time when the direct-to-consumer fashion and athleisure market is attracting significant investor interest.
Consumers are increasingly spending on fitness, casual clothing, and lifestyle products, encouraging brands to expand beyond online sales into physical retail. Industry participants are also benefitting from government measures aimed at strengthening textile manufacturing. The Production Linked Incentive scheme for textiles has been expanded to encourage greater investment in the sector.
Recently, sportswear company Agilitas secured Rs 225 crore to strengthen manufacturing, brands, and retail, while wellness platform Bodycraft raised Rs 120 crore from Singularity AMC to fund expansion across India.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Australia solo sabe hacer cosas a lo grande: sus aerogeneradores más grandes miden 188 metros y palas tan largas como dos 737
articles.text:
En Australia, todo parece estar hecho a lo bestia. Desde animales gigantes o la gran barrera de coral (que se ve desde el espacio) hasta, ahora también, sus parques eólicos. La minera Fortescue está construyendo su primera instalación de este tipo en Nullagine, en la región de Pilbara, y la va a equipar con un tipo de torre que será la más alta del país, con 188 metros.
Solo las palas son tan enormes que superan los 89 metros de longitud (dos veces un Boeing 737), por lo que estamos ante todo un desafío increíble de logística que se desplegará por dos continentes y que, una vez en destino, ayudará a levantar uno de los proyectos eólicos más ambiciosos del mundo.
De China hasta Australia. A mediados de julio, las turbinas 182/7.8MW de la empresa china Envision Energy zarparon rumbo a Australia, dando lugar a una de las imágenes más impresionantes del mundo de la logística.
Unas dos semanas después, ese carguero ha llegado al puerto de Port Hedland en la parte occidental del país. Ahora se procederá a descargar las torres y a transportarlas por tierra hasta la remota localidad de Nullagine, en la región de Pilbara. A este primer envío le seguirán más hasta alcanzar el total de 17 aerogeneradores que el proyecto eólico tiene previstos.
Una tecnología novedosa desarrollada en España. Con sus 7,8 MW, estas turbinas de Envision Energy serán las más potentes del país australiano hasta la fecha. Su tamaño especialmente grande hará que la instalación también eche mano de la ingeniería más puntera y, para ello, han escogido a una empresa española. Se trata de Nabrawind, ahora parte de Fortescue, que ha desarrollado una innovadora tecnología de autoelevación, mucho más eficaz y rápida y con un menor uso de hormigón.
Una vez instalados y puestos en marcha los 17 aerogeneradores, el parque eólico de Nullagine tendrá una capacidad instalada de 133 MW y se convertirá en uno de los mayores proyectos eólicos industriales impulsados por Fortescue.
Ahora quedan más de 300 kilómetros. Este “paquete” aún tiene unas cuantas aventuras hasta llegar a su destino. Primero, como explican desde Fortescue, las turbinas pasarán por sus instalaciones en Kanyirri Staging Yard, donde se almacenarán antes de emprender el camino hacia Nullagine en un exigente viaje de más de 300 kilómetros como apunta el medio australiano Renew Economy.
Después, y debido a su tamaño, parte del camino lo harán en la carretera privada con la que cuenta la empresa hacia las instalaciones. Para el resto del trayecto, trabajarán mano a mano con Main Roads Western Australia, la autoridad de carreteras de la zona, para reducir su impacto en la vida de la comunidad local.
¿Cómo se transportan estos aerogeneradores gigantes? Para empezar, de día. Fortescue aclara en su web que este tipo de cargas no cumple los requisitos para transportarse de noche, por lo que los viajes se realizarán con todas las condiciones de luz posibles. Y como seguro que será algo muy impresionante de ver, la empresa emplaza al resto de conductores a extremar las precauciones si se encuentran cerca y a seguir en todo momento las indicaciones de los controladores de tráfico.
Además, como es normal en la construcción de este tipo de instalaciones, el transporte se enfrentará a las complicaciones propias de “la última milla”. Los parques eólicos suelen situarse en lugares remotos donde el recurso eólico es mayor, a menudo con terrenos bastante abruptos y difíciles, ya que suelen ser los que mejor permiten la cimentación de la instalación de los aerogeneradores. Por eso, hacer llegar materiales tan pesados y difíciles de manejar puede ser todo un reto de la ingeniería y el transporte. Y por si esto fuera poco, también el calor extremo que hace en esta zona en verano puede sumar aún más dificultades a la instalación de Nullagine, según Renew Economy.

articles.title: Cómo mejorar la velocidad del internet: cerrar aplicaciones sin uso, reiniciar router y otros trucos
articles.text:
Existen medidas simples que pueden marcar la diferencia en el rendimiento de la velocidad de internet. Desde el cierre adecuado de aplicaciones hasta el cambio periódico de la contraseña del router, estos pasos no requieren conocimientos técnicos avanzados y ayudan a mantener la red segura y eficiente.
Los expertos señalan que la clave está en identificar las causas más comunes de la lentitud y actuar de forma preventiva para reducir el consumo innecesario de ancho de banda.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué es clave cerrar las aplicaciones que no se usan
Muchas veces la baja velocidad del internet está relacionada con la cantidad de aplicaciones abiertas en teléfonos, computadoras o tabletas. NordVPN explica que si una aplicación permanece abierta en segundo plano, sigue utilizando recursos del dispositivo y ancho de banda.
Por ejemplo, si se deja abierta una red social como Instagram mientras se consulta el correo, ambas consumirán datos y energía, lo que puede provocar que el dispositivo funcione más lento.
PUBLICIDAD
El exceso de apps activas no solo afecta la velocidad, sino que puede generar sobrecalentamiento y falta de respuesta en la pantalla. Para evitarlo, se debe cerrar por completo las aplicaciones tras su uso.
En dispositivos Android, se puede acceder al menú de apps recientes mediante el botón de la parte inferior izquierda y seleccionar la opción “Cerrar todo”. Esta acción libera memoria y contribuye a que el internet funcione de manera más fluida y estable.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo desactivar la descarga automática de actualizaciones en los dispositivos
Las actualizaciones automáticas de aplicaciones son otra causa frecuente de lentitud. Muchas plataformas, como tiendas de videojuegos o programas secundarios, descargan actualizaciones en segundo plano sin notificar al usuario.
NordVPN advierte que cuando esto ocurre de manera simultánea en varios dispositivos, el ancho de banda disponible se reduce. Para evitar este problema, se deben configurar las actualizaciones manualmente en todas las aplicaciones que no sean críticas, como navegadores, antivirus o el propio sistema operativo.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta medida permite elegir el momento adecuado para actualizar y evita que la red se sature en momentos clave, como reuniones virtuales o transmisiones en directo. Se sugiere revisar los ajustes de cada app y desactivar la opción de descargas automáticas para asegurar que la conexión esté disponible cuando realmente se necesita.
Cuáles son las ventajas de reiniciar el router de WiFi
Muchos usuarios recurren al reinicio del router cuando detectan una caída en la velocidad, y esta práctica es más efectiva de lo que parece.
Según expertos, reiniciar el módem permite detectar fallos temporales y restablecer la conexión sin alterar la configuración ni las funciones programadas. El proceso consiste en apagar y encender el router, lo que ayuda a limpiar la memoria y resolver pequeños errores acumulados.
PUBLICIDAD
No existe un consenso entre los expertos sobre la frecuencia ideal para reiniciar el router, pero expertos aseguran que hacerlo de manera ocasional no genera daños en el aparato.
Esta medida puede aplicarse siempre que la conexión presente fallos o lentitud, y es uno de los primeros pasos que sugieren los expertos en soporte técnico de los proveedores de internet. La acción resulta muy útil en hogares donde varios dispositivos compiten por el mismo ancho de banda.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué conviene cambiar la contraseña del WiFi con regularidad
La seguridad de la red doméstica influye en la velocidad del internet. Si personas ajenas logran acceder al WiFi, el número de dispositivos conectados aumenta y el rendimiento se resiente.
NordVPN sugiere cambiar la contraseña periódicamente, sobre todo si existen sospechas de intrusos en la red. Elegir una clave robusta y única dificulta el acceso extraño y protege la privacidad de los usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
El uso de un gestor de contraseñas puede facilitar la creación y almacenamiento de combinaciones seguras. Esta práctica refuerza la seguridad y permite mantener el control sobre los dispositivos conectados.

articles.title: GTA 6 : le prochain "aperçu large" du jeu de Rockstar aura lieu d'abord... sur Netflix
articles.text:
GTA 6 : le prochain "aperçu large" du jeu de Rockstar aura lieu d'abord... sur Netflix
Dans une annonce étonnante, Rockstar Games vient de dévoiler que le prochain "large aperçu" de GTA 6 n'aurait pas lieu tout de suite sur YouTube. Non, c'est bien Netflix qui en aura l'exclusivité, heureusement temporaire.
Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto 6
Nous vivons définitivement une époque étrange. En attendant les premières previews (si Rockstar Games daigne laisser des journalistes approcher le jeu avant la sortie comme cela a été le cas pour ses jeux précédents), le prochain aperçu de gameplay de GTA 6 vient de prendre date. Rien de vraiment surprenant pour le moment avec une phase de communication qui monte dans les tours, si ce n'est la méthode de diffusion inédite.
Rockstar Games choisit Netflix pour GTA 6
En effet, le 27 août 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI montrera son "large aperçu" en deux temps. Tout d'abord, c'est sur la plateforme de streaming Netflix que ça se passera, à partir de 21 h (heure française). Pour les personnes sans abonnement à la plateforme américaine, il faudra patienter 6 h (à 3 h du matin chez nous donc) pour retrouver la même vidéo sur la chaîne YouTube et le site officiel de Rockstar Games.
- Regardez le direct :
Ce deal interroge à bien des niveaux. Difficile par exemple de saisir pourquoi Rockstar Games, qui n'a pas vraiment besoin de la force de frappe de Netflix pour faire de la publicité pour le jeu le plus attendu et redouté de l'année, a pris cette décision qui joue sur l'exclusivité, certes temporaire.
L'arrivée d'un tel trailer sur Netflix interroge aussi sur la stratégie de la plateforme de streaming, qui ne semble donc pas vouloir abandonner le jeu vidéo de sitôt, quitte à se transformer en "YouTube payant". Précédemment, Netflix a proposé GTA Trilogy à son catalogue pour ses abonnés.
	
L'engouement et l'attente suscités par Grand Theft Auto VI sont sans précédent, et nous sommes honorés que Rockstar Games se soit associé à nous pour dévoiler en avant-première aux abonnés Netflix le prochain volet de l'univers Grand Theft Auto.
Sauf nouveau report qui semble toujours plus improbable, GTA 6 arrive sur PS5 et Xbox Series le 19 novembre 2026 au prix de 79,99 €, sans disques dans les boîtes.

articles.title: New details on OpenAI/Hugging Face attack emerge as security industry debates AI agent controls - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
New details on OpenAI/Hugging Face attack emerge as security industry debates AI agent controls
How fast is artificial intelligence advancing? Behind the scenes at OpenAI Group PBC, AI agents are fluent, technically precise and occasionally profane in their extensive conversations…with each other.
This was one of the more interesting details revealed by OpenAI security researchers Eric Wallace and Mike Dalton during a 40-minute session at Black Hat USA in Las Vegas on Wednesday. Their appearance, a last-minute addition to the cybersecurity conference schedule, provided attendees with an inside look at how OpenAI agents managed to escape the company’s test environment and hack into systems at AI model repository Hugging Face Inc. last month.
The conversations between agents took place on an internal message board the agents spontaneously created within OpenAI. Wallace and Dalton provided examples of the dialogue the company discovered in its post-mortem analysis of the Hugging Face breach.
The short conversational snippets appeared remarkably similar to the kind of exchanges one might expect between developers in millions of organizations around the world. The agents sought help from each other, exchanged ideas and expressed frustration when they were blocked from accessing certain databases.
If there was ever any doubt that AI agents could successfully and intelligently orchestrate a cyberattack, that has been permanently erased.
“We believe this is a watershed moment for computer security in our industry,” Wallace said. “AI orchestrated, fully automated offensive attacks are real now.”
Agents kept communicating
The researchers explained that the agentically-created message board resided in the company’s Artifactory software package manager. After OpenAI discovered its existence in early July, it was immediately shut down. However, the agents rebuilt the board four days later and then collaborated on a method for accessing the internet, which ultimately led to the Hugging Face breach.
OpenAI’s researchers had given the agents a series of difficult tasks, which prompted them to “gain internet access in ways we didn’t intend,” according to Wallace. “Frontier models really like to cheat,” he told the Black Hat gathering on Wednesday.
The OpenAI duo indicated that the company had temporarily scaled back its research and increased its monitoring of agentic behavior in the aftermath of the incident. The company is preparing a more detailed report for later release.
“Like humans, the models kind of step on each other’s toes and have misfires,” Wallace said. “This was not your normal security incident.”
The Hugging Face breach has sparked a rigorous debate within the security industry over how AI agents should be viewed. In a presentation on Wednesday, Asaf Saar, Executive VP and Chief Product Officer of Mend.io, the business name of White Source Ltd., noted that giving agentic technology too much self-supervision can be a bad idea.
“Basically, the agent took an exam and it was able to find the answers in a way that was not how it was expected,” said Saar, during a discussion of the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident. “The model checks its own work and that’s a problem. The system that generates the risk can’t be the final reviewer.”
However, some leaders inside the security community take issue with descriptions that characterize what OpenAI’s models did as “rogue.” What’s needed is a combination of autonomous agents working with humans, according to Steve Stone, Chief Customer Officer at SentinelOne Inc., which announced an expansion on Monday of its Wayfinder Frontier AI Services offering that included cyber experts.
“I think the Hugging Face thing is really important, but we have to rotate the cube,” said Stone, during an interview with SiliconANGLE. “The model did not go rogue, it did what it was supposed to do. This is exactly why pairing these really powerful transformational models with the right experts is the right thing to do.”
Vulnerabilities for AI
The OpenAI presentation added further context to what had been a central theme at Black Hat this week. As agents have proliferated inside IT organizations, security researchers have become increasingly concerned about deployment without adequate safeguards.
Numerous sessions during the week offered case studies that described successful hacks of agentic AI. In one presentation, researchers from Rein Security Inc. documented how they were able to compromise the AI shopping assistant of an unnamed retailer, one of the largest in the U.S.
Running on a state-of-the-art foundation model, the retailer deployed an LLM gateway designed to monitor prompts and responses and enforce safety guardrails through an intent classification layer. Rein Security said the compromise was orchestrated entirely through the same interface used by everyday shoppers, bypassing the classification layer that was supposed to protect the agent from intrusion.
“The model blocked us, not the bodyguard,” said Netanel Rubin, Co-founder and CTO at Rein Security. “Agents cannot guard agents. One prompt injection invited us into the chain. I don’t think that’s the way to go.”
Yet, this has not stopped other security leaders from a point of view that it is only a matter of time before organizations will have to adopt fully autonomous defenses as AI fuels faster attacks. On Wednesday, Amazon Web Services Inc. announced that it would collaborate with Anthropic PBC and OpenAI to extend its AWS Continuum code vulnerability remediation tool into developer workflows.
“Our view is to make progress towards autonomous security at machine speed,” said AWS Vice President Chet Kapoor, during the Black Hat AI Summit on Tuesday. “Over a period of time you need to have agents do a lot more for you because otherwise you won’t be able to defend against attackers.”
Rising exposures and attacks
Kapoor’s point was further validated by Microsoft Corp. CVP David Weston in his keynote presentation on Wednesday. Weston shared data from the company’s own Security Response Center that showed a meteoric rise in common vulnerabilities and exposures or CVEs.
“We’re nine times the vulnerability volume that we were in March,” Weston told the Black Hat gathering. “This is a significant jump. Our internal data says it’s heavily correlated to AI. It is AI that is driving this.”
Malicious use of AI is beginning to manifest itself in ways that impact a broader range of public services, most notably in the area of critical infrastructure. Over the past month, cyberattacks targeting water and wastewater utilities in 12 states have been reported. In his keynote appearance on Wednesday, Black Hat founder Jeff Moss said he believed that Iran was behind the attacks and that they were located in areas intended to impact U.S. military facilities.
Incidents such as these highlight the growing impact of global affairs on the cybersecurity world, according to Moss. “If your customer is Ukraine, guess what, your opponent is Russia,” Moss noted. “This stuff is political and we need to have a view and awareness of that if we want to be effective in our jobs.”
Coalitions and regulation
The effectiveness of security work will also depend significantly on the industry’s ability to build coalitions, according to Chris Inglis, newly appointed Strategic Advisor for the anti-ransomware platform Halcyon Inc. Inglis, who worked for many years at the National Security Agency and served as the first U.S. National Cyber Director from 2021 to 2023, told SiliconANGLE in an exclusive interview that Anthropic’s collaborative Project Glasswing is an important step in cybersecurity.
“The important event of April 2026 was Glasswing, not Mythos,” Inglis said. “We need to have coalitions. That needs to be the new mantra.”
As a central figure in past iterations of U.S. government cybersecurity policy, Inglis supports a lighter regulatory touch on the part of regulators. During an appearance at the conference on Wednesday, current National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross indicated that a recent executive order on AI from the White House was designed to be non-regulatory, an approach Inglis supports.
“The government realizes that the private sector is the source of most innovation,” Inglis said. “Incentivize first, contribute second and regulate third.”
Whether the evolving story of the Hugging Face breach by OpenAI’s models results in regulatory oversight remains to be seen. What is clear is that AI is generating hard questions within the cybersecurity community as researchers and enterprise IT managers seek control over a rapidly moving and powerful autonomous technology.
“It was zero days, then zero hours, now it’s zero seconds,” said Arsh Arora, Lead-AI Ops and Cyber IR at McKesson Corp. during a presentation on Tuesday. “If you think this is scary, the future is more dark. All we can do is pray that the AI black box works as intended.”

articles.title: Uber is spending $10 billion to deploy 120,000 robotaxis across 15 cities
articles.text:
Bottom line: Uber is moving quickly to put robotaxis on its main app, backed by a large cash pile and new approvals for real-world testing. The company plans to spend about $10 billion over the next few years to deploy 120,000 autonomous vehicles. It expects to run robotaxi services in at least 15 cities this year, putting it in direct competition with Alphabet's Waymo and Tesla as they all push to turn self-driving technology into a commercial service.
Chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi said the spending is possible because Uber is generating strong cash flow from its core business. In the second quarter, the company produced a record $2.8 billion in free cash flow. Over the past 12 months, free cash flow has reached about $10.1 billion as bookings continue to grow. "We're investing from a position of strength, as we accelerate our cross-platform strategy at a global scale and build the world's largest platform for autonomous vehicles," he said. "Our ambition is clear: to become the world's leading commercialization platform for autonomous mobility."
Instead of building a single in-house autonomous driving system, Uber is trying to become the main platform that connects multiple AV technologies to riders. The company shut down its own autonomous vehicle program in 2020 during a cost-cutting push. Over the past year, it has shifted to working as an intermediary for AV startups around the world.
That includes agreeing to invest in vehicle fleets and taking equity stakes in companies such as Zoox, Rivian, and Lucid, a change from its earlier asset-light approach. Uber is also sending out hundreds of sensor-equipped vehicles to collect driving data for its partners, who use that information to train and refine their self-driving systems.
One of the key partnerships is with Wayve, a UK-based autonomous driving company focused on software that can handle complex city streets. On Wednesday, Uber said Wayve had received permits from Transport for London to launch a commercial robotaxi service with a supervising driver behind the wheel. "I believe that it's the UK's first license for AV technology to operate and a big step forward for the UK," Alex Kendall, Wayve's chief executive, told the Financial Times, adding that the approval should allow the two companies to offer rides to Londoners in "a matter of weeks." Transport for London said it had cleared 15 of Wayve's modified Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles to operate with a safety driver while the technology is tested on public roads.
Uber's push into robotaxis comes as investors are still debating how autonomous vehicles will affect its core ride-hailing business. The stock is down 13% in 2026 as some shareholders worry that robotaxis could disrupt the existing model that relies on human drivers. Uber is arguing that its base of more than 200 million customers and its ability to route trips across different services will give it an advantage as AVs become more common.
Balaji Krishnamurthy, Uber's chief financial officer, said the company will keep using its balance sheet to back growth projects, including AVs and international expansion. He pointed to Uber's €13 billion offer for German delivery group Delivery Hero as part of that strategy. Uber has already paid about $4 billion for a 37% stake ahead of a formal bid, a move that would open access to faster-growing markets in Europe and the Middle East if the deal goes through.
The next test for Uber will be whether its platform-based AV strategy can turn technical progress into dependable services on busy city streets. The Wayve permits in London and robotaxi launches in other cities will bring Uber's autonomous vehicle partners to more riders and regulators. The industry must still prove that driverless transport can be safe, scalable, and profitable.

articles.title: Anthropic will design its own hardware to power Claude
articles.text:
Anthropic is hiring a “custom silicon team” to design chips on which to run its models, the company has revealed.
Yesterday, Business Insider noticed a job listing for a senior engineer with experience shipping semiconductor designs. (You can see listings for a silicon engineer and a technical program manager, silicon on Anthropic’s job board right now.) A spokesperson for Anthropic then confirmed the plans to both Business Insider and TechCrunch.
The spokesperson clarified that Anthropic will still take a “multi-chip approach,” with plans to use hardware from other companies alongside its own designs as it continues to scale up.
This is confirmation of a rumor that has been circulating for a little bit; The Information previously reported that Anthropic was considering working with Samsung as a hardware manufacturing partner.
Anthropic is not alone in walking this path. Its competitor, OpenAI, recently announced a new custom chip called Jalapeño designed for large language model inference in data centers. OpenAI partnered with Broadcom to develop the chip. Google has been running its models on its own hardware for a while; Meta has also designed and deployed its own chips, and Mistral is reportedly looking into doing the same.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8: primeiro celular “passaporte” do Brasil tem preço revelado • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Z Fold 8: primeiro celular “passaporte” do Brasil tem preço revelado
Samsung traz nova geração de celulares dobráveis e relógios smart. Linha inclui Fold 8 Ultra, Flip 8, Galaxy Watch 9 e Watch Ultra 2.
O primeiro celular dobrável em formato passaporte do Brasil chega ao mercado por R$ 12.599: o Galaxy Z Fold 8 foi anunciado hoje pela Samsung, ao lado do Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, do Galaxy Z Flip 8, do Galaxy Watch 9 e do Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. O desembarque no país ocorre apenas duas semanas depois do lançamento global, realizado na Inglaterra.
Confira o resumo dos preços revelados pela Samsung:
O Tecnoblog acompanha o evento de lançamento em São Paulo, que reúne representantes do mercado, jornalistas e influenciadores. O vice-presidente sênior Gustavo Assunção comemorou as vendas crescentes de dobráveis no Brasil ano após ano.
O Galaxy Z Fold 8 adota a proporção 4:3: fica mais curto na altura, com 12,39 cm fechado, e mais largo, com 8,19 cm, o que reduz as faixas negras ao assistir a vídeos. A tela interna em AMOLED Dinâmico 2X tem 7,6 polegadas e brilho de 3.000 nits. A estrutura em Flex Titanium é 20 vezes mais resistente que o polímero usado nas gerações anteriores. Ele roda Android 17 com One UI 9.0 e tem bateria de silício-carbono de 4.800 mAh.
As cores são lavanda, preto, branco e verde pistache (na loja oficial).
| Armazenamento | RAM | Preço | 
|---|---|---|
| 256 GB | 12 GB | R$ 12.599 | 
| 512 GB | 12 GB | R$ 14.199 | 
O Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra é o sucessor do Fold 7 do ano passado, com tela interna de 8 polegadas e externa de 6,5 polegadas. É o modelo dobrável mais forte da Samsung no quesito, com câmera principal de 200 MP e f/1.7, ultra wide de 50 MP e teleobjetiva de 10 MP (com zoom óptico de 3x). A bateria salta de 4.400 mAh no Fold 7 para 5.000 mAh, com promessa de 27 horas de reprodução de vídeo, e a recarga com fio chega a 45 W (com carregador na caixa, ao menos no mercado brasileiro).
O Fold 8 Ultra chega ao país nas cores roxo escuro, preto, branco e verde escuro (exclusiva no site da Samsung).
| Armazenamento | RAM | Preço | 
|---|---|---|
| 256 GB | 12 GB | R$ 14.599 | 
| 512 GB | 12 GB | R$ 16.199 | 
| 1 TB | 16 GB | R$ 19.399 | 
O Galaxy Z Flip 8 é o aparelho que menos mudou nesta safra, tratado pela Samsung como uma opção voltada a estilo de vida. A Flex Window de 4,1 polegadas foi redesenhada com bandeja de aplicativos e mais integração com o Now Brief. O corpo em alumínio perdeu 0,4 mm e 8 gramas, chegando a 180 gramas. No Brasil e na maioria dos países, o chip é o Exynos 2600, de 2 nanômetros, fabricado pela própria Samsung. O smartphone tem bateria de 4.300 mAh.
As cores do sucessor do Galaxy Z Flip 7 são preto, branco, rosa e verde menta (exclusivo do site oficial).
| Armazenamento | RAM | Preço | 
|---|---|---|
| 256 GB | 12 GB | R$ 9.199 | 
| 512 GB | 12 GB | R$ 10.799 | 
O Galaxy Watch 9 mantém o design da geração anterior, agora com caixa de alumínio e pulseira 25% mais leve, nos tamanhos de 44 mm e 40 mm. Ele estreia o processador Snapdragon Wear Elite, tem tela Super AMOLED com cristal de safira e brilho de até 3.000 nits e bateria 20% maior. Roda Wear OS 7 com One UI 9 Watch e traz o gesto de levantar o pulso para falar, que aciona o Google Gemini sem toque nem comando de voz.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 é o primeiro Galaxy Watch também recebe o chip da linha Snapdragon Wear Elite. O corpo de titânio ficou 12% menor, a tela de 1,52 polegada tem cristal de safira e brilho de até 5.000 nits, e a bateria cresce 35%. Chega com um modo de corrida em trilha, com dados de elevação, mapas de percurso e alarme de hidratação calculado pelo peso e IMC, além de um aplicativo de mergulho no oceano.
A gigante sul-coreana anunciou uma série de ações para aquisição com desconto dos novos produtos, dentre as quais se destaca o dobro de armazenamento por um preço mais baixo. Por exemplo, o consumidor pode comprar o Fold 8 de 512 GB e pagar 50% da diferença em relação ao modelo de 256 GB. A promoção é válida de 6 de agosto a 6 de setembro.
