articles.title: ASUS DisplayWidget Center Update Introduces AI Agent-Ready Controls
articles.text:
Thursday, August 6th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
ASUS DisplayWidget Center Update Introduces AI Agent-Ready Controls
ASUS today announced a major update to the ASUS DisplayWidget Center monitor management software, providing users with a more intuitive way to control compatible ASUS and ROG displays. This latest release adds AI-based automation, deeper personalization with App Tweaker and OLED Care, and broader device integration—all while keeping monitor management simple with a mouse or keyboard instead of physical monitor buttons. Available as a free download from the ASUS website, DisplayWidget Center supports Windows 11 or later and macOS on compatible devices. Additional improvements include a firmware update notification feature and one-key product registration that automatically fills in the device serial number. 
AI agent-ready display control
This latest update to DisplayWidget Center moves it into the AI agent era. With ASUS Display Control Command Line Interface (CLI) and Agent Skill installed, compatible AI agents can adjust monitor settings through natural-language requests. Users can manage brightness, color mode, color temperature, and OLED Anti-Flicker without having to manually navigate through menus.A single command can configure multiple monitors settings simultaneously on compatible ASUS monitors. For competitive gamers, the agent can draw on past usage habits to recommend a higher refresh rate, FPS, and OLED Anti-Flicker, along with the user's preferred brightness setting.
Users can also ask the agent to check their calendar and automatically switch profiles to match the time of day: a morning profile with high brightness, 6500K color temperature, and Blue Light Filter off can give way to an evening profile with lower brightness, 4000K color temperature, and a higher Blue Light Filter setting for more comfortable viewing before bed.The CLI executes monitor-control commands locally on the workstation, while the agent translates user intent into a series of supported actions. In IT environments, the CLI can also be deployed through endpoint-management platforms such as Microsoft Intune to help adjust various settings across multiple displays.
New AI-powered features
DisplayWidget Center also introduces two additional AI-powered features. AI Visual, available on compatible ROG and TUF Gaming monitors, reads on-screen content in real time and automatically applies the most suitable visual mode. AI Assistant supports both text and voice input, letting users adjust display settings, access product FAQs, and get help with monitor functions through a convenient interface.
Personalized viewing experiences through App Tweaker and OLED Care
For convenience, DisplayWidget Center includes App Tweaker and OLED Care. The updated App Tweaker feature helps users create personalized display experiences for each application. It automatically switches display settings based on the app currently in use, allowing users to create unique profiles with customized image and color settings. This reduces the need for manual adjustment and creates smoother transitions between tasks.
At present, additional OLED Care functions include Boundary Detection, Outer Dimming Control, Global Dimming Control, and Pixel Cleaning. Together, these features help reduce image retention risk and support long-term panel care. Users can manage these settings, along with pixel-cleaning activation and reminders, directly in DisplayWidget Center.
Tailored for gaming, creative tasks, and daily productivity
This latest update to DisplayWidget Center also adds features designed around different display use cases, from gaming and content creation to business and daily computing. Gamers can launch GamePlus directly from DisplayWidget Center and call up the OSD menu with a keyboard hotkey or via a supported controller, instead of relying on monitor buttons.
For creators, ColorSync helps keep color settings consistent across multiple identical displays, while MacBook Brightness Control lets compatible macOS users adjust monitor brightness with familiar laptop keys, once enabled through macOS accessibility settings. ZenScreen users also benefit from Auto Rotation, which senses monitor orientation and switches automatically between portrait and landscape.
For business and daily users, new Eye Care tools such as Blue Light Filter, Color Augmentation, and Rest Reminder help make extended screen time more comfortable. Multi-screen management and keyboard hotkeys also support more efficient everyday workflows.
End-to-end coverage across the ASUS display ecosystem
DisplayWidget Center now extends beyond monitor settings. Users can fine-tune virtual display settings and spatial screen layouts on ROG XREAL R1 Gaming AR Glasses, or manage function keys and launch color calibration on the ProArt CaliContrO MCA02 calibrator—all from the same software. This wider integration helps make DisplayWidget Center a more unified control center across the ASUS display ecosystem.

articles.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword's Sekiro-style combat makes for a spectacular action-packed experience that I'm pumped to spend more time with
articles.text:
I spent three hours with Onimusha: Way of the Sword — and its spectacular sword action has me more convinced than ever that Capcom can’t miss
Simply magnificent
A new entry in Capcom's cult-classic Onimusha franchise has been a long time coming, and there was no better time than now for its resurgence, during the developer's largely successful RE Engine era.
So far, it seems that the resurgence will pay off extremely well: I spent three hours with the upcoming demon-hunting slasher, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and I came away absolutely amazed by just how well Capcom has taken the formula from previous entries and modernized it brilliantly.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword absolutely shines within every combat encounter, with its weighty, methodical, and stylish sword clashes. It very much reminds me of From Software's Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, which might sound concerning for those who aren't fans of excessively hard souls games.
You can throw that thought out, though: Way of the Sword is a challenging but very accessible and enjoyable experience, with a variety of boss battles that will test your mettle.
However, with enough practice via boss rematches or against standard enemies in training arenas, similar to previous entries, you'll become accustomed to its combat in no time.
Poised to be the best yet
Rasho-gan's boss battle was intense; a clash with one of the best-designed demons in the game I saw. The opening cutscene was creepy, and it quickly became apparent how cruel the demons are. (Video credit: Capcom)
Onimusha: Way of the Sword is poised to be the best entry in the franchise, without a doubt. It's fair to say that potential acclaim is heavily carried by Capcom's magical RE Engine, responsible for major hits like Resident Evil 4 (2023), Resident Evil Requiem, Monster Hunter World, and other titles in both franchises for almost a decade.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Visuals are at their best in Onimusha: Way of the Sword. Character models, environment details, and the art style all lend to the immersive samurai demon-hunting experience Capcom is trying to deliver — but it's not just about visuals.
I spoke highly of the animations during combat in my coverage of the public demo. After the three-hour preview, I'm convinced that Onimusha: Way of the Sword will set a new standard for sword clashes and how detailed they are.
The 'Issen' technique (evident in the video above) was a core aspect of combat in previous titles and is back and better than ever. It allows players to perform a deadly counterattack right before an enemy attack, and it was a maneuver I spent plenty of time practicing during the preview.
It's not easy to pull off, as it requires very precise timing, but it comes in clutch when outnumbered or facing off against the three tough bosses during my preview (which I won't spoil), by doing plenty of stagger damage. Once I unlocked Chain Issen, I could take out multiple enemies in rapid fashion — and the new flashy and stylish animation makes it so much more satisfying.
Byakue is the hardest boss I've come across in Way of the Sword so far, with constant erratic and unpredictable movements. You've got to have your guard up at all times against this one. (Video credit: Capcom)
My mention of stagger damage is important because Onimusha: Way of the Sword's combat, especially during boss battles where parries are pivotal, reminds me very much of From Software's Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Again, this isn't a souls-like, so don't expect much similarity to Sekiro elsewhere, and thankfully, Way of the Sword is much more forgiving for mistimed parries.
However, the sword clashes with bosses like Byakue are incredibly well designed, with audio and visuals that are fantastically gripping, creating the same back-and-forth flow that worked so well in Sekiro.
The great thing is that it seems as though Capcom has used Sekiro as inspiration for combat and built on it, adding extra details like a brief slowdown and zoom when a perfect parry is performed, creating openings for further attacks.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword is also not heavily reliant on parries in normal enemy encounters or boss battles, thanks to the presence of perfect dodges and Issen. Those three elements combined make for a pleasant experience — and outside of the practice arena, there are side quests you can take on for non-player characters (NPCs) with semi-open hubs (similar to Resident Evil 4's boat segment) to explore.
Wind-Whipper is a secondary weapon, but it's certainly a room clearer. It saved me numerous times when encountering more formidable foes while travelling across one of the game's semi-open hubs. (Video credit: Capcom)
Perhaps the only worry I do have is that Way of the Sword seemingly won't have any other primary weapons for Miyamoto Musashi, the main protagonist, to wield. There are indeed secondary weapons, but they are seemingly limited to Oni Armaments, which can only be used when their meters are filled when engaging in duels.
Don't get me wrong, those secondary weapons like the Two Celestials (dual blades) and the Wind-Whipper spear-like weapon I unlocked in my three-hour run are great — but I'm hoping there are enough skills for Musashi's katana to keep gameplay fresh through the game's runtime.
Either way, I'm incredibly excited for Onimusha: Way of the Sword's launch on September 4, 2026, releasing on PS5, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC — and I'm sure it will be yet another massive hit.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.

articles.title: Hackers caught hijacking this Chinese Windows VPN's installers to spread malware
articles.text:
Hackers caught hijacking this Chinese Windows VPN's installers to spread malware
QuickFox Windows installers found to be secretly dropping a persistent backdoor to spy on specific business and crypto users
- Fortinet experts found malicious code in QuickFox VPN's Windows installer
- The attack actively avoided personal gaming computers
- QuickFox has since removed the malicious components from version 3.59.6
Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a severe supply chain attack targeting QuickFox, a popular Chinese Windows VPN application.
According to a new report from Fortinet’s FortiGuard Labs, attackers trojanized the software's installers for over a year to quietly deploy malicious backdoor implants onto users' machines.
As Fortinet's experts explain, QuickFox "is a VPN proxy and game accelerator typically employed by Chinese users to speed up access to Chinese-based resources, often to improve video game user experience."
However, experts found that malicious actors altered the application's underlying code to deliver a highly targeted malware campaign. The threat actors modified an HTML file within the app's installer to automatically download and execute malicious JavaScript.
To avoid raising suspicion, this malicious code was pulled from a fake domain intentionally registered to mimic QuickFox’s legitimate infrastructure. Fortinet notes that the campaign had been active since at least August 2025, with QuickFox removing the malicious code with version 3.59.6.
TechRadar has not independently verified Fortinet's findings, but we have reached out to QuickFox for comment and will update this article if we receive a reply.
A highly targeted backdoor
The malware didn't infect everyone who downloaded the compromised VPN software. Instead, it used clever guardrails to filter out standard consumers.
If the malicious script detected Steam — the popular distribution service for online games — running on the victim's device, it immediately stopped the infection process to avoid personal gaming computers.
However, if it found tools used by developers, IT administrators, or cryptocurrency users, such as Visual Studio Code, Telegram, or various cryptocurrency wallets, it proceeded with the attack. This behavior suggests the hackers were explicitly hunting for high-value corporate environments and professionals rather than casual gamers.
When a target was deemed suitable, the script abused a legitimate Microsoft utility to secretly install the FDMTP implant and inject the malware. This persistent backdoor allowed attackers to collect sensitive system information, including IP addresses, active processes, MAC addresses, and usernames.
Because FDMTP is highly modular, it also enabled the hackers to remotely download and execute additional malicious plugins, granting them long-term access to compromised machines.
While macOS builds contained the modified file, the infection process only executed on Windows endpoints. Android and iOS apps were completely unaffected.
How to stay safe
While Fortinet researchers have not confidently attributed the attack to a specific group, they noted significant technical crossovers with Twill Typhoon, a known threat actor.
The good news is that the threat now appears to be contained. According to the cybersecurity firm, "QuickFox has removed the described malicious components from their Windows installer from v3.59.6," following responsible disclosure.
If you have used QuickFox on a Windows machine over the last year, you should immediately update to the latest version directly from the vendor and run a full antivirus scan on your system.
Organizations are also advised to check their networks for any unusual activity or unrecognized file transfers originating from QuickFox installations.

With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.

articles.title: $1 billion of iPhone 18 Pro chips 'on the shelves awaiting packaging' due to DRAM shortages — memory shortages reportedly put a wrinkle in Apple's launch plans
articles.text:
$1 billion of iPhone 18 Pro chips 'on the shelves awaiting packaging' due to DRAM shortages — memory shortages reportedly put a wrinkle in Apple's launch plans
Apple has the wafers ready to go. It's just waiting on DRAM like everyone else.
Apple reportedly has around $1 billion in "processor wafers on the shelves awaiting packaging" amid ongoing memory shortages, putting pressure on the firm as it nears the launch of the iPhone 18. Tim Culpan of Culpium says Apple is "scrambling" for memory supply ahead of release, working with suppliers to get memory ready so it can finish packaging the A20 Pro and C2 chips that are reportedly inside the iPhone 18 lineup.
It's an interesting peek behind the curtain of the current supply chain limitations, which reach beyond simply DRAM chips. With fully-integrated SoCs across both desktop and mobile, Apple is uniquely vulnerable to supply chain limitations, not only in DRAM supply, but also in packaging capacity to bring together DRAM chips with processor wafers.
According to Culpan, Apple primarily sources DRAM from Micron, with smaller engagements from SK Hynix and Samsung. Micron (along with the other major memory players) has reportedly sold capacity for DRAM and HBM through 2027. A flurry of long-term agreements (LTAs) have cropped up over the past several months, guaranteeing supply to certain companies for several years.
The A20 Pro is the first chip to use TSMC's N2 process, and it has been progressing well, with TSMC reportedly sitting on around $1 billion worth of Apple wafers awaiting packaging with DRAM. Packaging happens with TSMC's new Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) process, according to Culpan, which is similar to the CoWoS packaging but for mobile parts.
Culpan reports that "Apple and its assemblers remain confident that they can meet initial demand," but DRAM shortages could put pressure on shipments past the initial launch. Apple reportedly plans to ship around 200 million iPhone 18 units across the lineup throughout the device's lifespan. The iPhone 17 range saw record shipments last year, surpassing 245 million devices shipped in 2025.
Apple is one of several companies reportedly looking to alternative suppliers for DRAM, namely China's CXMT. The Chinese memory supplier has become a hot topic in the halls of the U.S. government over the past several weeks, with Apple reportedly lobbying for clearance as the government weighs the option to ban CXMT.

articles.title: Vogue just gave another nod of approval to the tech world | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Vogue World is coming to San Francisco next year — perhaps another indication that tech billionaires have become leaders in the fashion zeitgeist.
Of course, the announcement of the enormous fashion/art/music event doesn’t say that. Instead, Anna Wintour wrote that Vogue believes in celebrating cities and “San Francisco is a city like none other.”
“It’s a place of diverse communities living side by side, a place that loves the arts, loves creativity, and isn’t afraid of change.” She also noted the city’s history of rebelliousness and innovation.
“I love that San Francisco has always stood up for values and the things it believes in,” Wintour wrote. “Vogue World will support San Francisco’s creative minds and strengthen the entire ecosystem — and it will offer another opportunity to show San Francisco is on the rise.”
There were rumors that Vogue World would head to San Francisco after Winter was seen having meetings with the city’s mayor, Daniel Lurie.
Plus, in the past year, Wintour has cozied up to the most powerful names in tech, culminating in this year’s Met Gala, which saw Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sanchez, serve as lead sponsors for the event. Google’s Sergey Brin and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg were also spotted at the event (the latter’s first, that is). In fact, OpenAI bought a table, as did Meta and Snap (for $350,000 a pop). It’s true that TikTok, Apple, and Instagram previously sponsored the event, but the presence of the tech crowd was so considerable that the Met Gala this year was dubbed the “tech gala” in some places.
Last year, Vogue put Lauren Sanchez on the cover of the magazine after her wedding to the Amazon founder. To the fashion world, this was Wintour’s stamp of approval — not just for Sanchez’s ascent into the fashion world, but that tech and its leaders were worthy of cultural recognition.
Though Bezos and Sanchez reportedly live in Florida (and Amazon is, of course, headquartered in the Seattle area), there is no city more associated with tech than San Francisco. By locating Vogue World there, this is another indication of Wintour’s approval.
Vogue, as a media publication, is always following the money, and as a cultural bible, is always looking for ways to stay relevant. Turning toward the worldwide headquarters of AI, good or bad, is brilliant for business (and Wintour is nothing if not brilliant).
But Vogue World was previously held in New York, London, Paris, and this year, Milan. Maybe because I live in an East Coast bubble, but I’ve not heard anyone in recent years refer to San Francisco as a beacon of style to rank alongside these other cities.
While the city has a reputation as the land of the free-spirited bohemian, tech and its workers have a reputation for hoodies, Patagonia vests, and expensive athletic shoes, if they even dress up that much.
For instance, billionaire Alexandr Wang, who is now running Meta’s all-important Superintelligence Labs, just did an interview with Y Combinator’s Garry Tan in front of a packed stadium wearing a faded Nintendo T-shirt and what looked like a pair of Crocs. Comfy? Yes. High fashion? Decidedly no.
But maybe that’s changing. Wang’s boss, Mark Zuckerberg, who once always appeared in a plain gray T-shirt and jeans, has made efforts in recent years to become more fashionable. Zuck and his wife Priscilla Chan were spotted front row at a Prada show this season. The new campaign for Meta Glasses has a slew of celeb ambassadors and looks like it could be a Saint Laurent or Balenciaga ad.
OpenAI and Palantir have recently released merch collabs, playing on the minimalist style of tech workers (the merch line of the latter, I would argue, looks inspired by Virgil Abloh’s Off-White).
I concede that creatively there is much to be done with the understated, Northern California style. Surrounded by beautiful nature and cooler temperatures, plenty of fashion designers could be motivated by San Francisco’s tech industry. I look forward to seeing Claude-inspired terra cotta-colored gowns and Vogue-emblazoned quarter-zips soon.

articles.title: Nashville attempts to block controversial data center near zoo with eminent domain — city could force developer to sell the land for public use, rather than $700 million installation
articles.text:
Nashville attempts to block controversial data center near zoo with eminent domain — city could force developer to sell the land for public use, rather than $700 million installation
One way to stop a data center project is to buy the land that it will sit on.
The Nashville Metro Council just gave the go-signal to Mayor Freddie O’Connell's plan to use eminent domain to block a planned 23-acre data center campus sitting right beside the Nashville Zoo at Grassmere. According to real estate news platform CoStar, the city council approved the measure by a 27-5 vote last Wednesday, meaning the city government can now take the next steps to proceed with the legal process that will force the purchase of the property.
“I’m glad Metro Council passed our legislation that gives us the option to acquire property next to the zoo for a number of public needs,” Mayor O’Connell said in a statement. “We’re working closely with our Finance and General Services departments to plan for the site.”
The developer of the property, DC Blox, wanted to put up a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center on the site that was expected to cost more than $700 million to build. It would sit right beside the 188-acre Nashville Zoo at Grassmere, which opened in 1990 as the Grassmere Wildlife Park. This zoo is one of the biggest attractions in Tennessee, expecting to receive two million visitors annually by 2027. Aside from that, it also participates in more than 50 conservation programs with institutions across the world.
Zoo officials objected to the development, raising concerns about disruptions like noise and light pollution, among others. They even started an online petition that garnered more than 500,000 signatures by the end of July, even getting support from celebrities like Brad Paisley, Sheryl Crow, and Jack White.
DC Blox argues that 648 Grassmere Park used to provide data center functions, so putting up a newer one on the site would not necessarily disrupt the community, including its neighboring zoo. However, there have already been several widely reported incidents from across the U.S. that highlighted the noise and light pollution that zoo officials have been concerned about.
Residents in a town in Michigan have been complaining for about two years now after their neighboring data centers started emitting noise 24/7, comparing it to the sound that a vacuum makes in your living room. Aside from that, some people complain about infrasound, high- and low-frequency vibrations that do not register on decibel meters but could sometimes be felt coming from data centers and potentially cause adverse health effects. A Microsoft data center in Wisconsin is also facing a lawsuit due to noise and extreme light pollution.
While this does not mean that the proposed Nashville data center will cause a similar issue, it seems that city officials do not want to take this risk. Light and noise pollution could have adverse effects on the animals housed by the zoo, potentially disrupting their habitats and behavior.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The city council vote would allow the local government to negotiate with DC Blox for the acquisition of the property. However, this does not automatically mean that Nashville would automatically have the right to own the property. It will first have to negotiate with the owner to determine that property’s fair market value, and if the two parties cannot agree, then a judge or jury will have to determine the final amount. The company could also challenge the eminent domain claim.
There have been fears that the government will use eminent domain to advance data center projects, which was further spurred by Georgia Power’s use of the power to acquire 30 residential properties to expand the power grid. Although the utility company said that it wasn’t in the data center business, the move was made to connect a substation to a power plant, with 70% to 80% of the electricity traveling through it expected to serve data centers. But, as Nashville showed, this authority can also be used to block data center projects.

articles.title: Canal+ : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en août 2026
articles.text:
Canal+ : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en août 2026
Canal+ met de nombreuses séries à la disposition de ses abonnées, mais quelles sont celles qu'il ne faut surtout pas rater ? Les Numériques vous dévoile sa sélection pour août 2026.
Si vous ne partez pas en vacances en août, vous avez peut-être tout de même envie de vous changer les idées pendant votre temps libre. Pour cela, direction Canal+ car entre les propositions exclusives et les créations originales de la chaîne cryptée, il y a de quoi faire pour les amateurs de séries.
En plus, le catalogue propose aussi de nombreux programmes provenant d'autres plateformes de streaming comme Apple TV et Paramount+.
Pour vous aidez à faire votre programme, Les Numériques a sélectionné pour vous, comme en juillet dernier, son top des 10 séries à ne pas manquer sur Canal+ en ce moment.
Pour rappel, les contenus Apple TV sont disponibles dans toutes les offres d'abonnement Canal+. Les séries Paramount+ et Ciné+ OCS sont elles accessibles via les offres Canal+ Ciné Séries et Canal+ La Totale.
Quelles sont les meilleures séries à voir sur Canal+ en août 2026 ?
Prisoner
Lorsqu'un convoi pénitentiaire est pris d’assaut, Amber Todd, agente chargée du transfert, se retrouve prise au piège avec Tibor Stone - ancien tueur d’élite devenu témoin clé contre Pegasus, le réseau criminel qu’il a autrefois servi. Pourchassés par ce puissant conglomérat du crime et par des autorités corrompues, Amber et Tibor, deux inconnus que tout oppose, sont forcés de fuir ensemble…
Tahar Rahim et Izuka Hoyle forment un duo de choc dans ce thriller d'action bourré d'une tension que seuls les Britanniques semblent parfaitement bien maîtriser. Avec six épisodes au compteur, Prisoner captivent l'attention dès ses premières minutes et ne lâchent pas son spectateur avant son dénouement, faisant avancer son intrigue à un rythme soutenu et reposant sur une distribution impeccable pour maintenir les yeux du spectateur rivés sur l'écran.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Silo
Dans un futur proche, les dix mille dernières personnes sur Terre sont réfugiées à plusieurs mètres sous terre pour se protéger du monde extérieur, toxique et mortel. Mais personne ne sait quand et pourquoi le silo a été construit et toute personne qui tente de trouver la réponse s'expose à des conséquences fatales. Une ingénieure va partir à la recherche de réponses, et découvrir un mystère plus complexe que ce qu'elle avait imaginé.
Adaptée de la trilogie de livres à succès de Hugh Howey, Silo est une série ambitieuse, à la fois huis-clos anxiogène et critique subtile de nos sociétés modernes. Elle propose un récit prenant et une production de haute qualité, servie par un excellent casting, Rebecca Ferguson en tête. Du haut de ses trois saisons (une quatrième est en préparation), elle se positionne dans le haut du panier des séries d'Apple TV+, bref, un programme à ne pas rater.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Ted Lasso
Ted Lasso, un entraîneur de football américain, traverse l'Atlantique et débarque à Londres pour entraîner l'AFC Richmond, une modeste équipe de football... pas américain. Face à une équipe et une ville dubitatives, arrivera-t-il à leur faire adopter la méthode Ted Lasso ?
Fausse série sur le ballon rond, et vrai programme feel-good et doux-amer, Ted Lasso enrobe dans son vernis coloré un vrai cœur de personnages complexes et de thèmes sérieux comme la dépression, la relation père-fils et la masculinité toxique. Créée et écrite (entre autres) par Bill Lawrence (Scrubs) et Joe Kelly (How I Met Your Mother) et portée par le sympathique Jason Sudeikis (Comment tuer son boss, Les Miller), la série vous laissera le sourire aux lèvres et les larmes aux yeux à chaque fin d'épisode. Et pour ne rien gâcher, la saison 4 vient de sortir !
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Cape Fear : Les Nerfs à Vif
Une tempête s’apprête à s’abattre sur le couple d’avocats Anna et Tom Bowden lorsque Max Cady, le fameux tueur qu’ils ont mis derrière les barreaux, est libéré de prison avec la ferme intention de se venger.
Sans égaler le chef-d’œuvre de Martin Scorsese, cette réinvention sérielle de Cape Fear remplit son contrat de thriller psychologique haut de gamme. Si le format de 10 épisodes étire inutilement l'intrigue et en dilue la tension, la proposition plastique rétro et la performance magnétique de Javier Bardem suffisent à nous captiver. Une œuvre imparfaite, mais recommandable, qui confirme le goût d'Apple TV pour les productions léchées et les castings prestigieux.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Miniature Wife
À première vue, les Littlejohn mènent une vie de rêve. Les, scientifique de renom, apporte les derniers réglages à une machine révolutionnaire qui pourrait éradiquer la faim dans le monde. Lindy, autrice célèbre et lauréate du Prix Pulitzer, tente, elle, de renouer avec l’inspiration. Mais à y regarder de plus près, leur mariage prend l'eau. Lorsque Lindy annonce à Les qu’elle le quitte, une dispute éclate au cours de laquelle Les dirige par accident vers sa femme un rayon de son invention destiné à miniaturiser les cultures agricoles. Et voilà Lindy réduite à quelques centimètres.
Au croisement de La guerre des roses et Chérie, j'ai rétréci les gosses, cette série examine avec un humour aiguisé les tribulations d'un couple en pleine crise. Elizabeth Banks et Matthew Macfadyen sont au top de leur forme et livrent des performances débridées dans cette fiction aux effets visuels efficaces et à la mise en scène dynamique.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Star City
Dans ce récit alternatif où l’Union soviétique est devenue la première nation à poser un pied sur la Lune, Star City plante son décor derrière le rideau de fer et montre le quotidien des cosmonautes, des équipes d’ingénierie et des agents du renseignement intégrés au programme spatial soviétique, et les risques que chacun d’eux a pris pour faire basculer l’humanité vers une nouvelle ère.
Spin-off de For All Mankind, Star City est à la fois un récit alternatif, un thriller paranoïaque, une série d'espionnage et un drame haletant. Elle ne demande pas de connaître For All Mankind sur le bout des doigts pour être appréciée, et elle sait parfaitement comment s'en démarquer dans sa proposition tout en en étant un bon complément. La série jongle avec une bonne dose de complot, de tromperie et de tension pour offrir à ses spectateurs une histoire ambitieuse que l'on suit avec un intérêt grandissant.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Widow's Bay
Le maire d'une ville de Nouvelle-Angleterre souhaite en faire une destination touristique, malgré les avertissements sur le fait qu'elle est maudite.
Vous aimez l'horreur, les intrigues pleines de mystère et l'humour noir ? Alors vous serez comblé par cette série porté par un Matthew Rhys (The Americans) en grande forme. Sur fond de petite île à l'atmosphère inquiétante, Widow's Bay déroule une histoire prenante, soutenue par une mise en scène experte et des performances irréprochables de la part de l'ensemble de la distribution. Un petit bijou pour les adeptes de série de genre.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Sa majesté des mouches
Un groupe de garçons britanniques échoués sur une île tropicale inoccupée tombe progressivement dans l'anarchie à mesure que les conventions sociales disparaissent et que les tentatives de gouverner de manière responsable échouent.
Portée par une réalisation soignée et une structure narrative diablement efficace, la série Sa Majesté des mouches est à la fois une adaptation brillante et une proposition viscérale. La justesse désarmante de son jeune casting hisse immédiatement cette production au rang de petit chef-d'œuvre télévisuel. Si le récit s'avère parfois éprouvant par sa noirceur, Sa Majesté des mouches s'impose comme l'une des séries incontournables de l'année.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
The Madison
Confrontée à un deuil, une famille new-yorkaise décide de s’installer dans la vallée de la rivière Madison, dans le centre du Montana.
Même si cette série n’est pas un spin-off de Yellowstone, elle devrait plaire aux fans de la série de Taylor Sheridan. Il s’agit sans doute là du projet le plus personnel du prolifique scénariste à ce jour, ainsi que d’une poignante exploration du deuil. Fait de paysages époustouflants et de performances sans fausse note de Michelle Pfeiffer et Kurt Russell, The Madison nous transporte dans une histoire aussi déchirante que saisissante.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Margo a des problèmes d'argent
Margo, fille d’une ancienne serveuse chez Hooter’s et d’un ex lutteur professionnel, a récemment abandonné ses études et aspire à devenir écrivaine. Elle se retrouve à devoir concilier sa vie de jeune mère, les factures qui s’accumulent et peu de moyens pour les payer.
Elle Fanning (The Great) donne la réplique à Michelle Pfeiffer (The Madison) et Nick Offerman (Parks and Recreation) dans cette comédie dramatique créée par David E. Kelley (Big Little Lies) d'après le roman de Rufi Thorpe qui lui donne son titre. Produite par A24, cette nouvelle série arrivée en avril 2026 sur Apple TV est aussi audacieuse que touchante et amusante, et ses épisodes se regardent sans bouder son plaisir face aux tribulations de Margo.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :

articles.title: Apple revoit à la hausse les tarifs de son programme de reprise pour les iPhone, iPad et Mac : voici la liste complète
articles.text:
Apple n’est pas connu pour reprendre les anciens iPhone au meilleur prix, mais propose depuis quelques années un service Trade In qui permet de faire recycler ses anciens appareils contre de l’argent. En passant par Leboncoin ou une plateforme spécialisée, il est généralement possible d’obtenir plus d’argent pour un smartphone en bon état. Mais la marque dispose d’un argument important : la simplicité.
Comme l’ont remarqué nos confrères d’iGen, Apple a discrètement modifié le 6 août 2026 les montants proposés dans le cadre de son programme Trade In. La plupart des iPhone valent désormais quelques euros de plus, avec une hausse particulièrement importante pour les modèles les plus récents.
Jusqu’à 55 euros de plus pour faire reprendre son iPhone
La hausse n’est pas spectaculaire, mais elle concerne de nombreux modèles. Un iPhone 13 passe par exemple de 215 à 225 euros, un iPhone 14 Pro de 355 à 370 euros et un iPhone 15 Pro Max de 525 à 545 euros. Le record revient à l’iPhone 16 Pro Max, dont la valeur maximale passe de 700 à 755 euros.

Il s’agit à chaque fois de la valeur maximale proposée par Apple. L’état de l’appareil peut faire baisser le montant (même si Apple est réputé plus généreux que d’autres repreneurs, notamment au niveau des rayures et des traces d’usage). Et tous les changements ne vont pas dans le bon sens : l’iPhone 16 Plus perd 5 euros et l’iPhone 15 perd 10 euros.
Ces montants ne vous rendront pas riches mais sont intéressants pour un téléphone oublié dans un tiroir : 105 euros pour un iPhone 11, 130 euros pour un iPhone 12, 225 euros pour un iPhone 13 ou encore 85 euros pour un iPhone XR… C’est toujours ça de pris.
Les iPad, Apple Watch et Mac valent aussi un peu plus cher

L’Apple Store est une bonne manière de faire reprendre un iPhone
Faut-il vendre son iPhone à Apple ? Si votre seul objectif est d’en tirer le maximum d’argent, probablement pas. Une vente entre particuliers rapporte généralement davantage, tandis que certains reconditionneurs peuvent afficher des estimations supérieures.
Mais comme Numerama l’a raconté dans une enquête sur les plateformes de reprise, le montant affiché sur Internet ne correspond pas toujours au montant finalement versé. Une fois l’appareil envoyé, un reconditionneur peut considérer que son état ne correspond pas à la déclaration initiale et faire une contre-proposition beaucoup moins généreuse. Le client doit alors accepter ou demander le retour de son téléphone. Dans notre propre cas, un iPhone 11 estimé à 135 euros avait vu son prix tomber à 85 euros à cause de quelques rayures au dos. Le même appareil avait ensuite été repris au tarif maximal dans un Apple Store, où ces traces avaient été considérées comme de l’usure normale.
L’avantage d’Apple est surtout intéressant en magasin. Le diagnostic est effectué directement avec un employé et le montant est connu avant de laisser son appareil. Il n’y a pas besoin d’envoyer son smartphone puis d’attendre plusieurs jours pour découvrir si l’estimation initiale est maintenue. La reprise en ligne d’Apple reste, elle aussi, soumise à une vérification de l’état après réception.
Apple permet ensuite de déduire le montant d’un nouvel achat ou de récupérer sa valeur sous la forme d’une Apple Gift Card. Cette dernière peut être ajoutée au solde de son compte Apple et servir à acheter un Mac, un iPhone ou des accessoires, mais aussi des applications et certains abonnements comme Apple Music ou iCloud+.
L’autre avantage est qu’Apple recycle les iPhone avec son robot Daisy : les appareils ne sont pas broyés bêtement.
Une autre solution : attendre une offre de reprise boostée
Si vous n’êtes pas pressé, il peut néanmoins être plus intéressant d’attendre. Apple modifie régulièrement ses valeurs Trade In et les opérateurs, constructeurs ou revendeurs proposent ponctuellement des bonus de reprise lors du lancement d’un nouveau smartphone. Un téléphone repris 200 euros peut alors bénéficier de plusieurs dizaines, voire centaines d’euros supplémentaires sous certaines conditions. Peut-être que le lancement des iPhone 18 Pro incitera les opérateurs à faire des offres ?

articles.title: Why Starting Matters More Than Waiting for the Perfect Plan
articles.text:
Why Starting Matters More Than Waiting for the Perfect Plan
Discover why the first step often determines success and how starting with purpose creates momentum, confidence, and lasting results.
“The beginning is the most important part of the work.” This famous quote, often attributed to the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, highlights a truth that applies to nearly every area of life. Whether we are starting a business, learning a skill, writing a book, pursuing a fitness goal, or building a relationship, the first step often determines the direction and momentum of everything that follows. Many people focus heavily on the finish line. They dream about success, achievement, and results. However, they often overlook the importance of the beginning. The early stages of any journey establish habits, create momentum, and lay the foundation for future progress. A strong beginning does not guarantee success, but a weak or delayed start can make success far more difficult to achieve.
Why do people struggle to begin
Starting something new can feel intimidating. The fear of failure, uncertainty, and imperfection often prevents people from taking action. Many individuals wait for the perfect moment, believing they need more knowledge, resources, or confidence before they begin. Unfortunately, this mindset can lead to endless procrastination. The truth is that clarity often comes after action, not before it. People learn by doing. They gain confidence through experience. The willingness to start despite uncertainty is what separates progress from stagnation. Every successful project, career, and accomplishment begins with a moment when someone decides to take the first step.
The beginning creates momentum
One of the most important reasons beginnings matter is that they create momentum. When a person starts a task, they overcome the initial resistance that often feels overwhelming. Once progress begins, continuing becomes easier. A writer who completes the first page is more likely to finish the next one. A student who studies for twenty minutes often continues longer. A person who begins exercising develops a routine that becomes easier to maintain over time. Momentum transforms effort into habit. The hardest part is often not the work itself but getting started.
Early decisions shape future outcomes
The choices made at the beginning of any journey often influence the final result. When building a house, a strong foundation is essential. In education, understanding basic concepts makes advanced learning easier. In business, a clear vision helps guide future decisions. Similarly, personal goals require a strong beginning. Establishing healthy habits early creates consistency. Setting realistic expectations prevents discouragement. Defining a clear purpose keeps motivation strong during difficult periods. Small decisions made at the start can produce significant results later.
Perfection is the enemy of progress
Many people delay starting because they want everything to be perfect. They spend weeks planning, researching, and preparing without taking meaningful action. While preparation is important, excessive preparation can become a form of avoidance. The most successful people understand that improvement comes through practice. Their first attempt is rarely their best work. They allow themselves to begin imperfectly because they know growth happens along the way. A rough draft can be improved. A business plan can be adjusted. A skill can be refined. However, none of these improvements is possible without a starting point.
Confidence grows after action
A common misconception is that confidence comes before action. In reality, confidence often develops because of action. Most people do not feel fully prepared when they start something important. They feel uncertain, nervous, and sometimes afraid. Yet each small success strengthens their belief in their abilities. The first presentation builds public speaking confidence. The first workout creates fitness motivation. The first article helps a writer develop their voice. Action creates evidence that growth is possible. Confidence becomes a result of effort rather than a requirement for it.
Every great achievement starts small
History is filled with examples of extraordinary accomplishments that began with simple first steps. Great companies often start in garages, dorm rooms, or small offices. Bestselling books begin as rough ideas on a blank page. Skilled athletes begin as beginners who struggle with fundamentals. People often admire the final achievement without seeing the humble beginning behind it. Recognising this truth helps reduce the pressure associated with starting. The goal is not to begin perfectly. The goal is to begin.
How to create a strong beginning
Creating a meaningful start does not require dramatic action. Small, consistent steps are often more effective than ambitious plans that are difficult to sustain. Start by defining a clear objective. Understand why the goal matters to you. Break large tasks into manageable actions. Focus on progress rather than perfection. It is also important to remove unnecessary obstacles. Prepare your environment, establish a routine, and commit to taking action even when motivation is low. The quality of your beginning often depends on your willingness to start before you feel completely ready.
The lasting impact of a good start
A strong beginning influences more than immediate progress. It shapes mindset, habits, and long-term commitment. When people experience early success, even on a small scale, they become more motivated to continue. Positive momentum creates confidence, while consistent effort strengthens discipline. Over time, these small advantages accumulate into significant achievements. The beginning may seem like a small part of the journey, but it often determines whether the journey happens at all.
Conclusion
Plato's insight that “The beginning is the most important part of the work” remains deeply relevant today. Every meaningful accomplishment starts with a decision to begin. While planning and preparation have value, they cannot replace action. The first step creates momentum, builds confidence, and establishes the foundation for future success. Instead of waiting for perfect conditions, focus on making a strong start. The beginning may not be easy, but it is often the most important moment in the entire process.

articles.title: Oubliez beIN Sports, tous les matchs de la Liga espagnole arrivent sur Disney+ et DAZN
articles.text:
Oubliez beIN Sports, tous les matchs de la Liga espagnole arrivent sur Disney+ et DAZN
Bonne nouvelle pour les adeptes de football, et notamment espagnol : toute la prochaine saison de LALIGA arrive sur Disney+ et DAZN dès le 15 août prochain.
Alors que les nouveaux tarifs de la plateforme Ligue 1+ ont probablement refroidi de nombreux adeptes de football, Disney+ et DAZN viennent de faire une annonce intéressante en ce début août 2026.
Alors que toujours plus de services de SVoD classiques diffusent un nombre croissant de disciplines et de compétitions, cette fois c'est LALIGA (anciennement appelée la Liga), le championnat espagnol de football, qui arrive sur les deux plateformes. Depuis 14 ans, cette compétition était proposée par beINSports.
DAZN et Disney+ récupèrent LALIGA à beINSports pour 3 ans
DAZN et Disney+ proposeront la même chose, à savoir l'intégralité des 380 matchs de chaque saison à raison de dix par jour. La production assurée par ESPN proposera une couverture complète avec des commentaires en français.
Ce deal sera actif en France dès cette saison 2026/2027 lancée le 15 août, jusqu'à la saison 2028/2029. Pendant au moins trois ans donc, les adeptes de LALIGA sur beINSports devront revoir leurs habitudes.
Du côté de Disney+, il ne sera pas nécessaire de souscrire à un abonnement supplémentaire pour pouvoir profiter de LALIGA.
	
Nous sommes ravis d'accueillir LALIGA sur Disney+. Cette compétition entretient un lien particulier avec le public en France grâce à la présence de nombreux joueurs français évoluant en Espagne, de Kylian Mbappé à Eduardo Camavinga, Aurélien Tchouaméni ou Jules Koundé. Avec ses clubs légendaires et certaines des plus grandes affiches du football mondial, elle constitue un formidable enrichissement de notre offre sportive. Nous avons hâte d'offrir à nos abonnés une expérience éditoriale ambitieuse, innovante et pensée pour les fans de football d’aujourd'hui.
Concernant cette arrivée sur deux plateformes en France, Javier Tebas, Président de LALIGA, déclare : "Ce sont deux plateformes différentes: l’une est davantage spécialisée dans le sport, tandis que Disney+ ne propose pas uniquement du contenu sportif. À notre avis, elles se compléteront très bien en France. Ce sont deux plateformes nouvelles et innovantes qui permettront au public de suivre notre compétition." On relèvera qu'au fil des mois Disney+ propose toujours plus de sport, notamment sur ses marchés européens.
Outre la question du prix – à partir de 6,99 €/mois chez Disney+ avec pub et à un prix encore inconnu chez DAZN mais probablement pas sous les 10,99 €/mois –, la question de la qualité vidéo sera également un sujet pour les futurs abonnés.
Rappelons qu'il y a peu Disney+ Premium perdait (puis regagnait partiellement et progressivement) la 4K et la HDR.

articles.title: Large genome models used to design new viruses
articles.text:
A lot of the AI work in biology has been focused on designing proteins. That’s partly because proteins do most of the business of life, catalyzing the interesting chemistry and structuring cells. So, figuring out how to make a new protein can mean directly tinkering with biochemistry, providing new and potentially useful functions.
Since the genetic code provides a layer of abstraction between DNA and proteins, it wasn’t obvious what a model trained on DNA could do. Yet people went ahead and made a large genome model, and it turned out to be able to output DNA sequences that could encode functional proteins in bacteria and mimic the gene structures found in complex cells. Now, those same models have been used to output the genomes of viruses that infect bacteria.
This isn’t science fiction—all the viruses the models created are closely related to an existing virus. But they do have some distinct features that would be challenging to evolve. And the researchers who did the work, based at Stanford University, suggest we may want to start thinking now about preparing for the potential that someone could develop a related AI that can design a virus that targets vertebrates.
Large genome models
Large language models are essentially trained on their ability to predict the next bit of verbiage in as large a compendium of human-generated text as their developers can get ahold of. Large genome models are the same approach, but applied to DNA. To an extent, that simplifies matters, given that DNA only uses four “letters,” A, T, C, and G. But it’s more complicated in that genomes typically have areas where the next letter matters a great deal, interspersed with sequences where the next base could be anything and it wouldn’t matter.
So large genome models need to recognize the biological context of the sequence they’re outputting in many situations where we humans haven’t figured it out yet. Yet, if we feed them enough genome sequences, they seem to be able to. Bacterial genes with related functions tend to cluster together. Prompt a large genome model with the sequence of part of a cluster, and it’ll output DNA sequences that encode proteins with related functions—potentially including working proteins that look like nothing else we’ve identified so far.
But our own lack of knowledge places limits on what we can do with these models. If we prompt them with a bit of sequence from a complex cell, it will respond with a string of bases that contain what look like genes and regulatory DNA. But, since most genes can be located essentially anywhere in a eukaryotic genome, we have no idea what functions these hallucinated genes might perform (if any), so we can’t really test them in any way.
Still, as a precaution while training these models, termed Evo 1 and Evo 2, the researchers did not provide them with any sequences from viruses that target complex cells. Even if we can’t understand what they output, there’s a chance that they’ll output something dangerous.
But there’s a whole world of viruses that attack bacteria and can’t infect humans. And those, the Evo developers figured, are fair game. So, rather than looking at whether Evo 1 and Evo 2 could output reasonable-looking genes, they decided to test if they could output an entire genome.
Order from chaos
The model virus they chose as a test case is the catchily named ΦX174, part of a larger family of viruses that infect E. coli. In addition to the convenience of using the best-studied bacteria on the planet for tests, ΦX174 has a number of notable features. It’s fairly simple: At 11 genes spread over about 5,400 bases, all 11 of those genes have identified functions, and the virus’s infection cycle is well characterized.
It also has a useful feature from the perspective of working with a large genome model: The end of the virus always has the same short sequence of bases. So, if you use those bases as a prompt, the large genome model should be able to recognize that it needs to respond by outputting a sequence that is in some way related to ΦX174.
To further prepare their models, Evo 1 and Evo 2 were fed over 2 million additional bases of DNA sequences from viruses that infect bacteria (termed bacteriophages), and then fine-tuned with sequences specific to Microviridae, the group that ΦX174 belongs to. After that, they experimented with different prompts. Prompt with too much of the ΦX174 start sequence, and it would simply spit the rest of the genome back out. Too little, and it would generate lots of unrelated sequences. The researchers eventually found prompts with four to nine bases of the start sequence worked best.
While the outputs were primed to return something that looked like ΦX174, they literally could be anything—from near-carbon-copies of the normal virus to sequences that are only vaguely viral. To address this, the research team put a lot of pre-conditions on the outputs designed to throw away some of the more extreme ones while still enforcing a bit of tinkering.
For example, ΦX174 uses its own version of a spike protein to latch onto and infect bacteria; if the gene that encodes spike is missing or damaged, the virus simply wouldn’t work. So they discarded any outputs that had a spike protein that was less than 60 percent identical to the real one. They also threw out viruses that were too long or too short (< 4,000 bases or > 6,000), any that had strings of the same base more than 10 bases long, and any that had unusual frequencies of the two base pairings (GC and AT).
Throwing out those at the computer analysis stage left them with a reasonable number of potential outputs to test: 302 proposed viral sequences. They were able to chemically synthesize the sequences of 285 of them and inserted them into bacteria to see what happened. In most cases, the answer was “nothing.” But 16 of the sequences managed to inhibit the growth of the E. coli, suggesting they were actually working as viruses. Nine were the initial sequences output by the AI, and the remaining seven had acquired additional mutations after being inserted into bacteria.
The same, yet different
In some ways, these designed viruses were quite similar to the original ΦX174, but in other ways they were quite distinct.
For the “the same” perspective, the most effective viruses in the group of 285 tended to look a lot like the original. The overall fraction of viable viruses was only 16 out of the 285 outputs tested (5.6 percent). But if you looked only at the outputs that were most similar to the original ΦX174 (those with 98 percent sequence similarity and up), viability rose to 46 percent. So, if you don’t look a lot like a normal ΦX174, chances are good that you’re not going to work as a virus at all.
Most of the viable viruses had the same set of genes found in the original. None of them had even a single change in the stretch of DNA where the duplication of the virus’s genome starts.
All of that is in keeping with past studies that have shown that making even a single base change that alters just one amino acid in one of the proteins made from the virus’s genome had, on average, a 20 percent chance of inactivating the virus entirely. ΦX174 doesn’t just fear change; it’s typically murdered by it. Accordingly, the changes suggested by the AI produced a population of viable viruses that, on average, looked a lot like the original.
But, as individuals, the viruses were fairly distinct. One of them lost one of the viral proteins entirely, compensating for its loss with changes elsewhere in the genome. Another added an entirely new gene. Many had genes that were either longer or shorter than the original. One even replaced one of the ΦX174 genes with a gene from a very distantly related virus.
The researchers did an interesting analysis based on the idea that any one amino acid change had a 20 percent chance of inactivating the virus. Doing the math, they say that any viruses with less than 25 changes have only a 2.3 percent chance of being viable. Of the 300 or so viruses the AI output, five viruses fell in that range, and three of them were viable. At above 25 individual amino acid changes, the chances of producing a viable virus are essentially zero. Yet nearly a quarter of the AI-suggested viruses that had more than 25 changes were viable, including two that had over 50 amino acid alterations.
This tells us the AI is far more likely to make changes that leave a viable virus behind than random mutation.
Benefits and risks
This study is interesting from an intellectual perspective, but the researchers also show that it might be useful. Bacteriophages have been tested as therapies for bacterial infections that are resistant to standard antibiotics. But many bacterial strains have already evolved resistance to some families of viruses, including ΦX174. One potential solution to that is to use a cocktail of bacteriophages, since it may not be easy or even possible to evolve resistance to all of them.
And here, the AI has produced a cocktail of potential viruses. So the team tested a cocktail of natural bacteriophages that normally prey on E. coli and compared it to a cocktail of the 16 viable AI products. In their tests, the natural bacteriophage cocktail failed, but the AI-generated group managed to quickly evolve the ability to infect their otherwise resistant hosts. The researchers suspect that the process of overcoming resistance involved some of the AI-designed viruses swapping segments of DNA and the appearance of additional mutations.
It’s not clear whether this is a major potential benefit; phage therapies have been under consideration for years but haven’t seen widespread public use, despite the growing problems with drug-resistant bacterial strains. And the authors are very clear that large genome models come with risks. Although they excluded viruses that infect vertebrates from their training data, anyone with access to sufficient computing resources could repeat the process with those viruses included.
The paper ends with a call for better governance of this and related areas, such as the ordering of custom DNA sequences. So far, however, regulation of AI has largely failed to keep up with the rapid pace of the field.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: Jsaux Gaming Announces Voidjoy Controller-Focused Sub-Brand
articles.text:
Thursday, August 6th 2026
	
	
	
	
Jsaux Gaming Announces Voidjoy Controller-Focused Sub-Brand
JSAUX GAMING today announced Voidjoy, a new JSAUX sub-brand focused on gaming controllers and controller accessories. The announcement marks JSAUX GAMING's move into a dedicated controller category in its tenth year.
Voidjoy will be showcased at IFA 2026 in Berlin from September 4 to 8, where JSAUX will preview three Voidjoy product areas: portable controllers, pc controllers, and controller accessories.From Gaming Accessories to Player Control
For JSAUX GAMING, controllers are a natural extension of its work in gaming accessories: practical hardware designed around how people actually play. Voidjoy gives the category a dedicated focus within the JSAUX GAMING ecosystem.
"Over the past decade, JSAUX GAMING has built its products around practical design and real player needs," said Winnie Chen, Marketing Communications Manager at JSAUX. "Voidjoy brings that same thinking into gaming controllers, one of the most direct ways players experience their games."
A Preview of the Voidjoy Lineup
The Voidjoy lineup will center on three controller-focused product areas.
First Public Showcase at IFA 2026
At IFA 2026, JSAUX will present Voidjoy to media, partners, and visitors for the first time. JSAUX will exhibit from September 4 to 8, 2026 at Messe Berlin, booth H7.2b_117.
During the show, attendees will be able to see Voidjoy's three product lines at the JSAUX booth, alongside other products from the JSAUX GAMING lineup.

O Edge 70 Fusion Plus de 512 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.699 no Pix com cupom EDGE500 no Magazine Luiza. O celular da Motorola com tela AMOLED de 144 Hz, chip Snapdragon e câmeras de 50 MP atinge o menor preço já visto pelo Achados, com desconto de 36% sobre o original de R$ 4.199.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro could be in short supply soon after launch: report
articles.text:
Supply of the iPhone 18 Pro may be constrained at launch due to wider component shortages.
According to Culpium, a lack of DRAM could make it harder to get the Apple handset, which is expected to be unveiled in September. While the publication notes that production of Apple’s A20 Pro processor is “progressing well,” there’s a backlog on the DRAM side. In total, the site reports that about US$1 billion worth of Apple processors are sitting around waiting for DRAM before the next phase of production can begin.
Culpium says Apple and its manufacturing partners are “confident that they can meet initial demand” but have concerns that post-launch inventory will quickly deplete.
What could make this issue worse is the fact that Apple is reportedly not planning to introduce a base iPhone 18 model this year. Instead, the company is expected to only debut the higher-end iPhone 18 models and its long-rumoured foldable iPhone Ultra during its usual September keynote. The base iPhone 18 and lower-cost Air 2, meanwhile, are said to be slated for 2027. Therefore, your only options for new iPhones this year will very likely be the (more expensive) iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and iPhone Ultra.
At any rate, we won’t have to wait long to find out. The company is expected to hold this year’s fall iPhone event either on Wednesday, September 8 or Thursday, September 9, right after the Labour Day holiday. We should find out an exact date and time soon.
Source: Culpium

articles.title: AI security skills gap widens across Black Hat USA - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Defenders adapt as attackers accelerate: theCUBE’s Black Hat day one keynote analysis
The accelerating speed of AI-driven attacks is exposing an AI security skills gap that many security teams are only beginning to address. Defenders can’t hire their way out of that speed differential as attackers continue to outpace traditional security operations.
Black Hat USA opened with security teams grappling with frontier AI models that continue to compress the time between compromise and full exploitation. Defenders face a growing challenge that extends beyond simply keeping pace with faster attacks, according to Krista Case (pictured, left), principal analyst and practice lead for cyber resilience and security at theCUBE Research.
“These frontier AI models … are really accelerating the speed and the scale that attackers can move at, which is compressing the window for response for our defenders,” Case said. “One of the big things that defenders need … is context.”
Case and co-host Jon Oltsik (right) provided a day one keynote analysis at Black Hat USA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cyber resilience, threat intelligence and the new security skill sets AI adoption demands. (* Disclosure below.)
Closing the AI security skills gap
The gap between attackers’ speed and defenders’ ability to respond is widening, according to Oltsik. Mandiant’s M-Trends 2026 report found the median time between initial access and full compromise has collapsed to 22 seconds, down from more than eight hours in 2022. That pace is beyond what a human-only security operations center can match.
“Cyber resilience is the intersection point between technology and the business,” Oltsik said. “Before we have resilience, we have to understand: What are our business processes? What’s important to the business, and who are the constituents that need to make that decision?”
The skills gap is already reshaping staffing. Organizations will need AI penetration testers to stress-test agentic applications and AI governance specialists to track changing regulations and governance guardrails, according to Oltsik. Building effective agentic AI oversight also requires the right mix of people, process and technology, he added. Case noted that AI’s value comes from strengthening human decision-making, not eliminating it.
“The human still needs to be in the loop,” she said. “Combined, human plus AI, we can do more than we could do with just AI or just the human.”

articles.title: Pourquoi mettre son smartphone au frigo est la pire erreur de l'été
articles.text:
Quand le thermomètre s’affole, nos téléphones souffrent. Et sur TikTok, une solution miracle tourne en boucle pour calmer un smartphone brûlant : faire un petit tour au frigo. L’idée paraît imparable, sauf que les professionnels hurlent à la catastrophe. Le média américain Techspot rapporte d’ailleurs que les réparateurs européens voient défiler un nombre ahurissant d’appareils flingués par cette manie estivale. Mettre son smartphone au frais n’a rien d’une astuce de génie, c’est même le meilleur moyen de l’achever.
Humidité et choc thermique : le combo perdant
Le vrai problème de cette pratique ne se voit pas de l’extérieur : c’est la condensation. Prenez un téléphone bouillant, jetez-le dans un environnement à 4 degrés, et l’air chaud enfermé à l’intérieur va se refroidir d’un coup sec. Résultat ? Des gouttelettes se forment directement sur la carte mère et les puces. Vous vous dites peut-être que votre modèle est étanche. Grave erreur. La certification IP68 protège d’un plongeon accidentel dans la piscine, absolument pas de l’humidité qui naît au cœur même du châssis.
 @itsprincemarko Putting your phone in the Fridge helps actually 📲 #android #androidtips #princetechtips ♬ original sound – Prince Marko 
L’autre menace s’appelle le choc thermique. Les batteries au lithium détestent ça. Faire subir un tel grand écart de température à ces composants fragiles va massacrer leur endurance à long terme. Dans les pires scénarios, le choc physique est tellement violent que le verre de l’écran ou la façade arrière finit par craquer.
Comment refroidir son mobile sans le détruire
Si votre appareil affiche ce fameux écran d’alerte ou vous brûle les doigts, oubliez les solutions extrêmes. La première chose à faire est bête comme chou : enlevez la coque. Ces protections bloquent souvent la dissipation de la chaleur et transforment le téléphone en mini-four.
À lire aussi : Canicule : comment protéger smartphone, PC, TV et box Internet de la chaleur ?
Ensuite, calmez le jeu du côté logiciel. Coupez vos jeux gourmands, stoppez le streaming ou le GPS, et basculez sans attendre en mode économie d’énergie. Cela soulagera immédiatement le processeur. Éloignez-le vite des rayons du soleil et trouvez-lui un coin à l’ombre. Posez le téléphone sur une surface fraîche et attendez qu’il reprenne ses esprits. S’il est vraiment bouillant, éteignez-le un petit quart d’heure. Enfin, une règle d’or : ne laissez jamais votre appareil dans la boîte à gants d’une voiture garée en plein soleil. C’est l’assurance d’une batterie détruite, voire d’un départ de feu.

articles.title: Blue Origin révèle enfin la cause de l’explosion de la fusée New Glenn
articles.text:
Dave Limp, directeur général de Blue Origin, a dévoilé sur X l’origine de l’explosion massive de la fusée New Glenn. Bonne nouvelle : le problème devrait être relativement simple à résoudre, et les vols pourraient reprendre dès cette année. Elon Musk est même venu apporter son soutien à Blue Origin, qui semble bientôt prêt à réintégrer pleinement la course à la conquête spatiale. Il faut dire que l’entreprise a de nombreux satellites à mettre en orbite et plusieurs missions lunaires à assurer.
Une vanne défaillante sur un moteur est à l’origine de l’explosion de la fusée New Glenn
Pour rappel, le 28 mai dernier, la fusée New Glenn de l’entreprise Blue Origin a explosé lors d’une tentative de mise à feu statique. Il est question de l’une des explosions les plus importantes de l’histoire aérospatiale moderne. Les dégâts ont été quant à eux conséquents : le pas de tir LC-36 de Cap Canaveral (Floride) a notamment été fortement endommagé. Cet incident risque d’impacter le déploiement des satellites Amazon Leo et les missions lunaires de la NASA prévues pour 2028.
Nous savions que l’explosion provenait du premier étage de la fusée, mais l’origine exacte du problème restait inconnue. Jusqu’à maintenant. En effet, Dave Limp, directeur général de Blue Origin, a dévoilé sur X la cause précise de cet incident : l’explosion est due à une anomalie au niveau de la vanne principale d’oxygène de l’un des sept moteurs BE-4 équipant le premier étage de la fusée. Après avoir récupéré les débris de la fusée et mené plusieurs inspections et tests, les équipes de Blue Origin sont parvenues à cette conclusion.
Un problème qui devrait être résolu relativement facilement
Comme l’explique Dave Limp : « La voie à suivre est claire ». Les équipes de Blue Origin vont apporter quelques « petites modifications » pour corriger la défaillance de la vanne principale d’oxygène fixée sur les moteurs BE-4. Et bonne nouvelle, ces vannes d’oxygène modifiées pourront être facilement intégrées aux moteurs existants. Il n’est donc pas question de repenser le mode de fonctionnement de la fusée : de simples modifications sur une pièce devraient permettre de régler le problème. Pour Blue Origin, le soulagement doit être conséquent. La vanne principale d’oxygène modifiée sera prête d’ici la fin de ce mois d’août. Blue Origin espère maintenir son calendrier et faire voler New Glenn cette année.
De son côté, Elon Musk est venu apporter son soutien à Blue Origin. En effet, en réponse au post de Dave Limp faisant état de l’origine de l’explosion de New Glenn, le patron de SpaceX a déclaré : « J’espère que vous pourrez bientôt reprendre les vols ». Il faut dire que les deux entreprises collaboreront dans le cadre de la mission Artemis III. Enfin, rappelons aussi que, suite à l’explosion de New Glenn, Blue Origin a décidé de changer de stratégie en ayant recours désormais à une grue géante pour placer verticalement les fusées.

articles.title: Après le Dual Refresh Rate, les écrans gaming passent au Triple Refresh Rate
articles.text:
Les écrans Dual Refresh Rate (ou Dual Mode) ont commencé à résoudre un dilemme bien connu des joueurs : conserver une définition élevée pour les jeux immersifs ou la sacrifier afin d’atteindre une fréquence de rafraîchissement supérieure. AOC ajoute désormais un troisième palier à cette formule avec le CQ32G4ZA, présenté comme son premier moniteur Triple Refresh Rate.
Cet écran incurvé de 31,5 pouces propose du QHD (2 560 × 1 440 pixels) à 260 Hz, du Full HD (1 920 × 1 080 pixels) à 360 Hz et un mode HD à 500 Hz. Trois configurations accessibles depuis l’OSD, censées adapter le moniteur au type de jeu plutôt que d’imposer un compromis permanent entre finesse et fluidité.
Sponsorisé
Vous conservez l’électricité solaire produite en trop pendant la journée pour la réutiliser lorsque vos besoins augmentent.
Sponsorisé
Trois modes pour des usages très différents
AOC destine le mode QHD à 260 Hz aux RPG, jeux de stratégie et aventures en monde ouvert. Le Full HD à 360 Hz vise davantage les FPS compétitifs, tandis que le troisième mode pousse la fréquence jusqu’à 500 Hz pour répondre aux exigences de l’e-sport.
L’idée est cohérente : réduire la définition diminue le nombre de pixels que la carte graphique doit calculer et facilite l’obtention de fréquences d’images très élevées. Un seul moniteur pourrait ainsi servir aussi bien à parcourir un vaste monde ouvert qu’à rechercher la latence la plus faible possible dans Counter-Strike 2 ou Valorant.
Dans les faits, les trois modes ne présentent cependant pas le même intérêt. Le QHD à 260 Hz offre déjà un équilibre particulièrement solide entre netteté et fluidité. Le Full HD à 360 Hz constitue une alternative crédible pour le jeu compétitif. Le passage à 500 Hz paraît beaucoup plus spécialisé.
500 Hz : un choix assumé pour l'esport
Le mode 500 Hz répond à une logique bien connue des joueurs compétitifs : réduire la définition afin d'augmenter le nombre d'images par seconde. En passant en HD (1280 × 720 pixels), il devient beaucoup plus facile d'approcher, voire d'atteindre les 500 fps sur des titres e-sport comme Counter-Strike 2 ou Valorant avec une configuration suffisamment performante.
La contrepartie est toutefois importante. En se limitant à une définition HD sur une dalle de 31,5 pouces, l'image perd nettement en finesse. Les textes, les interfaces et les détails apparaissent beaucoup moins précis qu'en Full HD ou en QHD. Pour la plupart des joueurs, le mode Full HD à 360 Hz devrait ainsi représenter le meilleur compromis entre performances et qualité d'affichage.
La connectique constitue également un point à prendre en compte. L'écran dispose de deux entrées HDMI 2.0 et d'un DisplayPort 1.4. Si AOC n'a pas encore précisé les fréquences maximales accessibles sur chaque interface, le DisplayPort devrait logiquement être indispensable pour exploiter les modes les plus exigeants en bande passante.
Une dalle VA face aux exigences de l’e-sport
Le CQ32G4ZA repose sur une dalle Fast VA incurvée 1500R, annoncée avec un contraste natif de 4 000:1, un pic lumineux pouvant atteindre 450 cd/m² et un temps de réponse de 1 ms GtG.
Ce choix devrait favoriser la profondeur des noirs par rapport à une dalle IPS ou TN. Pour autant, une fréquence de 500 Hz ne garantit pas à elle seule une image parfaitement nette en mouvement. Les dalles VA peuvent notamment montrer davantage de lenteur dans les transitions sombres, avec du ghosting ou du black smearing. La valeur de 1 ms annoncée par le constructeur devra donc être confrontée au comportement réel de la dalle.
Une nouveauté surtout intéressante par son prix
Pour la majorité des joueurs, le CQ32G4ZA sera vraisemblablement utilisé en QHD à 260 Hz, avec quelques passages en Full HD à 360 Hz pour les jeux compétitifs. Le mode 500 Hz ressemble davantage à une fonction destinée à une petite niche et à un argument différenciant qu’à un futur réglage quotidien.
Le positionnement tarifaire change toutefois la lecture du produit. AOC annonce son écran à 319 euros, avec une disponibilité prévue en novembre 2026. À ce prix, le Triple Refresh Rate pourrait rendre cette flexibilité accessible à un public bien plus large. Plus que les 500 Hz, c’est finalement la possibilité de choisir entre trois équilibres différents sur un même écran qui constitue ici la véritable nouveauté.
