articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 6, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 6, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, August 6, 2026.
Indian startups are continuing to tap capital markets but at lowered valuation as fresh money comes into deeptech startups, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
Featured stories
Shiprocket cuts IPO size
The Gurugram-based ecommerce enablement platform has reduced the size of its initial public offering by 31% from Rs 2,342 crore to Rs 1,618 crore ahead of its market debut on August 12.
Cresa's fix for India's 12-billion sanitary pad disposal problem
Cresa makes hot-water-soluble sanitary pads that are 100% biodegradable, plastic-free, and dissolve in 80 seconds, tackling disposal waste, sanitation workers' dignity, and menstrual stigma in one plant-based innovation.
Influencer Anushka Rathod on making personal finance simple, responsible and accessible
Influencer Anushka Rathod speaks about responsible content creation, women’s financial empowerment, and why building wealth is ultimately about small, consistent habits.
Piper Serica raises Rs 300 Cr as first close of Bharat Tech Fund
Piper Serica, a Mumbai-based investment house that invests in public and private markets, has raised Rs 300 crore as the first close for its Rs 800 crore Bharat Tech Fund. A statement said nearly 50% of the commitments for the first close came from the existing investors of Fund I who were institutional investors, family offices, and high-net-worth individuals.
Funding news
Quick commerce startup HomeRun raises $12M in Series A+
HomeRun, a quick commerce platform for construction and interior materials, has raised $12 million in a Series A+ round of funding led by Nexus Venture Partners with participation from existing investors Sorin Investments, Titan Capital, Sparrow Capital and Consumer Collective by Atrium.
BlackSoil invests Rs 80 crore in Mintoak
Alternative credit platform BlackSoil has invested Rs 80 crore in Mumbai-based fintech SaaS company Mintoak to finance the debt component of its acquisition of Dubai-headquartered loyalty technology firm ICC Loyalty. The acquisition expands Mintoak's presence to over 20 countries, with partnerships across more than 50 banks including HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, SBI Payments and Emirates Islamic.
The combined entity now supports over five million merchants, 11 million customers and processes annual payment volumes exceeding $93 billion. BlackSoil said the investment was driven by Mintoak's profitable growth, strong banking relationships and technology-led business model. The merged business generates over $30 million in annual revenue, reflecting BlackSoil's growing focus on acquisition financing and technology-enabled enterprises.
Consint.AI raises Rs 22 crore Series A funding
Deeptech startup Consint.AI has raised Rs 22 crore in a Series A funding round led by BIG Global Investment JSC, Equanimity Ventures Trust II and Seafund Venture India Scheme I. The company will use the fresh capital to accelerate international expansion, strengthen enterprise delivery and develop a foundational AI model dedicated to fraud, waste and abuse detection across insurance and banking. Consint.AI said its AI platform has analysed over 100 million transactions, identified fraud worth more than Rs 1,000 crore and deployed over 500 AI and machine learning models. The startup also plans to expand its healthcare and insurance offerings while growing operations across India, the Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and the United States.
Typsy Beauty secures Rs 20 Cr funding
Beauty and personal care brand Typsy Beauty has raised Rs 20 crore in a funding round led by Saama Capital, with participation from existing and new strategic investors including Sanjay Kapoor, Tanaaz Bhatia, SRF Group and family offices of Havells and Eicher Motors. The company plans to utilise the funds to strengthen its presence in quick commerce and offline retail, expand into skincare through hybrid skincare-makeup products and scale its fragrance business.
Typsy Beauty currently offers 27 products across makeup and fragrances and sells through its own website as well as platforms such as Nykaa, Amazon, Myntra, Flipkart, Tira, Blinkit and Zepto. The company expects to launch more than 10 new products in the coming months.
Amigo raises Rs 4.5 Cr from Foxhog Ventures
Food delivery startup Amigo has raised Rs 4.5 crore in funding from Foxhog Ventures to expand its affordable fresh-food delivery business. Founded by entrepreneurs Anshuk and Saswat, the startup aims to provide freshly prepared meals at accessible prices while focusing on quality and consistency.
The company plans to begin operations in Kolkata before expanding to other markets. Amigo said it intends to differentiate itself in India's competitive food delivery market through value pricing and a strong emphasis on fresh meals prepared to customer expectations. The investment will support market launch, operational expansion and customer acquisition as the startup seeks to build a sustainable presence in the country's rapidly evolving online food delivery ecosystem.
Other news
PhonePe launches fixed deposits and daily savings product
PhonePe has launched fixed deposit distribution on its platform in partnership with banks and NBFCs while introducing a digital Daily Recurring Deposit product with Shivalik Small Finance Bank. The new savings offering allows customers to begin investing with as little as Rs 100 per day, encouraging disciplined savings.
Users can also compare and book fixed deposits directly within the PhonePe app and manage multiple deposits through a single interface. Fixed deposits offered through partner banks are insured up to Rs 5 lakh under Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation guidelines. PhonePe said the launch expands its financial services portfolio by providing customers with secure, low-risk investment and savings options.
Super.money launches splitStore credit platform
UPI platform Super.money has launched splitStore, a checkout-based credit solution that enables consumers to split purchases into interest-free repayments in partnership with regulated lenders. The company said the offering integrates credit directly into the payment journey, making purchases more affordable while encouraging responsible borrowing.
Super.money said splitStore is designed to help India's growing new-to-credit population establish formal credit histories through timely repayments. The launch marks the company's expansion from a UPI payments platform into a broader commerce and financial ecosystem that combines payments, shopping and embedded credit. The company believes the new "split-commerce" model will improve affordability and enhance access to formal credit for digital consumers.
HEX20 signs multi-launch pact with Skyroot Aerospace
Technopark-based spacetech startup HEX20 has signed a Multi-Launch Agreement with Skyroot Aerospace for Earth observation constellation and in-orbit payload demonstration missions. Under the agreement, HEX20 has secured three dedicated launches aboard Skyroot's Vikram launch vehicles beginning in the fourth quarter of 2027.
The missions will support HEX20's spacecraft while also offering rideshare opportunities for third-party satellites. The partnership combines Skyroot's launch capabilities with HEX20's expertise in spacecraft engineering, payload integration, ground operations and mission delivery. The companies said the collaboration aims to create an integrated ecosystem covering spacecraft development, launch services, orbital operations and Earth observation data from India.
Winners of Boeing’s BUILD programme 2026
Boeing has announced seven teams comprising university students and early-stage start-up entrepreneurs as winners of the fifth edition of the Boeing University Innovation Leadership Development (BUILD) program 2026.
The winning teams are Aerosearch Technologies, Alkamy Carbon, DIASOL Pvt. Ltd., EarthSprint Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Oreejoy MedTech Pvt. Ltd, StelX Dynamics, and SWRN Systems Pvt. Ltd. These winners will be further supported by Boeing and incubator partners over the next few months to help develop their ideas into market-ready and viable business solutions.
Each winning team will receive a grant of Rs 10 lakh to support the development of their ideas. Over the past five years, BUILD has received more than 7,000 applications and supported more than 35 startups across sectors including aerospace and defence, technology, sustainability, and social impact.
Quest Global appoints four independent directors
Engineering services company Quest Global has appointed Emiko Higashi, Dr. John Hillen, Sabine Kohleisen and Rostow Ravanan as independent directors to its board, expanding its leadership to 12 members. The appointments increase women's representation to one-third of the board and are aimed at strengthening governance and strategic oversight as the company expands across industries including aerospace, automotive, energy, healthcare, rail and semiconductors.
The new directors bring expertise in investment management, defence, enterprise transformation, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Quest Global said the appointments reflect its commitment to diverse leadership and long-term growth while enhancing strategic thinking and governance as it scales its global engineering services business.
Paramotor partners Aditya Birla Capital Digital
Paramotor Digital Technology has entered into an arrangement with Aditya Birla Capital Digital Limited (ABCDL) to distribute prepaid payment instruments, including digital and physical prepaid cards and gift cards.
Under the partnership, Paramotor will leverage its fintech expertise and digital distribution network to expand the reach of ABCDL's prepaid payment solutions among corporate and retail customers. The company will also ensure compliance with Reserve Bank of India regulations, customer protection standards and industry best practices. The collaboration aims to strengthen the availability of secure and technology-driven prepaid payment products while combining Paramotor's partner ecosystem with ABCDL's regulated payments infrastructure to support broader adoption across India.
InCred Capital names Abhinav Khanna CEO – Capital Markets
InCred Capital has appointed Abhinav Khanna as Chief Executive Officer – Capital Markets to lead its Institutional Equities, Equity Capital Markets and Asset Services businesses. Khanna brings more than 25 years of experience across institutional equities, capital markets and investment management, having worked in India, the UK and the Middle East.
Most recently, he served as Managing Director and Chief Business Officer – Global at ValueQuest Investment Advisors. He also spent over a decade at Citigroup Global Markets, where he held senior leadership roles including Managing Director and Head of Equity – India. InCred said the appointment will help strengthen its institutional equities and capital markets franchise and accelerate future growth.
InsuranceDekho appoints Rohan Mittal as Group CFO
InsuranceDekho has appointed Rohan Mittal as Group Chief Financial Officer to strengthen its leadership team as the company enters its next phase of growth. Mittal will oversee finance, capital strategy and corporate governance, bringing nearly two decades of experience across listed and high-growth companies. Most recently, he served as Group CFO at RateGain, where he played a key role during the company's $280 million acquisition of Sojern. He has also held senior finance leadership roles at Yatra Online, Allcargo-Gati and Rivigo. InsuranceDekho said his experience in scaling businesses, managing capital and driving strategic growth will support the company's long-term expansion plans.
Snapdeal launches AI-powered shopping suite
Snapdeal has introduced a multi-solution AI Suite featuring personalised recommendations, conversational search and image-based product discovery to improve online fashion shopping. The company said its AI-powered recommendation engine, StyleMatch, now influences 76% of customer orders by analysing browsing behaviour, purchase history, location and preferences to personalise recommendations.
Snapdeal also processes more than five million AI-assisted conversational searches every month using large language models, enabling customers to search naturally instead of relying on product keywords. The company said the new AI capabilities are designed to make product discovery more intuitive and accessible, particularly for shoppers across Bharat, while enhancing customer engagement and shopping experiences on its platform.
Hexaware joins Microsoft Intelligent Security Association
Hexaware Technologies has become a member of the Microsoft Intelligent Security Association (MISA), a global ecosystem of software developers and security partners that integrate with Microsoft Security solutions. The company's end-to-end security solution for Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, available on Microsoft Marketplace, helps enterprises accelerate Zero Trust adoption through unified extended detection and response, security information and event management, identity protection and cloud security capabilities.
Powered by Hexaware's Tensai Security Ops framework, the solution also provides security assessments, attack validation and compliance-focused analysis. Microsoft validated the offering as part of the membership process, strengthening Hexaware's position in enterprise cybersecurity services.
REPLUS Engitech receives Rs 43 crore under RDI Scheme
REPLUS Engitech, a subsidiary of Bhilwara Energy, has been selected under the Government of India's Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme and awarded Rs 43 crore to develop advanced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) technologies.
The funding will support research, strengthen indigenous technology capabilities and contribute to India's clean energy ambitions. Administered by the Department of Science and Technology, the RDI Scheme promotes investments in emerging sectors such as energy transition, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, deep technology and climate action. REPLUS said the grant will help accelerate innovation in energy storage and support the country's growing renewable energy, electrification and advanced manufacturing ecosystem.
Flipkart Foundation supports school nutrition programme
More than one lakh government school children across Bengaluru and Hubli received nutritious morning snacks under a partnership between Flipkart Foundation and The Akshaya Patra Foundation. Implemented through Akshaya Patra's Morning Nutrition Programme, the initiative complemented the Government of India's PM POSHAN scheme by serving over 21 lakh nutritious meals to improve children's nutrition, energy and classroom readiness.
The programme was delivered through Akshaya Patra's kitchen and distribution network and is estimated to have positively impacted more than four lakh people, including students' families and communities. Flipkart Foundation said the initiative aligns with its focus on community development, skill development, entrepreneurship and environmental responsibility, having positively impacted over 4.14 million underserved individuals since 2022.
GFF AI launches Enterprise Intelligence Engineering model
GFF AI PTE. LTD. has introduced Enterprise Intelligence Engineering, a new framework designed to help organisations transition from digital enterprises to AI-native businesses. The model combines enterprise strategy, intelligent systems, sovereign AI infrastructure and responsible AI governance into a unified engineering approach. According to the company, the framework enables businesses to embed intelligence across core operations to improve security, scalability and long-term competitiveness.
GFF AI will initially focus on sectors including banking, insurance, manufacturing, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, mining, defence, government and higher education. The company said the integrated model aims to help enterprises build AI-driven operating intelligence and accelerate digital transformation while ensuring responsible and future-ready AI adoption.
Yoginii partners with The Woman’s Company
Yoginii, a women-first wellness platform and marketplace, has announced the onboarding of The Woman’s Company, an intimate wellness brand built by women, for women. The collaboration aligns with Yoginii’s plan to onboard over 100 curated wellness brands over the next year as it builds a trusted ecosystem of purpose-driven, women-first brands addressing diverse wellness needs.
Through the association, a curated range of The Woman’s Company products will be made available on the Yoginii ecommerce platform, expanding access to thoughtfully designed solutions that support women’s comfort, confidence and intimate wellbeing. The partnership brings together two brands united by a shared vision of empowering women to prioritise their health and wellness without hesitation or stigma. The Woman’s Company offers products that place comfort, self-care and confidence at the centre of the experience.

articles.title: Cyprus-based enterprise agentic CX company Omilia secures €58.1 million in Series B funding | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Omilia, the Cyprus-based self-learning agentic CX company, has secured a €58.1 million ($67 million) Series B funding round led by Expedition Growth Capital.
The company plans to use this capital to support continued growth acceleration in North America and globally, including the opening of Omilia’s first US office in the second half of 2026. The raise also follows a series of senior go-to-market appointments as the company scales its global commercial organisation
“Omilia has been growing strongly for many years, and that momentum is now accelerating, particularly in the US. The Omilia Cloud Platform has become an essential foundation for our customers’ interactions with their millions of customers every day. Our game-changing Self-Learning CX Agents are setting a new standard in the contact centre market. This funding will accelerate our distribution of this powerful capability to the many enterprise customers that are seeking a best-in-class AI platform for their contact centre transformation,” said Dimitris Vassos, CEO and co-founder at Omilia.
Founded in 2002 by Vassos, Pelias Ioannidis, and John Nikolaidis, Omilia is an enterprise agentic CX company that helps enterprises transform customer service with AI. It claims that it caters to the world’s largest and most demanding enterprises; organisations often in regulated industries such as banking, insurance and healthcare.
The company states that its native self-learning CX agents automate interactions with precision, help human agents in real time, and deliver seamless, personalised experiences across all channels.
As per the company, its voice-first AI platform is built entirely on its own proprietary agentic Voice AI technology, and supports the most stringent enterprise security and compliance standards, including FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA and GDPR.
Omilia reported that it runs some of the largest agentic voice deployments in production today. These include a Tier 1 US bank handling over 1 million calls per day, and one of the world’s largest real-time agent-assist programmes for a multinational US insurance company, handling over 600,000 calls per day.
According to the company, this scale is possible because its Voice AI is purpose-built for large-scale, enterprise voice interaction, and for the unstructured customer data behind every call. “Owning the core of that stack, rather than orchestrating across third-party components, is what allows Omilia to resolve 50,000+ concurrent voice interactions for a single client, whilst maintaining sub-second latency, predictable cost, and industry-leading accuracy,” the company mentioned in the press release.
The company also launched Lexis, a generative text-to-speech (TTS) model designed specifically for enterprise contact centres and built natively into the Omilia platform.
Omilia highlighted that since raising its Series A, it has grown live annual recurring revenue (ARR) by more than 10x to over €52 million ($60 million), without raising additional equity capital in the interim. In July, Omilia announced an expanded strategic agreement with Taco Bell, whose voice AI deployment with Omilia spans 1,000+ US drive-thrus across 38 states.
“Omilia has paired deep domain expertise with demonstrable product leadership to build a highly satisfied enterprise customer base. Omilia’s Self-Learning Agentic CX is delivering a step change in call containment and operational improvement, with glass-box auditability and cost predictability that is structurally difficult for other vendors to compete with. This is a world-class team, and we are proud to be doubling down on our partnership,” said Oliver Thomas, Founder and Managing Partner, Expedition Growth Capital.
The company’s notable clients include Capital One, Discover, Taco Bell, RBC, DWP, First Financial Bank, Purolator, and PSEG.

articles.title: L'acteur Uli Latukefu incarnera Ganondorf dans le film The Legend of Zelda
articles.text:
On en sait enfin un peu plus sur le casting du film The Legend of Zelda, alors que nous sommes à moins d’un an de la sortie au cinéma et que le tournage est terminé depuis avril. Jusqu’à maintenant, Sony Pictures et Nintendo n’avaient confirmé que les rôles principaux, à savoir Bo Bragason en Zelda et Benjamin Evan Ainsworth en Link. Les deux ont une ressemblance frappante avec les deux héros, ce qui est de bon augure.
Dans un article publié le 6 août 2026, Deadline ajoute un troisième nom qui tient une importance capitale dans l’adaptation : c’est donc Uli Latukefu qui a été choisi pour enfiler le costume de Ganondorf, le grand méchant. Selon les sources du média, il aurait signé un deal portant sur plusieurs films. On connaît donc le trio majeur du film The Legend of Zelda, sachant que d’autres noms ont été ajoutés par ailleurs.
The Legend of Zelda sera l’un des derniers films du regretté Sam Neill
Contrairement à Bo Bragason en Zelda et Benjamin Evan Ainsworth, Sony Pictures et Nintendo ne font pas le pari de la jeunesse avec Uli Latukefu, Australien âgé de 42 ans. Il est connu pour avoir interprété Dwayne Johnson dans la série Young Rock. Au cinéma, on l’a vu dans Alien: Covenant, Black Adam, Next Goal Wins ou encore MaXXXine. Avec The Legend of Zelda, sa carrière pourrait totalement changer.
Dans une autre publication, Deadline annonce que The Legend of Zelda sera l’un des derniers films du regretté Sam Neill, disparu en juillet à l’âge de 78 ans. Le rôle occupé par l’acteur vu dans les films Jurassic Park ou encore la série Peaky Blinders n’est pas précisé. Mais tout porte à croire qu’il incarnera le roi d’Hyrule.
De son côté, Dichen Lachman (Severance) jouera Impa, garde du corps et proche conseillère de Zelda. Quant à Yvonne Strahovski (Handmaid’s Tale), elle sera une reine, sans plus de précision sur le personnage exact. Cela fait à l’arrivée cinq noms en tout dans la distribution connue de The Legend of Zelda, dont l’histoire demeure un mystère. Nul doute que nous ne sommes plus qu’à quelques semaines de la diffusion de la première bande-annonce, qui devra rassurer les fans sur le ton et la photographie. Sony Pictures et Nintendo jouent gros, mais le potentiel est là.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8, Ultra et Z Flip 8 : le nouveau format pliant de Samsung fait un carton en France
articles.text:
Samsung peut avoir le sourire. À quelques jours de leur commercialisation officielle prévue le 7 août, les nouveaux smartphones pliants de la gamme Galaxy Z, les Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra et Galaxy Z Flip 8, surpassent déjà les objectifs de la marque en Europe. Dans l’Hexagone, l’engouement est particulièrement notable : les précommandes enregistrent une hausse de plus de 20 % par rapport à la génération précédente (Galaxy Z Fold 7 et Z Flip 7).
Le pari gagnant du format « passeport »
La véritable star de cette nouvelle cuvée s’appelle le Galaxy Z Fold 8. Avec son nouveau format hybride, ce modèle accapare à lui seul plus de 40 % des précommandes de la série en France. Un chiffre impressionnant qui tend à valider la prise de risque du constructeur sud-coréen.
Conçu pour devenir le champion du divertissement, ce modèle abandonne le format tout en hauteur pour adopter un gabarit type « passeport », plus léger (201 grammes) et surtout plus compact. Comme nous l’avons constaté lors de notre test, son ratio d’écran optimisé (4:3 en paysage, 3:4 en portrait) a de quoi séduire massivement les utilisateurs cherchant un appareil aussi à l’aise pour la lecture que pour le visionnage de vidéos.
« Le dépassement des objectifs de précommandes de notre précédente génération de smartphones pliables témoigne d’un intérêt toujours plus marqué des consommateurs pour les innovations liées aux smartphones pliables », se félicite Menno Van Den Berg, Président du Samsung European Telecom Office, en soulignant l’engouement spécifique suscité par ce nouveau Z Fold 8.
Z Fold Ultra et Z Flip : une gamme désormais bien segmentée
Si le modèle « passeport » capte l’essentiel de l’attention, les deux autres déclinaisons trouvent leur place grâce à une segmentation technique beaucoup plus tranchée. Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra justifie son positionnement tarifaire par une configuration plus musclée que le Z Fold 8, notamment en photo, et un châssis affiné à 4,1 mm d’épaisseur.
De son côté, le Galaxy Z Flip 8 maintient le format à clapet emblématique tout en renouvelant sa fiche technique avec un processeur Exynos 2600.
La période de précommande s’achève ce jeudi 6 août sur la boutique officielle et chez les revendeurs partenaires. Les trois modèles arrivent en rayon dès demain, l’occasion de vérifier si ce pic d’intérêt initial se maintient dans le temps.

articles.title: As African newsrooms shrink, big companies face less scrutiny
articles.text:
This article draws from my conversation with Ivana Heijnen in Episode 7 of the Voices and Visions podcast, which explores the people and ideas shaping Africa’s innovation economy.
Across much of Africa, companies are becoming larger, richer, and more influential. The newsrooms expected to scrutinise them are moving in the opposite direction.
I found myself returning to this contradiction during the seventh episode of Voices and Visions, a podcast hosted by Ivana Heijnen about the people shaping Africa’s tech and business ecosystems.
I have always believed that journalism begins with caring about people, systems, and whether they work as they should. A reporter’s responsibility is not merely to describe events. It is to examine who is exploiting whom, which institutions are failing, and who benefits when they do.
“There’s that surveillance role of a journalist,” I told Heijnen. “You scrutinise who is stealing from whom, what is going on well, what is not working as it is supposed to, and give people solutions to some of these things.”
That role is becoming harder to perform.
African newsrooms are operating under severe financial pressure. Advertising revenue has shifted to global tech platforms such as Facebook, Google, and X. Print circulation has declined, while audiences increasingly expect news to be free. Media organisations have responded by imposing hiring freezes, laying off staff, and shrinking editorial budgets.
Reporters are expected to produce more stories across more platforms with fewer resources.
Investigative journalism is particularly vulnerable. It is expensive, slow, and legally risky. A reporter may spend weeks pursuing a story that generates no immediate revenue and may never be published. By contrast, a sponsored event or corporate announcement can generate income and be turned into multiple pieces of multimedia content within hours.
While this is now being presented as a media business problem, it is also a big accountability crisis.
“Media has a huge role,” I said during the conversation. “Surveillance. We need to scrutinise everything that is in the public. We need to hold everyone to account, and that is telling the story as it is.”
But watchdog journalism cannot survive on responsibility alone. It requires reporters, editors, lawyers, travel budgets, data, and institutions willing to withstand commercial and political pressure. As those resources disappear, the people and companies requiring the greatest scrutiny gain more room to shape the stories told about them.
Powerful companies, weaker newsrooms
Large companies have resources that most African publications currently do not. They retain communications advisers, lawyers, lobbyists, and public relations agencies. They cultivate relationships with editors, sponsor industry events, and buy advertising across multiple platforms.
None of those activities is inherently improper. Companies have a legitimate interest in explaining what they do. The problem arises when their capacity to influence the public narrative exceeds the media’s capacity to interrogate it.
Some of the companies journalists cover are also among the biggest sources of advertising revenue. Their executives may have close relationships with media owners. In some countries, the people who possess political or commercial power also directly own the outlets expected to scrutinise them.
“Some of these people who have this power also own the media outlets,” I told Heijnen. “They just want reporters to rejig whatever they want to churn out.”
A financially secure newsroom can resist some of that pressure. A struggling one must calculate what it can afford to lose.
This imbalance matters because large corporations are not passive victims of weak systems. They can possess enormous power to influence regulation. A major bank, telco, or multinational can lobby policymakers, hire influential advisers, and gain access to decision-makers in ways that an ordinary citizen cannot.
“If they want a regulation or a policy to be changed, they can lobby, they can push for it,” I said. “But they choose not to because they also benefit from that flawed system. And who loses in all this? The ordinary person.”
Without independent reporting, the public sees only part of that relationship. Companies speak enthusiastically about innovation, inclusion, and the jobs they create. Far less is said about market dominance, labour practices, political connections, or the regulations they helped shape.
Press releases become the story
The effects are especially visible in Africa’s tech ecosystem. Startup coverage is heavily influenced by fundraising announcements, founder profiles, and carefully constructed claims about impact.
The companies receiving the most attention are often those with the strongest communications machinery, not necessarily the strongest businesses.
“Capital follows narrative,” I told Heijnen.
Before capital becomes rational, it can follow emotion and attention. A compelling founder story attracts coverage. Coverage creates visibility. Visibility suggests momentum. That momentum attracts investors, partnerships, and still more coverage.
Many highly funded startups understand this loop. They retain effective PR firms and build relationships with journalists and editors across the continent. They appear repeatedly in the media, becoming familiar to investors and policymakers.
“Whether their business models are good, or they are solving a problem that is there, is neither here nor there,” I said. “They’ve mastered what can capture attention.”
Journalists are meant to interrupt that loop with difficult questions. How many jobs did the company create? How much revenue does it generate? Are its customers better off? Did the product lower costs? What happened to the millions it raised three years ago? Are its claims independently verifiable?
Yet these questions require time and expertise. It is much easier to rewrite an announcement saying that a startup has raised $5 million than to spend months investigating what happened after its previous round.
“Fundraising should no longer be news,” I said. “A good idea should attract investment. The story should be the impact.”
The amount raised is not meaningless. Funding can reveal where investors see opportunity and which sectors are attracting capital. But money entering a company should mark the beginning of the scrutiny, not the successful conclusion of its story.
If journalism stops at the announcement, the media becomes part of the startup’s fundraising infrastructure.
Funding accountability
The answer is not to pretend journalism can exist without money. Reporters need to be paid. Publications need sustainable revenue. Events, sponsorships, subscriptions, and advertising can all support valuable reporting.
The danger arises when the organisation being scrutinised becomes indispensable to the survival of the organisation conducting the scrutiny.
That dependency can change editorial priorities even without direct interference. Publications begin producing more of the content advertisers want. Reporters spend more time at corporate events and less time with workers, customers, and whistleblowers. Success is measured by output, traffic, and commercial partnerships rather than the public significance of the reporting.
Meanwhile, communities harmed by corporate decisions usually lack professional communications teams. A customer challenging a bank, a worker dismissed by a company, or a small business squeezed by a dominant platform cannot organise a press briefing whenever they want to influence coverage.
Journalism is supposed to correct that imbalance. It gives people without institutional power a way to confront those who possess it.
But that requires media institutions strong enough to absorb the consequences.
In my conversation with Heijnen, I acknowledged that newsrooms are undergoing a profound transformation and that older business models are no longer as profitable as they once were. Those constraints affect what stories can be pursued. Still, financial difficulty cannot erase the reason journalism exists.
“We need to think of it in the long term,” I said. “How do we keep up with storytelling and holding people to account?”
There is no simple answer. African media will need more readers willing to pay for journalism, more diversified revenue models, and stronger legal and institutional protection for reporters. Newsrooms must also draw a clearer line between commercial partnerships and editorial decisions.
Journalists, for their part, must resist becoming distribution channels for corporate narratives. We must interrogate fundraising claims, question impact figures, and return to companies after the headlines have faded.
The survival of African journalism is not only about saving reporters’ jobs or preserving familiar media brands. It is about maintaining one of the few institutions capable of confronting absolute political and corporate power.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: OpenAI rolls out a major ChatGPT upgrade, even if you don’t pay for it
articles.text:
OpenAI is rolling out a more reliable version of ChatGPT GPT-5.6 Sol for Plus and Pro users, while Free users are getting unlimited text chats with GPT-5.6 Luna.
The changes are focused on making ChatGPT more direct, factually accurate, and consistent across quick questions and deeper reasoning tasks.
In our tests, BleepingComputer observed that GPT now gives you greater control over the model's reasoning and intelligence with a new slider.
As you can see in the screenshot, you can slide GPT's reasoning from Instant to High. Instant would respond almost immediately, while High reasoning could take several minutes.
You can keep the slider low for everyday questions or increase the reasoning effort for tasks such as research, coding, writing, planning, and complex decisions.
GPT-5.6 Sol is getting more focused and reliable answers
OpenAI says the updated GPT-5.6 Sol has been tuned specifically for how people use ChatGPT, rather than for the longer-running agentic workflows found in Codex and ChatGPT Work.
"It delivers more focused answers, adapts its level of detail to the question, avoids unnecessary formatting, and offers a helpful correction when simply agreeing wouldn't be useful," OpenAI said.
For example, if you ask simple questions, GPT should answer directly without adding unnecessary background. For more complicated work, it should provide enough detail while keeping the main recommendation easy to identify.
A question like "Who is the president of the United States?" will have a single-line answer, but a question like "How are elections held in the US?" will have a longer answer with background information.
OpenAI also claims that GPT-5.6 Sol is less likely to make factual mistakes when handling dates, numbers, sources, legal rules, medical information, financial questions, or assumptions.
In internal tests, OpenAI found that responses containing at least one factual error were 68% less common with GPT-5.6 Sol than with GPT-5.5 Instant.
Moreover, GPT-5.6 Luna reduced such responses by 62% in the same evaluation.
Free users are getting unlimited GPT-5.6 Luna chats
GPT-5.6 Luna will become the default model for Free and Go users this week, and some users are already seeing the change. I spotted it in my OpenAI account with a Go subscription that costs approximately $10.
Starting next week, OpenAI also plans to remove the rate limit for text chats on those plans, although usage will remain subject to abuse protections. However, limits will still apply to file uploads, image generation, and other ChatGPT tools.
With a free account, you will still receive a new Think button that gives GPT-5.6 Luna additional time to reason through harder questions.
"For questions that require deeper reasoning, Free users can tap the new Think button to give GPT-5.6 Luna more time to work through the answer," OpenAI noted.
The update does not affect GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex or Work
The revised version of GPT-5.6 Sol is designed for everyday conversations and will only be available through ChatGPT's regular Chat experience.
OpenAI is also introducing additional protections for users believed to be under 18.
These include stricter boundaries around romantic roleplay, sexual content, dangerous activities, eating disorders, body-image risks, age-restricted goods, and graphic violence.
Today's changes are rolling out gradually.

articles.title: 3.8 Million Impacted by Unlimited Technology Systems Data Breach
articles.text:
Unlimited Technology Systems is notifying over 3.8 million individuals that their personal information was stolen in a data breach.
Based in Montgomery, Ohio, Unlimited provides advanced financial and revenue cycle technology to healthcare providers and organizations. It claims to be working with more than 4,500 oncology offices and over 6,500 specialty providers.
The incident, it says, was discovered in October 2025 and involved one of its commercial data centers. The company’s investigation determined that hackers stole certain data from its systems between October 5 and October 10, 2025.
The stolen data, Unlimited notes in a notification letter to the affected individuals, a copy of which was submitted (PDF) to the Iowa Attorney General’s Office, includes personal, medical, and health insurance information.
The hackers stole names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, Social Security numbers, medical record numbers, diagnoses, dates of service, insurance policy numbers, claims/benefits information, and scanned documents (such as driver’s licenses and government IDs).
“The data involved in the incident does not include full patient medical records, medical imaging, or financial information, such as credit card or bank account information,” Unlimited said.
The company also notes that it is not aware of any attempted or actual misuse of the information compromised in the data breach.
In late July, the company notified the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that 3,803,750 people were affected. The HHS added Unlimited to its breach portal on August 6.
The company is providing the affected people with two years of free credit monitoring, fraud consultation, and identity theft restoration services.
Unlimited has not named the threat actor responsible for the attack, and SecurityWeek has not seen any known extortion or ransomware groups claiming it.

articles.title: Surfshark crée un « double numérique » pour votre boîte mail pour mieux protéger ses données — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est un fait, les violations de données personnelles sont en hausse. Et c’est la CNIL qui pose le constat dans son rapport annuel. Un chiffre en augmentation de presque 10 % par rapport à l’année précédente. En 2025, ce sont en effet pas moins de 6 167 cas qui ont été signalés aux gendarmes d’internet.
Une augmentation qui s’explique en partie par la digitalisation croissante de nos vies. Faire ses courses, lire le journal, réserver ses vacances… tout ou presque passe par le web en 2026. Si elle devient donc inévitable, la dilapidation de vos données personnelles peut être endiguée par une hygiène de vie numérique et un petit coup de pouce de la part d’entreprises spécialisées dans le domaine comme Surfshark.
Non contente de proposer ses services via son VPN, l’entreprise offre dorénavant l’accès à un système anti-arnaques poussé, le tout à partir de 3,35 euros TTC par mois.
Surfshark Alternative ID : le bouclier de votre boîte mail
Pour éviter que votre adresse personnelle ne finisse dans les bases de données piratées, Surfshark a intégré Alternative ID. Le principe : générer un profil numérique fictif crédible (avec nom et prénom) associé à des adresses e-mail alternatives.
Vous souhaitez obtenir un code promo de -10 % sur une boutique peu connue ou tester un nouveau service en ligne ? Plutôt que de livrer votre véritable e-mail et risquer le spam, vous fournissez l’alias généré par Surfshark. Les courriels envoyés sur cette adresse jetable sont automatiquement transférés vers votre vraie boîte de réception. Le site expéditeur, lui, ne connaît jamais votre véritable identité.
Et si ce même site se fait pirater ou revend ses fichiers clients et que votre alias commence à être inondé de publicités ou de tentatives de phishing, il suffit d’un clic dans l’application ou l’extension Surfshark pour le supprimer ou le mettre en pause. Le flux de messages indésirables est coupé à la source, gardant votre messagerie personnelle parfaitement propre.
CleanWeb et Alert : la protection proactive
Alternative ID permet donc de sécuriser vos futures communications de données, mais quid de celles qui circulaient avant de souscrire aux services de Surfshark ? Ça, c’est le travail de la fonctionnalité Alert.
Grâce à cette fonctionnalité, Surfshark surveille le web et le dark web en permanence. Si votre adresse e-mail, vos mots de passe ou vos numéros de carte bancaire apparaissent dans une nouvelle fuite de données, vous recevez une notification immédiate pour réagir avant qu’il ne soit trop tard.
CleanWeb agit également comme un filtre de navigation. Au-delà de bloquer les publicités intrusives et les traqueurs, cet outil empêche l’accès aux sites frauduleux déjà référencés comme tels. Un filet de sécurité bien utile si vous cliquez un peu trop vite sur un faux lien de suivi de colis reçu par SMS.
Enfin, l’ensemble de ces outils s’appuie sur le socle historique de Surfshark : un VPN qui chiffre votre trafic et masque votre adresse IP pour sécuriser vos connexions, notamment sur les réseaux Wi-Fi publics.
Surfshark One : un VPN premium par défaut
Car c’est ça la vraie force des offres Surfshark : assurer, de base, une sécurité maximale sans se perdre dans une myriade d’offres.
Avec une seule formule, le VPN intègre tous les standards de l’industrie pour chiffrer vos données. Ce bouclier cryptographique neutralise d’office les attaques dites de « l’homme du milieu » (Man in the Middle), qui visent à intercepter vos saisies (mots de passe, données bancaires) lorsque vous vous connectez à des réseaux Wi-Fi publics mal sécurisés.
Vous bénéficiez aussi systématiquement d’un Kill Switch (qui coupe automatiquement l’accès à internet si la connexion au serveur saute) et de la fonction MultiHop, permettant de faire transiter votre trafic par deux pays distincts pour brouiller davantage les pistes.
Surtout, Surfshark applique une politique no-logs stricte et régulièrement auditée par des cabinets de sécurité indépendants. L’entreprise garantit ainsi qu’aucune de vos données de navigation n’est enregistrée sur ses serveurs. Le contrat est clair : une protection complète, sans options facturées en supplément ni exploitation de vos données personnelles.
En ce moment, Surfshark offre trois mois d’abonnement gratuits en plus, ce qui revient, si vous souscrivez à son offre Surfshark One à ne payer que 3,35 euros par mois TTC pendant les 24 premiers mois.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 : histoire, date de sortie, bande-annonce… Tout savoir sur la série Prime Video
articles.text:
Blade Runner 2099 : histoire, date de sortie, bande-annonce… Tout savoir sur la série Prime Video
Une nouvelle série basée sur l'univers de science-fiction créé par Philip K. Dick arrive bientôt sur la plateforme de streaming Prime Video. Histoire, date de sortie, casting, trailer… Voici tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur la série Blade Runner 2099.
Une décennie après la sortie de Blade Runner 2049, et 44 ans après celle du culte Blade Runner, l'univers dystopique peuplé de replicants et imaginé par Philip K. Dick va connaître une suite sous la forme d'une mini-série disponible sur le service de streaming Prime Video.
Un show sombre et prometteur qui verra Michelle Yeoh et Hunther Schafer lancées en pleine traque dans une ville de Los Angeles au bord de l'implosion. Date de sortie, histoire, casting, images… Voici tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur la future série Blade Runner 2099.
L'histoire de la série
Publié en 1968, le roman "Les Androïdes rêvent-ils de moutons électriques ?"de l'auteur Philip K. Dick est l'un des grands classiques de la littérature d'anticipation, racontant un futur où la Terre a été dévastée par une guerre nucléaire, et où vivent les rares humains qui ont choisi de ne pas émigrer sur Mars, ou qui n'en avaient pas les moyens.
Le livre est adapté pour la première fois au cinéma en 1982 avec le film Blade Runner réalisé par Ridley Scott, et avec Harrison Ford en tête d'affiche. Échec à sa sortie, le long-métrage a néanmoins gagné un statut culte au fil du temps.
En 2017, sa suite Blade Runner 2049 signée Denis Villeneuve a malheureusement elle aussi essuyé un échec commercial, avec seulement 259 millions de dollars de recettes mondiales pour un budget 150 millions de budget.
Cette nouvelle mini-série Blade Runner 2099 se déroule donc un demi-siècle après les événements du précédent film, et racontera une histoire inédite dont voici le synopsis officiel :
"Cinquante ans après les événements de Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles renaît, mais pas grâce à l'humanité. Cora, une fugitive qui tente une dernière fois de mettre fin à sa fuite, endosse une ultime identité : celle de Blade Runner. Contrainte de faire équipe avec Olwen, une Réplicante à l'article de la mort, elle traque un fugitif qui dissimule une vérité susceptible de faire s'effondrer leur fragile cité."
Qui est aux commandes de Blade Runner 2099 ?
Créée par Silka Luisa (Shining Girls, Halo), Blade Runner 2099 est produite par Ridley Scott, réalisateur du tout premier film, ainsi que par Andrew Kosove et Broderick Johnson, déjà présents sur Blade Runner 2049.
Parmi son équipe de scénaristes, la série peut compter sur la présence de Tom Spezialy (The Leftovers), Claire Kiechel (Watchmen) et Kirsa Rein (See).
Après de nombreux reports, dus en partie par la massive grève hollywoodienne et le remplacement de réalisateurs, la série a finalement pu se tourner de mai à décembre 2024 à Prague et à Barcelone.
Le réalisateur Jonathan van Tulleken (Shogun) signe les deux premiers épisodes, quand les autres sont notamment mis en scène par Ariel Kleiman, Marcela Said, et Karena Evans.
Quelle date de sortie pour Blade Runner 2099 ?
Blade Runner 2099 a été annoncée comme une mini-série, et n'aura donc qu'une seule et unique saison, composée de huit épisodes.

articles.title: Critical infrastructure security with OPSWAT - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OPSWAT targets file regeneration over detection for critical infrastructure security
Critical infrastructure security faces a novel threat of the sort that detection-based defenses were never designed to handle, and the critical personnel who run our power grids, water plants and financial systems can’t afford to learn this the hard way.
Benny Czarny (pictured), CEO and founder of cybersecurity company OPSWAT Inc., makes this argument clear in his USA Today bestselling book, Cybersecurity Upside Down. Czarny said AI has dramatically accelerated the speed and targeting precision of file-borne attacks, making the traditional detect-and-respond model all but obsolete. Response models are dangerously slow in an environment where 99% uptime is not good enough and taking systems offline for investigation or patching is often impossible.
“Whenever we look at critical infrastructure and how to protect it, the network is extremely complex, and you can’t really afford to have any downtime,” Czarny said. “Think about it. You run a nuclear facility, or you run defense, or you are running a very important financial service. 99% is not enough.”
Czarny spoke with Krista Case at Black Hat USA during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why prevention through file regeneration is more effective than detection for critical infrastructure security, how peripheral media remains a dangerously underestimated attack vector and what OPSWAT’s bootstrapped growth model has meant for its product focus and customer relationships. (* Disclosure below.)
Critical infrastructure security demands prevention through file regeneration
OPSWAT’s Deep Content Disarm and Reconstruction technology takes a radically disparate approach to critical infrastructure security. Instead of identifying malicious files, Deep CDR assumes all incoming files are potentially compromised, parses their structure and regenerates a clean version that’s mathematically free of embedded threats. The process is deterministic, meaning it doesn’t rely on signature databases or behavioral heuristics that AI-powered attacks can increasingly evade.
“You achieve prevention through file regeneration, not through detection,” Czarny said. “You assume that all of the file flow to your organization is malicious, and then you regenerate a new file that is malware-free.”
Peripheral media represents one of the most underestimated attack surfaces in OT environments. The threats go well beyond USB drives, including SD cards, phones, contractor laptops, external drives and even charging cables, Czarny noted. Device-based threats consist of hardware that masquerades as peripheral media while functioning as a network sniffer or a remote access tool. USB kill devices can deliver up to 240 volts of electrical power to a programmable logic controller, physically destroying equipment and shutting down a facility. Mapping and intercepting every data channel (file downloads, uploads, email attachments and peripheral media simultaneously) is the foundation of what Czarny refers to as a firewall of data.
“Think about intercepting all of your data flow from file downloads, file uploads, USBs, external peripheral media, email attachments,” Czarny said. “If you do that, you can eliminate so many threats and increase your cybersecurity posture and resilience significantly.”
For practitioners looking to start, Czarny recommended OPSWAT Academy as the most direct path to building the foundational skills necessary to implement a preventative architecture. The program has certified nearly 289,000 professionals to date.
“We make cybersecurity fun and exciting and visual to a point that anybody can understand,” Czarny said. “Episode one is about breaking the firewall — we’re mythbusting that the firewall is effective.”
